verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: weak as modelled. If an LLM writes every message, GPU cost is about 23 toman per message, and because a campaign customer sends tens of thousands of messages a month (90,000 on average at the plan mix below [D]), GPU cost eats most of the margin: gross margin is 65% on Starter but 31% on Growth and 7.5% on Scale. Revenue per customer is about 2.78M toman a month. The base case (80 customers at month 12, 300 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months: peak cash need is about 4,900M toman (about $18,500), month-24 profit is −169M toman a month and five GPU nodes are needed. Only the optimistic case (200 / 750) breaks even, in month 17, with +133M toman a month at month 24 and cumulative cash still −2,558M. All three stress cases stay loss-making. A design that fills templates per segment instead of calling the model per recipient would cost far less GPU time, but I did not model it. The carrier SMS fee is excluded because I could not verify any Iranian SMS price (see section 6), so the customer is assumed to buy SMS credit from its own panel. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Online shops with 10,000–500,000 customer phone numbers and an order history — core. (b) Mobile and web apps that send push or SMS notifications (food, ride, content, finance apps). (c) Agencies that run campaigns for several shops. Not targeted: shops with fewer than a few thousand contacts (a plain SMS panel is enough) and large groups that build in-house.

Imports the customer list and order history, builds segments (lapsed buyers, high spenders, abandoned carts), writes a Persian message variant per recipient or segment, picks the send time, sends through the customer's own SMS panel or push channel and reports orders won per campaign. Writing one variant by hand at 3 minutes [A] for a 50-person segment [A] costs about 143 toman of labour per message at the 1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance (143,023 toman an hour [D]); the plans below charge 15–40 toman per message, 10–28% of that [D]. The carrier fee for the SMS itself is separate and was not priced (section 6).

Web dashboard; API and plugins for Iranian shop platforms (connector terms not verified); Bale/Eitaa messages and web or app push as cheaper channels beside SMS; direct sales to e-commerce managers; agency partnerships; content on seller communities.

Assisted import and segment set-up in the first week, a monthly performance review for Growth and Scale accounts, self-serve for Starter. One customer-success person per 300 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by personalised messages: Starter 790,000 toman (20,000 messages), Growth 2,990,000 (150,000), Scale 11,900,000 (800,000) [A, anchored to the labour cost above, not to a competitor]. Mix 50% / 40% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 2,781,000 toman a month (about $10.48) [D]. Free trial of 2,000 messages [A]. The plan names a monthly fee; "per message" overage is not in the model.

Persian text model (8–9B open-weight class) fine-tuned on promotional copy; segmentation and send-time models on customer order history; domestic GPU nodes (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); a CPU server for sending queues and analytics; 2 engineers and 1 customer-success hire.
Persian copy quality within SMS length limits; consent and opt-out handling; segment and send-time modelling; connectors to shop platforms and SMS panels; measuring orders won per campaign.
SMS panel providers (the carrier route), domestic GPU/cloud host, payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]), shop-platform vendors and agencies.

Fixed: team 159.9M toman a month, GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 25M (includes the sending and analytics server [A]), accounting 8M, marketing 15M = 357.9M toman a month for one node (about $1,349) [D]; one-time setup 150M [A]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 300 customers, and an extra GPU node for every 72 customers [D], which dominates the cost at scale.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] 150 input (customer profile, offer, template) + 100 output (a Persian SMS-length text); text workload, so the #1 throughput proxy applies
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 60% use [A] of the 20,000 / 150,000 / 800,000 quotas, weighted by plan mix

not verified; one foreign blog lists operator-side prices of 100–200 rial on-network and 150–250 rial off-network [S, sent.dm, 3 May 2025], which looks like a wholesale operator rate rather than a retail panel price, so I did not use it

cost_model.x: With one node and no extra hire, break-even would be about 130 customers [D: 357.9M ÷ (2,781,000 × 0.99)], but 130 customers need two nodes. Counting the extra nodes and customer-success hires that each customer count requires, the stable break-even is about 416 customers with six nodes [D, by stepping through customer counts in code].

revenue.x: Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 150M setup falls in month 1; GPU nodes are added in whole units as load grows.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian shops or apps with a large enough phone list was found. Optimistic-case cumulative cash is still −2,558M toman at month 24 [D], so payback is beyond month 24, and the base case loses money each month at month 24.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 6% monthly churn [A, campaign tools are sticky once segments and history are loaded] lifetime revenue per customer is about 45.9M toman [D: 2,781,000 × 0.99 ÷ 0.06]. That figure is large only because it is revenue, not margin: at the Scale plan's 7.5% gross margin, lifetime gross profit is far smaller.

risks.x: Per-message generation: the model assumes one LLM call per message. Template-based personalisation would cut GPU time sharply, but it would also be easier for competitors and SMS panels to copy.

Telecom regulation: Iranian SMS falls under the Communications Regulatory Authority's rules on content, opt-out and data retention [S, sent.dm, 3 May 2025]; advertising SMS rules and sender-line types were not verified and could limit what the engine may send.
Customer data: phone lists and purchase history are personal data, so hosting must stay domestic; no Iranian data-protection requirement was verified.
Channel reach: web and app push depend on the browser and app-store environment inside Iran, and on whitelisting during internet restrictions.
Proof of uplift: customers will pay by results; no Iranian conversion figure for personalised SMS was found.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: Retail price per SMS in Iran by line type and package; the main SMS panel sites (Kavenegar, Ghasedak, sms.ir, Faraz SMS, Melipayamak and others) were blocked from automated reading.
Iranian push-notification platform prices (Najva, Pushe and others were blocked).
The number of Iranian shops and apps with phone lists large enough to use this.
Advertising SMS rules (sending hours, opt-out wording, line types) from the regulator.
Conversion uplift of personalised versus generic SMS in Iran.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 23 Oct 2026.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق گفتینو، رایچت و جایگزین‌های محلی Crisp به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۴٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۶۴٬۰۶۵٬۴۹۶ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable if the customer counts are reached, and the numbers are not fragile to cost. GPU cost is about 599 toman per conversation and gross margin is 74–81%. Revenue per customer is about 2.19M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 161 paying customers. The base case (120 at month 12, 450 at month 24) breaks even in month 14, with a peak cash need of about 2,675M toman (about $10,100) and +439M toman a month at month 24; cumulative cash is nearly back to zero (−184M) at month 24. The conservative case (40 / 150) does not break even within 24 months but is close (−23M a month at month 24). Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each delay break-even to months 16–20 and leave month-24 profit positive. The weak point is the customer count: 450 paying business customers in two years is a hypothesis with no sourced market size behind it. It also depends on an 8–9B open-weight model answering in Persian from retrieved passages without inventing facts, which I could not test. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. r: (a) Small and mid-size online shops and service firms with a website, product or service documents and 100+ customer questions a month — core. (b) Software and app companies with help-centre articles. (c) Agencies that install a chatbot on client sites. Not targeted: firms with fewer than about 50 questions a month, and large companies that build their own.

The customer uploads its FAQ, catalogue, policies or manuals; the service answers visitors in Persian with citations to the source passage and hands over to a human when unsure. One human-handled chat at 4 minutes [A] costs about 9,535 toman of labour at the 1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance (143,023 toman an hour [D]); the plans below charge 1,414–1,967 toman per conversation, 15–21% of that [D]. These are foreign prices and are not payable from Iran.

Assisted set-up in the first week (document upload, tone, hand-over rules), self-serve afterwards; weekly report of unanswered questions to improve the documents; one customer-success person per 300 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by conversations: Starter 590,000 toman (300 conversations), Growth 2,490,000 (1,500), Business 9,900,000 (7,000) [A, anchored to the labour cost above]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 2,186,000 toman a month (about $8.24) [D]. Free trial of 30 conversations [A].

An open-weight 8–9B chat model tuned for Persian answers with citations; a multilingual embedding model for retrieval (BGE-M3 is MIT-licensed with 8,192-token input and lists "more than 100 working languages" without naming Persian [S, Hugging Face model card, read 23 Oct 2026]); a vector store and document parser (PDF, Word, web pages); a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers and 1 customer-success hire.

title: ربات صوتی فارسی جایگزین منوهای مرکز تماس

engine: موتور ۳: تشخیص گفتار، صدا و TTS فارسی

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: بانک‌ها، بیمه‌ها و خرده‌فروشی‌های بزرگ (سازمانی، صنعتی و نهادی B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: کارکنان شیفت مرکز تماس (۲۵ تا ۳۵ میلیون تومان به‌ازای هر اپراتور در ماه). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۳۳ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۹ پایه، ۱۶ رشد، ۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۴٫۰٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «کارکنان شیفت مرکز تماس (۲۵ تا ۳۵ میلیون تومان به‌ازای هر اپراتور در ماه)» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: تشخیص گفتار و تبدیل متن به گفتار فارسی کم‌تأخیر با مسیریاب نیت؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق ترانک‌های SIP داخلی ایزابل، آستریکس و سیموتل به‌همراه ۰٫۹۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۵٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۵۵٬۵۲۷٬۰۷۸ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۰٫۹۶ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (پروژه + مصرف): پایه ۷٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۱۵٬۹۰۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۲۶٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۲٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۰۹٬۱۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۶٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۶۹٬۵۰۸٬۵۰۰ تومان/ماه.

The caller speaks instead of pressing menu digits; the bot understands Persian requests (balance, order status, branch hours, policy status), answers from the customer's systems, and transfers to an agent with a transcript when it cannot. cost_model.x: One node covers only about 3.7 customers at this usage [D: 184,569 ÷ (49,875 + 500 pilot minutes)], so GPU nodes scale with customers and break-even is not a single customer count. Break-even with one node would be about 7 customers [D: 461.7M ÷ (67.9M × 0.99)], but stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives about 17 customers with five nodes [D].

revenue.x: Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 400M setup falls in month 1; GPU nodes are added in whole units as load grows. Enterprise sales cycles are long, so a first paying customer in month 4 is optimistic [A].

Customer counts are [A]; I found no sourced count of Iranian banks, insurers and large retailers that run call centers of this size. The optimistic case needs 60 enterprise accounts in two years. Base-case cumulative cash is −3,579M toman at month 24 [D], so payback is well beyond month 24; the optimistic case is at +3,663M [D].

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 2% monthly churn [A, enterprise contracts with integration work are hard to switch] lifetime revenue per customer is about 3.36 billion toman [D: 67.9M × 0.99 ÷ 0.02]; sales and integration cost per account was not modelled and is large.

risks.x: Voice licence: the open Persian voices I found are non-commercial [S]; a licensed or self-trained voice could cost more than the 40M a month and 400M setup assumed.

Telephone-quality recognition: the leaderboard figures are not for 8 kHz phone audio, and the customer-service set shows whisper-large-v3 at 75.72 WER against 21.97 for the fine-tune [S]; real accuracy on accents, numbers and names must be measured.
Price ceiling: the buyer compares the price with a human agent-minute, and GPU cost per minute (813 toman) is already about a third of the minimum-wage agent-minute [D].
Latency and concurrency: calls arrive in bursts, so 30% average utilisation may be too high; a lower figure would raise node count.
Regulation and data: call recordings are personal and financial data; banks and insurers may require on-premises or domestic hosting and regulator approval, which I did not verify.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: Fully loaded cost of a call-center agent-minute in Iran, and the number of calls per month at Iranian banks, insurers and retailers.
Prices and capabilities of domestic competitors (Amerandish and others; pages were blocked or not opened).
Speed of any Persian text-to-speech or streaming speech-recognition model on the actual GPU, and the cost of a commercial voice licence or custom voice training.
Whether state and private banks may use externally hosted voice AI; regulator rules.
Telephony and SIP-trunk fees (assumed to stay with the customer).
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 23 Oct 2026.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with weak evidence on demand and accuracy. GPU cost is about 17,800 toman per audio hour (batch speech-to-text, speaker separation and a scoring pass, 154 GPU-seconds an hour [D]) and gross margin is 58–71%. Revenue per customer is about 45.4M toman a month, so the 352.9M toman fixed cost is covered by about 8 customers. The base case (20 customers at month 12, 70 at month 24) breaks even in month 7, with a peak cash need of about 1,328M toman (about $5,000) and +1,631M toman a month at month 24. Even the conservative case (8 / 25) breaks even in month 12, and doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each still break even by month 15. The weak points are the customer counts (no sourced count of Iranian call centers that record and would pay), and Persian accuracy on phone audio: the best open Persian model I found scores 21.97 word error rate on a customer-service set, and quality scores built on transcripts that wrong are noisy. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Call centers of banks, insurers, telecom resellers, delivery and retail firms that already record calls — core. (b) Sales teams that record calls and want coaching. (c) Outsourced call-center operators who must report quality to clients. Not targeted: firms that do not record calls, and very small teams where a manager can listen to every call.

Every recorded call is transcribed in Persian, split by speaker, scored against the customer's checklist (greeting, empathy, correct information, closing, forbidden phrases) and flagged for review; managers see agent and topic dashboards. A human analyst listening in real time and scoring takes about 75 minutes per audio hour [A], which costs about 178,779 toman at the 1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance (143,023 toman an hour [D]); manual teams usually sample a few percent of calls [A], while this scores all of them. The plans below charge 30,000–45,000 toman per audio hour, 17–25% of the manual figure [D]. Foreign reference: AssemblyAI lists pre-recorded speech-to-text at $0.15 to $0.21 an hour, plus $0.02 an hour each for speaker labels, summarization and sentiment [S, assemblyai.com/pricing, read 23 Oct 2026], about 55,700 toman an hour at the top rate [D]; its page does not confirm Persian support, and a foreign provider is not payable from Iran.

Web dashboard and upload API; connectors for common Iranian PBX and call-recording systems (not verified); direct sales to heads of customer service and quality; contact-center software vendors and outsourcers as resellers.

Paid two-week pilot on the customer's own recordings (20 free audio hours [A]); checklist set-up with the quality team; monthly review; one customer-success person per 20 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by audio hours: Starter 13.5M toman (300 hours), Growth 57M (1,500), Pro 180M (6,000) [A, set below the foreign reference and the manual labour cost]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 45.4M toman a month (about $171) [D].

Persian speech recognition (an open Persian Whisper fine-tune scores 11.08–21.97 WER on four Persian sets against 36.15–75.72 for whisper-large-v3; on the customer-service set the figures are 21.97 against 75.72 [S, open Persian ASR leaderboard, 23 Oct 2026]); speaker separation; an 8–9B language model for scoring and summaries; domestic GPU nodes (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers and 1 customer-success hire.

Telephone-audio accuracy on Persian (numbers, names, accents, overlapping speech); turning each customer's checklist into scoring prompts; calibrating scores against human reviewers; dashboards; secure handling of recordings.
Domestic GPU/cloud host; PBX and call-recording vendors; contact-center software vendors; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 159.9M toman a month, GPU node 150M, other infrastructure and storage 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 20M = 352.9M toman a month for one node (about $1,330) [D]; one-time setup 200M [A]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 20 customers, an extra GPU node for every 9 customers [D].

cost_model.x: One node covers about 9 customers at this usage [D: 8,433 ÷ (903 + 20 trial hours)]. Break-even is about 8 customers [D: 352.9M ÷ (45.375M × 0.99)], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives the same figure with one node [D].

revenue.x: Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 200M setup falls in month 1; GPU nodes are added in whole units as load grows.

Customer counts are [A]; I found no sourced count of Iranian call centers that record calls and might pay for scoring. Base-case cumulative cash is +11,407M toman at month 24 [D], and the conservative case is at +96M [D]. These results rest on the first paying customers arriving in month 4 and on a long sales cycle not delaying them, which I could not test.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 3% monthly churn [A, quality dashboards become part of the weekly routine] lifetime revenue per customer is about 1.50 billion toman [D: 45.375M × 0.99 ÷ 0.03]. Sales and pilot cost per account was not modelled; a paid pilot with 20 free hours is cheap in GPU terms (about 356,000 toman [D: 20 × 17,788]) but not in staff time.

risks.x: Transcript accuracy: on the customer-service set the open Persian fine-tune scores 21.97 WER and whisper-large-v3 scores 75.72 [S]; scoring against a checklist from transcripts that inaccurate may mislabel calls, so customers may demand human review of flagged calls, which adds cost.
Speed: the real-time factor of 30 is an assumption; at 15 the GPU cost per hour roughly doubles, close to the "GPU price doubles" row.

Recording consent and data: call recordings are personal data and may contain card or account details; hosting must stay domestic and some customers may refuse any external processing. No Iranian rule was verified.
Bundled alternatives: contact-center software vendors may add scoring as a feature; I did not find their prices.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian call centers that record calls, and how many hours they record.
Iranian competitors and their per-hour prices (the sources found were blocked or foreign).
Whether AssemblyAI or other foreign engines support Persian well (its price page does not say).
Real speech-to-text speed and accuracy on 8 kHz Persian phone calls on the actual node; the scoring prompt length.
Legal rules on recording and processing customer calls in Iran.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «زمان مهندس پشتیبانی سطح یک (۲۶ میلیون تومان در ماه)» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: مجموعه داده عیب‌یابی فارسی ISP، میزبانی و SaaS؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق WHMCS، Jira داخلی و پورتال‌های تیکت محلی به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۴٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۵۲٬۲۴۲٬۰۷۱ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۱۲ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر کاربر): پایه ۱٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۰۹۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۵٬۶۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۰۱٬۱۴۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۷۴٬۰۸۸٬۷۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۴۰ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۶۰٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۰٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen3-14B/32B کوانتیزه (AWQ، مجوز Apache 2.0) با vLLM + امبدینگ فارسی BGE-M3 + پایگاه برداری Qdrant روی CPU. مجموعه داده: مجموعه داده عیب‌یابی فارسی ISP، میزبانی و SaaS.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی مجموعه داده عیب‌یابی فارسی ISP، میزبانی و SaaS؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های WHMCS، Jira داخلی و پورتال‌های تیکت محلی در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: WHMCS، Jira داخلی و پورتال‌های تیکت محلی. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

bmc.title: ساختار هزینه (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: هزینه کامل مستقل: ۴۱۰٬۱۰۹٬۳۵۲ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA مستقل: ۱۹۱٬۰۳۰٬۶۴۸ تومان/ماه (۳۱٫۸٪). هزینه سبد موتور مشترک (تقسیم توسعه/دفتر بین ۳ ابزار هم‌خانواده): ۳۳۲٬۷۶۹٬۳۵۲ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA سبد: ۲۶۸٬۳۷۰٬۶۴۸ تومان/ماه (۴۴٫۶٪).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with demand unverified. GPU cost is only about 86 toman per ticket and gross margin is 96–97%, so the business is carried by fixed cost, not model cost. Revenue per customer is about 22.0M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 16 paying customers. The base case (20 customers at month 12, 80 at month 24) breaks even in month 11, with a peak cash need of about 1,892M toman (about $7,100) and +1,323M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case (8 / 30) breaks even in month 17, and doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each still break even by month 15. The weak points are the market and the quality of Persian drafts: I found no sourced count of Iranian software firms, ISPs and online businesses with a ticketing helpdesk of 5 or more agents, and 80 such customers in two years is a hypothesis. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Software and SaaS firms, internet providers and hosting companies with a support team of 5–80 agents — core. (b) Online shops and marketplaces with a ticket queue. (c) Banks' and insurers' digital-channel support teams. Not targeted: firms whose support runs only through chat on social apps (served by services #1 and #11) and firms with fewer than 5 agents.

Reads each incoming ticket, labels category, urgency and sentiment, routes it to the right team, finds the relevant knowledge-base passages and drafts a Persian reply for the agent to edit and send. Handling one ticket by hand (read, classify, search, write) at 6 minutes [A] costs about 14,302 toman of labour at the 1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance (143,023 toman an hour [D]); the plans below charge 1,833–2,500 toman per ticket, 13–18% of that [D]. Foreign reference: Freshdesk lists $19, $55 and $89 per agent a month (billed annually) and a Freddy AI Copilot add-on at $29 per agent a month, with AI agent sessions beyond the first 500 at $49 per 100 [S, freshworks.com/freshdesk/pricing, read 23 Oct 2026]; the Copilot add-on is about 7.69M toman a month at 265,295 [D], and a foreign vendor is not payable from Iran.
Plug-ins and API for the helpdesks Iranian firms use (which tools they use was not verified); email and web-form intake; direct sales to heads of support; IT-service and hosting communities.

Two-week trial on the customer's own past tickets (100 free tickets [A]); a monthly review of wrong labels and rejected drafts; one customer-success person per 30 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by seat bundle, with 600 tickets per seat a month [A]: Team 7.5M toman (5 seats, 3,000 tickets, 1.5M per seat), Business 26M (20 seats, 12,000 tickets, 1.3M per seat), Enterprise 88M (80 seats, 48,000 tickets, 1.1M per seat) [A, priced at 13–18% of the labour cost and well below the foreign add-on]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 22.0M toman a month (about $83) [D].

An 8–9B Persian-capable model for labels and drafts; retrieval over each customer's knowledge base; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); helpdesk connectors; 2 engineers and 1 customer-success hire.
Persian label and draft quality, including mixed Persian and English technical terms; learning each customer's tone and macros; connector upkeep; measuring edit rate of drafts.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; helpdesk software vendors (as integration partners); hosting and IT-service communities; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 159.9M toman a month, GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 20M = 347.9M toman a month (about $1,311) [D]; one-time setup 150M [A]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 30 customers, an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity (not reached in any scenario).
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] 700 input (ticket thread and knowledge-base passages) + 250 output (labels and a Persian draft); text workload, so the #1 throughput proxy applies
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 60% use [A] of the 3,000 / 12,000 / 48,000 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 268 customers at this usage [D: 1,740,888 ÷ (6,390 + 100 trial tickets)], so the GPU is not a binding cost; a shared or smaller GPU would raise profit and was not modelled.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 16 paying customers [D: 347.9M ÷ (22.025M × 0.99)], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives the same figure [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 150M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian firms with a helpdesk of this size was found (the figures I found for the number of Iranian internet providers were from 2009–2016 and conflict, so I did not use them). Base-case cumulative cash is +7,207M toman at month 24 [D], and the conservative case is still −2,073M [D].

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 3% monthly churn [A, a helpdesk tool becomes embedded in a team's daily work] lifetime revenue per customer is about 727M toman [D: 22.025M × 0.99 ÷ 0.03]. Sales cost per account was not modelled; measure it in the trial.

risks.x: Draft quality: if agents rewrite most drafts, the time saved falls and customers will not pay for seats; the 6 minutes per ticket and the saving are assumptions.
Small market: firms with a 5+ agent helpdesk are a limited group, and many support through chat apps; the customer counts may be too high.
Bundled alternatives: helpdesk vendors may add their own AI drafting; I did not find Iranian helpdesk prices.
Customer data: tickets contain customer personal data, so hosting must stay domestic; no Iranian data-protection rule was verified.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian firms with a ticketing helpdesk of 5 or more agents, and which helpdesk tools they use.
Iranian helpdesk and support-AI competitors and their prices.
Persian draft quality and edit rate; real tokens per ticket and throughput on the actual node.
Whether Freshdesk's annual prices apply monthly (the page does not show monthly prices).
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 23 Oct 2026.

bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۸۸ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۱۳۲٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۶٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Whisper-large-v3-turbo (فارسی محاوره‌ای) تنظیم‌شده + تفکیک گویندگان Pyannote + صدای فارسی Piper/XTTS. مجموعه داده: تفکیک گویندگان و مدل LoRA خلاصه‌سازی رسمی فارسی.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی تفکیک گویندگان و مدل LoRA خلاصه‌سازی رسمی فارسی؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های اسکای‌روم، قرار، گوگل‌میت و یادداشت‌های صوتی بله در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: اسکای‌روم، قرار، گوگل‌میت و یادداشت‌های صوتی بله. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

bmc.title: ساختار هزینه (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: هزینه کامل مستقل: ۵۳۵٬۴۱۷٬۴۱۳ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA مستقل: ۱۳۶٬۰۹۲٬۵۸۷ تومان/ماه (۲۰٫۳٪). هزینه سبد موتور مشترک (تقسیم توسعه/دفتر بین ۳ ابزار هم‌خانواده): ۴۳۵٬۷۵۷٬۴۱۳ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA سبد: ۲۳۵٬۷۵۲٬۵۸۷ تومان/ماه (۳۵٫۱٪).

driver: تفکیک گویندگان و مدل LoRA خلاصه‌سازی رسمی فارسی

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable in the base case, but the margin depends on speech-recognition cost, which I could not measure. GPU cost is about 17,800 toman per meeting hour (144 of 154 GPU-seconds are speech recognition and speaker separation [D], on a throughput assumption [A]) and gross margin is 52–61%, so unlike a text-only service one GPU node serves only about 26 customers [D]. Revenue per customer is about 13.5M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 27 customers on paper and 42 once the second GPU node is counted [D]. The base case (30 customers at month 12, 120 at month 24) breaks even in month 14, with a peak cash need of about 2,373M toman (about $8,900) and +468M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case (10 / 40) does not break even within 24 months (about −14M a month at month 24), and doubling the GPU price also prevents break-even; halving customers delays it to month 19. The weak points are Persian accuracy on multi-speaker room audio (the best open Persian model I found scores 11–22 word error rate on four test sets, none of them meetings, and the widely used whisper-large-v3 scores 36–76 on the same sets [S]), the 30x throughput assumption, and the customer counts, which have no sourced market size behind them. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Companies and institutes of 10–150 staff that hold regular management, project or board meetings and write minutes by hand — core. (b) Universities, research institutes and municipal offices with committee meetings. (c) Consultancies and law or accounting firms that bill client calls. Not targeted: individuals, and large firms whose meeting content must stay on their own premises (served by service #99). Size of the pool: the DiscoLike index lists 432,280 Iranian company websites as of October 2026 with no size breakdown [S, discolike.com/company-stats/countries/iran, read 23 Oct 2026], and Tehran Times reports 7,882 knowledge-based companies in the Iranian year March 2022–March 2023 [S, tehrantimes.com/news/480196, read 23 Oct 2026]; neither says how many hold meetings worth recording.

Takes a recording of a meeting (uploaded file, browser or phone recorder), transcribes it in Persian with speaker labels, and returns minutes with decisions, owners and deadlines that the secretary edits and circulates. Writing minutes for a one-hour meeting takes about 90 minutes [A], which costs about 214,535 toman of labour at the 1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance (143,023 toman an hour [D]); the plans below charge 24,000–30,000 toman per meeting hour, 11–14% of that [D]. Foreign reference: Fireflies lists Pro at $10 and Business at $19 per user a month (annual billing) with no Persian named, only '100+ languages' [S, fireflies.ai/pricing, read 23 Oct 2026]; Otter lists Pro at $8.49 and Business at $24 per user a month and names English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Chinese only [S, otter.ai/pricing, read 23 Oct 2026]; HappyScribe markets a Persian meeting notetaker with a vendor-stated 'over 95% accuracy' and shows no price on that page [S, happyscribe.com/ai-meeting-notetaker/persian, read 23 Oct 2026]. Fireflies Pro is about 2.65M toman per user a month at 265,295 [D], and our per-user price (360,000–450,000 toman) is 14–17% of it [D]; a foreign vendor is also not payable from Iran.

Direct sales to office managers and heads of administration; webinars with industry associations; integration with the video-meeting tools Iranian organisations use (not verified which); referral from accounting and consulting firms. Joining Zoom or Google Meet as a bot was not assumed possible from Iran.

Two-week trial with 10 free meeting hours [A]; a sample of minutes checked together with the customer's secretary; one customer-success person per 30 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by user bundle, with 15 meeting hours per user a month [A]: Team 4.5M toman (10 users, 150 hours, 450,000 per user), Company 16M (40 users, 600 hours, 400,000 per user), Institute 54M (150 users, 2,250 hours, 360,000 per user) [A, priced at 11–14% of the labour cost of minute-taking and well below the foreign per-user price]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 13.5M toman a month (about $51) [D].

A Persian speech-recognition model with speaker separation (best open Persian model found: gooya-v1.4, 21.97 word error rate on a customer-service set [S, navidved open Persian ASR leaderboard, 23 Oct 2026]); an 8–9B Persian-capable model for minutes and action items; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers and 1 customer-success hire.

Persian recognition quality on room audio with overlapping speakers and mixed Persian and English terms; speaker labelling; a minutes template that matches Iranian office practice (agenda, resolutions, owners, deadlines); editing interface; audio retention and deletion policy.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; domestic object storage (Arvan lists €0.020 per GB for extra storage on its plans, with no date and no period on the page [S, arvancloud.ir/en/pricing/cloud-storage, read 23 Oct 2026]); industry associations; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 159.9M toman a month, GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 20M = 347.9M toman a month (about $1,311) [D]; one-time setup 150M [A]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 30 customers, an extra GPU node per about 8,400 meeting hours of monthly load (reached at 27 customers, 2 nodes at month 24 in the conservative case and 5 in the base case [D]), audio storage and traffic of 1,000 toman per meeting hour [A].
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026

[D] speech recognition 3,600 ÷ 30 × 1.2 = 144 s (30x real time [A]; 46x measured for faster-whisper large-v2 batch on an RTX 3070 Ti [S, pypi.org/project/faster-whisper, 23 Oct 2026], derated for Persian and room audio; +20% for speaker separation [A]) + minutes model 21,500 tokens ÷ (2,658.57 × 0.8) = 10.1 s [D] (20,000 transcript tokens in + 1,500 out [A]; 2,658.57 tokens a second is the A6000 vLLM benchmark used in #1 [S], × 0.8 [A])
[D] 2,592,000 s × 50% utilisation [A, a batch queue can be packed] ÷ 154.1
[A] audio of about 29 MB an hour kept six months; Arvan lists €0.020 per GB [S], which is about 170 toman per month at an assumed 300,000 toman per euro [A]
[D] 60% use [A] of the 150 / 600 / 2,250 hour quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 26 customers at this usage [D: 8,410 ÷ (310.5 + 10 trial hours)], so the GPU is a stepped cost here, unlike text-only services; a smaller or shared GPU, a faster recognition model or CPU-based recognition could change this and was not modelled.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 27 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 347.9M ÷ (13.475M × 0.99 − 310.5 hours × 1,000 toman) = 26.7], but stepping through customer counts with the nodes, hires and storage cost each needs gives 42 customers with 2 nodes [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 150M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian organisations that hold regular meetings and would pay for minutes was found. The base case reaches 120 customers, 0.03% of the 432,280-company DiscoLike index and 1.5% of the 7,882 knowledge-based companies of 2022–23 [D, both sources in the canvas]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −4,448M toman in the conservative case, +165M in the base case and +10,621M in the optimistic case [D].

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 4% monthly churn [A, a meeting tool becomes an office habit but small teams cancel when budgets tighten] lifetime contribution per customer is about 326M toman [D: (13.475M × 0.99 − 310.5 × 1,000) ÷ 0.04]. Because speech recognition is 93% of GPU time [D: 144 ÷ 154.1], the 30x throughput assumption matters more than any other cost input; measure it on the real node first.

risks.x: Recognition quality: the best open Persian model found scores 11–22 word error rate on four test sets that are not meetings, and none of them has overlapping speakers; if minutes need heavy correction, the 90-minute saving shrinks and customers will not pay.

Confidential content: board and management meetings contain commercial and personnel information, so customers may insist on on-premises processing; no Iranian data-protection or recording-consent rule was verified.
GPU cost: doubling the GPU price removes break-even in the base case, because load grows with every customer.

Bundled alternatives: video-meeting platforms or office suites may add Persian minutes themselves, and foreign tools used through workarounds are not priced for Iranian budgets; I did not find Iranian competitor prices.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian organisations that hold regular recorded meetings, and how many write formal minutes.
Iranian meeting-minutes competitors and their prices (HappyScribe shows no price on the page opened; Skyroom's meeting-volume claim appeared only as a search-result title, not opened).
Persian word error rate on real multi-speaker meeting audio, and real throughput of speech recognition with speaker separation on the actual node.
Iranian rules on recording meetings and on hosting confidential audio.
The period and date of Arvan's storage price and the euro rate in toman.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 23 Oct 2026.

title: پیش‌نویس نامه رسمی و مکاتبات اداری
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۵A: تولید محتوای فارسی و نگارش بازاریابی/آکادمیک

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: ادارات و پیمانکاران (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: کارشناس دفتری/اداری (۲۴ میلیون تومان در ماه). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۷۱ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۸۲ پایه، ۶۶ رشد، ۲۳ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۱۱٫۰٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «کارشناس دفتری/اداری (۲۴ میلیون تومان در ماه)» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: مجموعه داده آداب مکاتبات اداری ایرانی؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق قالب‌های اتوماسیون فراغستر، چارگون و بارید به‌همراه ۰٫۴۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۲٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۳۸٬۲۶۴٬۰۲۳ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۰۱ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر کاربر): پایه ۱٬۲۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۳۱۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۳۲۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۱۳٬۶۸۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۴۹۰٬۵۶۴٬۴۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۲۶ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۳۹٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۱۷٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen3-14B / DeepSeek-V3 Distill کوانتیزه با آداپتورهای LoRA لحن برند فارسی. مجموعه داده: مجموعه داده آداب مکاتبات اداری ایرانی.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی مجموعه داده آداب مکاتبات اداری ایرانی؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های قالب‌های اتوماسیون فراغستر، چارگون و بارید در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal. Model cost is negligible (about 118 toman per letter, gross margin 97–98% [D]), but each customer pays only about 9.35M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 38 paying organisations on paper and 42 once the customer-success hires are counted [D]. The base case (30 customers at month 12, 120 at month 24) breaks even in month 14, with a peak cash need of about 2,631M toman (about $9,900) and +615M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case (10 / 40) does not break even within 24 months (−15M a month at month 24; cumulative cash −4,925M). Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers delay break-even to months 17–20 and leave month-24 profit positive. The weak points are willingness to pay and the customer count: letters can also be drafted with general chat assistants, I found no Iranian price for a dedicated product, and a domestic letter-writing app already exists (found only as a search-result title, so its price is unknown). No sourced count of Iranian offices or contractors that would pay exists in this model. Quality of formal Persian register in an 8–9B open model is untested. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Administrative and secretarial staff of contractors, consultancies and mid-size companies who write several formal letters a day — core. (b) Private-sector offices that deal with ministries, municipalities, banks and insurers. (c) Associations and institutes. Not targeted: government bodies with their own office-automation systems, which would require procurement (see service #39 for archives), and individuals. Pool: Iran had 24,983,452 employed persons in Q4 2024 [S, tradingeconomics.com/iran/employed-persons citing the Statistical Centre of Iran, read 23 Oct 2026]; the public sector was 16.9% of employed persons aged 10 and over in 1391 (2012) [S, irandataportal.syr.edu/iran-at-a-glance, read 23 Oct 2026]. No count of office staff who write formal letters, or of contractors, was found.

The user states the purpose, recipient and key facts; the service drafts the letter in the correct formal Persian register, with salutation, reference line, subject line and closing formulas, and adjusts tone for a ministry, a bank or a client. It also rewrites received letters into a summary and a reply draft. Drafting a formal letter by hand takes about 25 minutes [A], which costs about 59,593 toman of labour at the 1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance (143,023 toman an hour [D]); the plans below charge 4,200–6,000 toman per letter, 7–10% of that [D]. Foreign reference: Jasper Pro lists $59 per user a month [S, costbench, last verified 1 Jul 2026], about 15.65M toman at 265,295 [D], and our per-user price (420,000–600,000 toman) is 2.7–3.8% of it [D]; a foreign vendor is not payable from Iran and is not built for Iranian letter conventions. A domestic app for writing letters and administrative texts exists on Cafe Bazaar [S, search-result title only; the page is blocked to fetch, so features and price are not verified].

Direct sales to office managers and company owners; Telegram and Instagram groups of contractors and administrative staff; Cafe Bazaar and web app listing; bundling with accounting or office-software vendors.

Free trial of 30 letters [A]; a library of the customer's own letter templates and letterhead; one customer-success person per 30 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by user bundle, with 100 letters per user a month [A]: Office 3M toman (5 users, 500 letters, 600,000 per user), Company 10M (20 users, 2,000 letters, 500,000 per user), Organisation 42M (100 users, 10,000 letters, 420,000 per user) [A, priced at 7–10% of the labour cost of drafting and far below the foreign per-user price]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 9.35M toman a month (about $35) [D].

An 8–9B Persian-capable model tuned on formal letter styles (the training corpus is a data need: public letter samples and customer templates, licence not verified); a template and letterhead engine; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers and 1 customer-success hire.

Register and formula quality (Persian honorifics, ministry and bank conventions); template management; export to Word and PDF with letterhead; a check that names, dates (Jalali), amounts and reference numbers in the draft match what the user typed.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; office-software and automation vendors for integration; contractor and business associations; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 159.9M toman a month, GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 20M = 347.9M toman a month (about $1,311) [D]; one-time setup 150M [A]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue and an extra customer-success hire per 30 customers; an extra GPU node is not reached in any scenario.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] 800 input (instructions, sender data, a reference letter) + 500 output (a Persian letter of about 300 words); text workload, so the #1 throughput proxy applies
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 60% use [A] of the 500 / 2,000 / 10,000 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 1,047 customers at this usage [D: 1,272,187 ÷ (1,185 + 30 trial letters)], so the GPU is not a binding cost; the economics are set by how many organisations pay.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 38 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 347.9M ÷ (9.35M × 0.99)], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives 42 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 150M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian offices, contractors or companies that would buy a dedicated letter tool was found, and the only workforce figure found (24,983,452 employed, Q4 2024 [S]) does not say how many write formal letters. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −4,925M toman in the conservative case, +983M in the base case and +14,643M in the optimistic case [D].

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 5% monthly churn [A, writing needs are steady but free general chat assistants are a close substitute] lifetime revenue per customer is about 185M toman [D: 9.35M × 0.99 ÷ 0.05]. Sales cost per account was not modelled; measure it in the trial.

risks.x: Free substitutes: staff can already draft letters with general chat assistants; if they do, a dedicated tool must win on correct register, templates and letterhead, and the prices above may be too high.
Register quality: formal Persian conventions differ by recipient; one wrong honorific or formula in a letter to a ministry or bank damages trust, and I could not test the model.
Small paying base: the service is a convenience, and only organisations that write many letters will pay per user; the customer counts may be too high.
Confidential content: letters name people, contracts and amounts, so hosting must stay domestic; no Iranian data-protection rule was verified.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian offices, contractors and companies that write formal letters daily and would pay.
The features and price of the existing domestic letter-writing app (page blocked to fetch), and of Iranian general chat-assistant resellers used as substitutes.
Formal-register quality of an 8–9B model in Persian, and the licence of any letter corpus used for tuning.
Real tokens per letter and throughput on the actual node.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 23 Oct 2026.

title: API تبدیل گفتار به متن فارسی
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۳: تشخیص گفتار، صدا و TTS فارسی

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: توسعه‌دهندگان (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: گویش‌پرداز یا APIهای خارجی مسدود و Whisper. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۵۸ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۵۳ پایه، ۷۷ رشد، ۲۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۷٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «گویش‌پرداز یا APIهای خارجی مسدود و Whisper» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: مدل آکوستیک فارسی تنظیم‌شده روی لهجه‌های منطقه‌ای با معیار PSRB؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق APIهای REST و WebSocket روی زیرساخت داخلی NIN به‌همراه ۰٫۶۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۵٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۵۴٬۵۹۳٬۲۵۵ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۱۸ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر دقیقه): پایه ۱٬۷۷۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۴۲۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۲۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۳۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۸۶٬۳۱۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۵۹٬۹۳۰٬۸۲۵ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۶۷ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۱۰۰٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۲٬۸۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Whisper-large-v3-turbo (فارسی محاوره‌ای) تنظیم‌شده + تفکیک گویندگان Pyannote + صدای فارسی Piper/XTTS. مجموعه داده: مدل آکوستیک فارسی تنظیم‌شده روی لهجه‌های منطقه‌ای با معیار PSRB.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی مدل آکوستیک فارسی تنظیم‌شده روی لهجه‌های منطقه‌ای با معیار PSRB؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های APIهای REST و WebSocket روی زیرساخت داخلی NIN در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with price competition and the model licence as the open questions. GPU cost is about 231 toman per audio minute (2 GPU-seconds a minute on a 30x throughput assumption [A]; about $0.052 an audio hour [D]) and gross margin is 84–87%. Revenue per customer is about 30.8M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 12 paying customers [D]. The base case (20 customers at month 12, 80 at month 24) breaks even in month 9, with a peak cash need of about 1,537M toman (about $5,800) and +1,716M toman a month at month 24. Even the conservative case (8 / 30) breaks even in month 14, and doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each still break even by month 13. The weak points are price and licence: foreign speech APIs list far lower prices than the plans below (Soniox $0.12 an audio hour, Google batch $0.003 a minute [S]) and are hard to pay for from Iran [A], developers can also self-host open Persian models, and I could not confirm that the best open Persian recognition model (gooya-v1.4, 11–22 word error rate on four sets [S]) may be used commercially. The customer counts have no sourced count of Iranian developers behind them. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Iranian software firms and start-ups building voice features, call-centre software, meeting and lecture tools — core. (b) Media, podcast and video platforms that need subtitles and search. (c) Research groups and agencies with archives of audio. Not targeted: end consumers, and enterprises that need on-premises installation (service #99). No count of Iranian developers or companies using speech APIs was found.

A REST and streaming API that returns Persian transcripts with word timestamps and speaker labels, billed in toman per audio minute and payable through Iranian gateways, with data kept on domestic servers. Transcribing by hand takes about 4 minutes per audio minute [A], about 9,535 toman of labour at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 950–1,200 toman per minute, 10–13% of that [D]. Foreign references: Google Speech-to-Text V2 lists $0.016 per minute up to 500,000 minutes a month and $0.003 per minute for dynamic batch [S, cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/pricing, read 23 Oct 2026]; Soniox lists $0.12 per hour (about $0.002 per minute) real-time with diarization included [S, vendor comparison page soniox.com/compare-stt/soniox-vs-assemblyai/persian, read 23 Oct 2026]; AssemblyAI lists $0.15–0.21 per hour pre-recorded, with Persian not mentioned [S, assemblyai.com/pricing, 23 Oct 2026]; Speechmatics lists Persian with a vendor-reported FLEURS word error rate of 17.44% against 33.14% for Whisper large-v3 and publishes no price [S, speechmatics.com/speech-to-text/persian, read 23 Oct 2026]. At 265,295 toman per USD, Google's standard rate is about 4,245 toman a minute, its batch rate 796 and Soniox 531 [D]; our plans are 1.2–1.5 times Google's batch rate and 1.8–2.3 times Soniox's [D]. No Iranian speech API price was found.
Developer documentation and free trial credit; listings on Iranian developer communities and GitHub; direct sales to media and call-centre software companies; reseller deals with cloud hosts.

Self-service sign-up with 100 free minutes [A]; a shared support channel; accuracy report on the customer's own sample audio; one customer-success person per 30 customers [A]. Monthly plans billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly prepaid bundles per account: Developer 3.6M toman (3,000 minutes, 1,200 per minute), Startup 28M (25,000 minutes, 1,120 per minute), Scale 190M (200,000 minutes, 950 per minute) [A, set between the foreign batch and standard rates above, long tail of small developers]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 30.8M toman a month (about $116) [D].

A Persian recognition model with word timestamps and speaker separation (best open model found: gooya-v1.4, 21.97 word error rate on a customer-service set, 11.08 on FLEURS [S, navidved open Persian ASR leaderboard, 23 Oct 2026]; its commercial licence was not confirmed); a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); a queueing and streaming layer; 2 engineers and 1 customer-success hire.

Persian accuracy on noisy and telephone audio, dialects and mixed Persian and English terms; punctuation and number normalisation; streaming latency; benchmarking against competitors on the customer's own audio; usage billing.
Domestic GPU/cloud host; Persian speech-data providers (licence terms unknown); developer communities; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 159.9M toman a month, GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 20M = 347.9M toman a month (about $1,311) [D]; one-time setup 150M [A]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 30 customers, an extra GPU node per about 648,000 audio minutes of monthly load (the second node is needed from the 36th customer; 1, 3 and 6 nodes at month 24 in the conservative, base and optimistic cases [D]).
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026

[D] 60 ÷ 30 (30x real time [A]; 46x measured for faster-whisper large-v2 batch on an RTX 3070 Ti [S, pypi.org/project/faster-whisper, 23 Oct 2026], derated for the Persian model, streaming and diarization; this is a non-text model, so the text-model throughput proxy is not used)
[D] 2,592,000 s × 50% utilisation [A, streaming traffic is bursty] ÷ 2
[D] 60% use [A] of the 3,000 / 25,000 / 200,000 minute bundles, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 35 customers at this usage [D: 648,000 ÷ (18,240 + 100 trial minutes)], so the GPU is a stepped cost that grows with usage; the Scale plan alone uses 120,000 minutes a month per customer at 60% use [D], about 18% of a node.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 12 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 347.9M ÷ (30.78M × 0.99) = 11.4], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives 12 customers on one node [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 150M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian companies that buy speech APIs was found. Cumulative cash at month 24 is +345M toman in the conservative case, +11,885M in the base case and +39,460M in the optimistic case [D]. The plan mix is the largest input: a mix with fewer large accounts lowers ARPU in proportion.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 3% monthly churn [A, API integrations are sticky but developers switch on price] lifetime revenue per customer is about 1,016M toman [D: 30.78M × 0.99 ÷ 0.03]. Sales cost per account was not modelled; measure it in the trial.

risks.x: Self-hosting: developers can run open Persian models themselves; if a team has a GPU, the API competes with its marginal cost, which is near zero.
Licence: I could not confirm commercial use of the best open Persian models or of their training data; if the licence forbids it, the service needs a model trained or licensed first.
Price pressure: foreign APIs list $0.002–0.003 a minute or less; any Iranian competitor or foreign vendor reachable through workarounds sets a ceiling on the 950–1,200 toman prices.

Accuracy: telephone and noisy audio are far worse than clean test sets (a customer-service set scores 21.97 for the best model and 75.72 for whisper-large-v3 [S]); developers will benchmark on their own audio.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian developers and companies that would buy a Persian speech API, and their monthly audio volume.
Iranian speech-API competitors and their prices (none found).
The commercial licence of gooya-v1.4 and of other open Persian models and datasets.
Real throughput of Persian recognition with streaming and diarization on the actual node.
Whether foreign speech vendors can be paid from Iran (assumed not).
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 23 Oct 2026.

title: تبدیل متن به گفتار فارسی با صدای اختصاصی برند
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۳: تشخیص گفتار، صدا و TTS فارسی

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: رسانه‌ها و مراکز تماس (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: ضبط استودیویی با صداپیشه (۳ تا ۸ میلیون تومان به‌ازای هر پروژه). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۴۶ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۵۴ پایه، ۷۷ رشد، ۱۵ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۷٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «ضبط استودیویی با صداپیشه (۳ تا ۸ میلیون تومان به‌ازای هر پروژه)» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: TTS فارسی با آهنگ طبیعی و مدیریت اضافه؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق سامانه‌های IVR، تولیدکنندگان یوتیوب/آپارات و اپ‌های کتاب صوتی به‌همراه ۰٫۶۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۵٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۴۷٬۹۶۱٬۳۱۷ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۱۶ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر کاراکتر): پایه ۱٬۷۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۵۳۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۳۸۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۱۵٬۰۹۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۴۹۱٬۹۱۰٬۹۵۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۶۲ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۹۳٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۲٬۸۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Whisper-large-v3-turbo (فارسی محاوره‌ای) تنظیم‌شده + تفکیک گویندگان Pyannote + صدای فارسی Piper/XTTS. مجموعه داده: TTS فارسی با آهنگ طبیعی و مدیریت اضافه.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی TTS فارسی با آهنگ طبیعی و مدیریت اضافه؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های سامانه‌های IVR، تولیدکنندگان یوتیوب/آپارات و اپ‌های کتاب صوتی در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: سامانه‌های IVR، تولیدکنندگان یوتیوب/آپارات و اپ‌های کتاب صوتی. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but blocked until a commercially usable Persian voice model exists. GPU cost is only about 257 toman per 1,000 characters (2.2 GPU-seconds on a 30x throughput assumption [A]) and gross margin is 95–96%, so the business is carried by fixed cost of 412.1M toman a month, which about 10 paying customers cover at 42.8M toman each [D]. The base case (20 customers at month 12, 80 at month 24) breaks even in month 8, with a peak cash need of about 1,733M toman (about $6,500) and +2,904M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case (8 / 30) breaks even in month 13, and doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each still break even by month 12. The weak points are the licence and the demand. The open Persian voice models I found are non-commercial (a Persian MMS voice is CC BY-NC 4.0, and a Persian XTTS voice is under the Coqui licence that restricts commercial use while its metadata says MIT [S]), so a sellable service needs a model trained on licensed voice data, which is not costed beyond the setup and royalty lines below. Custom voices also need documented consent from the speaker. There is no sourced count of Iranian buyers of synthetic speech. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Audiobook, podcast, e-learning and video producers who need narration in Persian — core. (b) Call-centre and IVR operators and app developers who need prompts and brand voices (services #12 and #17 sit next to this). (c) Radio, advertising and news sites that want article read-aloud. Not targeted: individual consumers, and users who want to clone a celebrity voice. No count of Iranian buyers of synthetic speech was found.

A Persian voice API and studio: natural-sounding stock voices, and a custom brand voice built from a consenting speaker's recordings, billed in toman per character through Iranian gateways. A finished minute of narration needs about 15 minutes of studio recording and editing [A]; for 1,000 characters (about 67 seconds of speech [A, 15 characters a second]) that is about 39,729 toman of labour at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), and real voice-artist fees are higher but I found none; the plans below charge 4,400–6,000 toman per 1,000 characters, 11–15% of that [D]. Foreign references: Google Cloud lists $4 per million characters for Standard and WaveNet voices, $16 for Neural2, $30 for Chirp 3 HD, $160 for Studio and $60 for instant custom voice [S, cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/pricing, read 23 Oct 2026], and ElevenLabs lists Pro at $99 a month for 600,000 credits and Business at $990 for 6M [S, elevenlabs.io/pricing, read 23 Oct 2026]; neither page was checked for Persian voice support. Our plans are $16.6–22.6 per million characters [D], 1.0–1.4 times Google's Neural2 and 0.55–0.75 times Chirp 3 HD [D].
Direct sales to audiobook, e-learning and podcast producers; API documentation for developers; listings with video and e-learning platforms; partnerships with call-centre software vendors (#12, #13).

Free trial of 100,000 characters [A]; demo of three stock voices; a project process for custom voices (recording brief, consent contract, listening test); one customer-success person per 30 customers [A]. Monthly plans billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly prepaid bundles per account: Basic 6M toman (1M characters, 6,000 per 1,000), Media 50M (10M characters, 5,000 per 1,000), Studio 220M (50M characters, 4,400 per 1,000), with one custom brand voice included in Media and Studio [A, priced between the foreign Neural2 and Chirp 3 HD rates above]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 42.8M toman a month (about $161) [D].

A Persian TTS model that may be used commercially (none confirmed: the Persian voices found are CC BY-NC 4.0 or Coqui-licensed [S, huggingface.co model pages, 23 Oct 2026]); licensed voice recordings from consenting talent; a text front end for Persian (diacritics are usually missing in text, and ezafe and homographs must be resolved); a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 audio and voice engineer and 1 customer-success hire.
Voice data collection and licensing; Persian pronunciation quality; custom-voice builds with listening tests; speaker consent and voice-misuse controls; API and studio uptime.
Voice talent and recording studios; domestic GPU/cloud host; call-centre and e-learning platforms; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 209.1M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M, 1 audio engineer at 40M and 1 customer-success at 30M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, infrastructure 10M plus voice-talent royalties and storage 15M [A], accounting 8M, marketing 20M = 412.1M toman a month (about $1,553) [D]; one-time setup 200M [A, studio sessions and listening tests for three stock voices]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 30 customers, an extra GPU node per about 583 million characters of monthly load (reached at the 106th customer; 1, 1 and 2 nodes at month 24 in the conservative, base and optimistic cases [D]).
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 audio engineer at 40M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[D] 1,000 ÷ 15 characters a second = 66.7 s of speech [A], ÷ 30x real time [A, small VITS or XTTS-class voice in batch; non-text model, so the text throughput proxy is not used]
[D] 60% use [A] of the 1,000 / 10,000 / 50,000 unit bundles, weighted by plan mix
[D] after GPU and 1% gateway; voice-talent royalties are in fixed cost
[D] team 209.1M + GPU 150M + infrastructure and voice royalties 25M + accounting 8M + marketing 20M

cost_model.x: One node covers about 105 customers at this usage [D: 583,200 ÷ (5,430 + 100 trial units)], so the GPU is not a binding cost; custom-voice training (a few GPU hours per voice [A]) was not modelled separately.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 10 paying customers [D: 412.1M ÷ (42.8M × 0.99) = 9.7], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives 10 customers on one node [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 200M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian audiobook, e-learning or IVR buyers of synthetic speech was found. Cumulative cash at month 24 is +2,104M toman in the conservative case, +20,661M in the base case and +64,567M in the optimistic case [D]. These results assume a licensed Persian voice model is available at the costs shown; if building one costs more than the 200M setup, every scenario's peak cash need rises by the difference.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 4% monthly churn [A, producers switch voices when a cheaper one sounds as good] lifetime revenue per customer is about 1,059M toman [D: 42.8M × 0.99 ÷ 0.04]. Sales cost per account was not modelled; measure it in the trial.

risks.x: Licence: the Persian voice models found are non-commercial or conflict on licence, so the model must be trained or licensed; this cost and its timing are the largest unmodelled item.

Voice misuse: cloning a person's voice without consent exposes the company to personality-right claims and misuse; each custom voice needs a signed consent and a controlled use policy; I verified no Iranian rule on this.
Quality: Persian text lacks diacritics, so mispronounced names and ezafe constructions are common in synthetic speech; producers may not accept the output for audiobooks.
Price pressure: foreign APIs list $4–16 per million characters; any foreign or domestic competitor reachable by buyers caps the 4,400–6,000 toman prices.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian buyers of narration and IVR voices, and what they pay voice artists and studios today.
Iranian text-to-speech competitors and their prices (none found), and whether Google, ElevenLabs or Azure offer Persian voices.
Any commercially licensed Persian TTS model or voice dataset, and its price.
Real synthesis throughput of a Persian voice model on the actual node, and the GPU time to build a custom voice.
Iranian rules on voice cloning and personality rights.
Azure's per-character prices (the page text did not include the amounts).
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 23 Oct 2026.
