verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: weak on these assumptions, and licence-dependent. Per-query cost is dominated by data, not the model: the model costs about 317 toman per query, but I assumed 6,000 toman of data purchase per query because no data price was found, giving a gross margin of 62–77% [D]. Revenue per customer is about 4.88M toman a month ($18.39) against 485.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 146 paying customers on paper and 190 with hires counted [D]. The base case (30 customers at month 12, 120 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months: it loses 196M toman a month at month 24 and its cumulative cash is −8,548M toman (about $32,200), a floor; the conservative case (10 / 40) loses 389M a month at month 24, and only the optimistic case (80 / 350) breaks even, in month 17, with a peak cash need of 5,162M toman, +388M a month at month 24 and −3,646M cumulative. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base loss. A 2023 law created two kinds of licensed credit-scoring company, one using government-held national data and one using non-government data, and a paper proposes capping their fees at operating cost plus 30% [S]; this service would need the second kind of licence, and I could not confirm the requirements, the cost or whether a start-up can get one. I first priced at 10,000–20,000 toman per query with a 20,000 toman data cost, which gave negative margins on the two larger plans [D]; the data price is therefore the main uncertainty. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Wholesalers and manufacturers that sell to retailers on credit or against post-dated cheques and want a risk view of each new buyer — core. (b) Small lenders and leasing or factoring firms that finance SME invoices. (c) Marketplaces that offer buy-now-pay-later to shops. Pool: the number of Iranian suppliers who extend trade credit was not found. A 2023 law on financing production and infrastructure defines two types of credit-scoring company, Type I using government-held national data and Type II combining non-government sources such as fintech platforms, telecom operators and financial institutions [S, jte.ut.ac.ir/article\_106743\_en.html, abstract read 24 Oct 2026].

An SME risk report for a buyer in minutes: a score with reasons (payment behaviour the supplier and the network know, cheque record where legally available, company age and registration, sector and size signals), a suggested credit limit and payment terms, and monitoring alerts. A credit analyst assessing one buyer by hand takes about 45 minutes [A], about 107,267 toman of labour at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 12,000–20,000 toman per query, 11–19% of that [D]. The language model only writes the narrative; the score is a statistical model on a CPU.
Direct sales to wholesalers' associations and finance departments; integration with accounting and cheque tools (#22, #25 in this list); partnerships with lenders and marketplaces.

3 free queries [A]; onboarding of the customer's own payment history; one customer-success person per 40 customers [A], because this is B2B; quarterly model-performance reports. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by query bundle: Supplier 1.0M toman (50 queries, 20,000 each), Business 4.8M (300, 16,000 each), Lender 18M (1,500, 12,000 each) [A, priced at 11–19% of the analyst cost above; no competitor price found]. Mix 50% / 35% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 4.88M toman a month (about $18.39) [D].

Licensed access to data (government or non-government, depending on licence type); a scoring model trained on repayment outcomes, which needs labelled history that a new entrant does not have; an 8–9B model for narratives; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 credit-risk analyst and 1 compliance and legal hire (100M gross together [A]), 1 customer-success hire.
Obtaining and keeping the licence; data agreements; model building and back-testing; explaining scores; handling disputes and corrections by the people scored.

Data holders (banks, telecom operators, platforms), lenders, an existing licensed credit-scoring company as a possible reseller route; domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 282.9M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + analyst and compliance 100M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 30M = 485.9M toman a month (about $1,832) [D]; one-time setup 300M for legal work, licence and first data agreements [A]. Variable: data purchase 6,000 toman per query [A], gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 40 customers [A].
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + analyst and compliance 100M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] 3,000 input (features and data summary) + 500 output narrative; text workload, so the #1 throughput proxy applies
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[A] no price found; the fee-cap paper proposes operating cost plus 30% for scoring firms, with no amounts [S]
[D] 70% use [A] of the 50 / 300 / 1,500 bundles, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node could serve about 1,879 customers at this usage [D: 472,527 ÷ (249 + 3 trial queries)], so the GPU is not the constraint.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 146 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 485.9M ÷ (4.88M × 0.99 − 249 queries × 6,317 toman) = 145.5], and stepping through customer counts with the hires each needs gives 190 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 300M setup falls in month 1. Data purchase is charged per query in the cash rows.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian suppliers that extend trade credit and would buy scores was found. In the conservative and base cases cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position and would grow if losses continued [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −10,359M toman in the conservative case, −8,548M in the base case and −3,646M in the optimistic case [D]; the optimistic peak of 5,162M came earlier, before revenue overtook cost.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 3% monthly churn [A, B2B risk tools are embedded in credit workflows] lifetime contribution per customer is about 111M toman [D: (4.88M × 0.99 − 249 × 6,317) ÷ 0.03]. Data price sensitivity: at 20,000 toman per query the Business and Lender plans had negative gross margins in my first run [D]. Sales cost per account was not modelled.

risks.x: Licence: a Type I or Type II credit-scoring licence may be required; conditions, capital and timing were not found, and operating without one could stop the service.
Data access and price: scores depend on data from banks, telecom operators or platforms that a start-up may not obtain; the data price is a pure assumption here.
Cold start: a scoring model needs repayment outcomes; the first months run on rules and supplier-reported history.
Liability and fairness: a wrong low score can cost a small firm its supplier credit; disputes and corrections must be handled, and the fee-cap paper suggests regulators care about this.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: Whether the licence is needed for B2B trade scoring, its requirements and cost, and which of the two types fits; I read only the abstract of one paper.

Prices of data and of existing credit reports in Iran (the one scoring company's data listing says pricing is not published [S, datarade.ai/data-providers/iran-credit-scoring/profile, read 24 Oct 2026]).
The number of suppliers that extend credit and their current spending on credit checks.
Which data sources a Type II company can actually obtain and under what consent rules.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 24 Oct 2026.

segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۴: شاخص‌بندی تورم، قیمت‌گذاری و پیش‌بینی تقاضا

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: درگاه‌ها و فروشگاه‌ها (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: شارژبک و تقلب مثلثی کارت‌های سرقتی. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۴۶ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۶۷ پایه، ۶۱ رشد، ۱۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۶٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «شارژبک و تقلب مثلثی کارت‌های سرقتی» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: تحلیل ناهنجاری لحظه‌ای IP، سرعت شبا/کارت و گراف دستگاه؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق زرین‌پال، پی‌پینگ، وندار و صرافی‌های رمزارز/طلا به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۵٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۴۴٬۸۵۷٬۴۱۲ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۰۱ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر تراکنش): پایه ۱٬۶۲۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۴۲۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۵٬۸۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۴۱۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۴۸۱٬۷۵۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۴۶۰٬۰۷۶٬۰۲۵ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۱۸ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۲۷٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۴٬۳۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: LightGBM / Prophet با فصلیت جلالی + حل‌کننده قید OR-Tools + توضیح‌دهنده Qwen3-8B روی CPU/GPU مشترک. مجموعه داده: تحلیل ناهنجاری لحظه‌ای IP، سرعت شبا/کارت و گراف دستگاه.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی تحلیل ناهنجاری لحظه‌ای IP، سرعت شبا/کارت و گراف دستگاه؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های زرین‌پال، پی‌پینگ، وندار و صرافی‌های رمزارز/طلا در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: زرین‌پال، پی‌پینگ، وندار و صرافی‌های رمزارز/طلا. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: weak on these assumptions, and dependent on data I could not confirm. The model cost is almost nil (about 4.5 toman per scored transaction, gross margin 70–95% [D]) because scoring is a CPU model and only an assumed 5% of transactions get a written explanation [A]; the economics are set by fixed cost. Revenue per customer is about 1.89M toman a month ($7.12) against 484.8M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 259 paying customers on paper and 358 with GPU nodes and hires counted [D]. The base case (80 customers at month 12, 350 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months but is almost level at the end (−14M toman a month at month 24, cumulative cash −7,125M toman, about $26,900, a floor); the conservative case (30 / 120) loses 334M a month at month 24; only the optimistic case (200 / 900) breaks even, in month 18, with a peak cash need of 4,631M toman and +346M a month at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each leaves the base case loss-making. The market is large (Iranian e-commerce was 2.5 billion transactions in the first half of the Iranian year starting March 2025 [S]), but a fraud model needs labelled chargeback or fraud history and card or device data from customers, and I found no evidence on what Iranian gateways or merchants can share or what rules apply. The plan mix is the largest input: the 5% of customers that are payment providers send 2 million transactions each in the model. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Online shops with a few thousand paid orders a month that lose money to fake orders, stolen-card use and return abuse — core by number. (b) Mid-sized gateways and marketplaces. (c) Payment service providers licensed by the national card network, by volume the largest accounts. Pool: Shaparak, the national card network, handles more than 50 billion transactions a year [S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaparak\_(company), read 24 Oct 2026, citing a June 2024 report]; in the first half of the Iranian year (21 March to 22 September 2025) e-commerce had 2.5 billion transactions worth 32.63 quadrillion rials, an average of about 13.15 million rials (about 1.3M toman) per transaction [S, ice.it/it/news/notizie-dal-mondo/294227, quoting the Ministry of Industry, Mining and Trade via Tehran Times, read 24 Oct 2026]. The number of payment providers and of shops that would buy fraud scoring was not found.

A real-time API that scores each order or payment attempt (0–100) from signals such as device and IP, order pattern, delivery address, phone number age, mismatch between cardholder and recipient, and the shop's own history; it returns a reason in Persian for orders sent to manual review, and learns from the shop's confirmed fraud and return labels. The labour replaced is manual review: about 3% of transactions reviewed by hand at 3 minutes each [A], about 215 toman per transaction at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 12–100 toman per scored transaction, 6–47% of that [D]. The shop's real saving is the fraud loss avoided, which cannot be sourced here.
Plug-ins for shop platforms (WooCommerce is the largest Iranian platform in one count, see #9) and gateway APIs; partnerships with payment providers; developer documentation.

Free trial of 500 scored transactions [A]; onboarding to import past fraud labels; one customer-success person per 60 customers [A]; monthly performance report (fraud caught, false alarms). Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by scored-transaction bundle: Shop 0.2M toman (2,000 transactions, 100 each), Mid gateway 2M (50,000, 40 each), PSP 25M (2,000,000, 12.5 each) [A, no competitor price found]. Mix 70% / 25% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 1.89M toman a month (about $7.12) [D].

A gradient-boosted scoring model and feature pipeline with low-latency CPU serving; an 8–9B model for reason texts; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 data scientist and 1 fraud analyst (95M gross together [A]), 1 customer-success hire; labelled fraud data (the main scarce asset).
Feature engineering; label collection; model monitoring for drift and attacks; keeping latency low; handling false positives that block real customers.
Shop-platform plug-in makers; gateways and PSPs; domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway for our own billing (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 276.8M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + analysts 95M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 20M (real-time CPU serving), accounting 8M, marketing 30M = 484.8M toman a month (about $1,827) [D]; one-time setup 200M [A]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 60 customers [A].
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + analysts 95M + 1 customer-success at 30M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] 5% of transactions get a 1,000-token explanation; scoring runs on CPU; text workload, so the #1 throughput proxy applies
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 80% use [A] of the 2,000 / 50,000 / 2,000,000 bundles, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node could serve about 361 customers at this mix [D: 33,076,865 ÷ (91,120 + 500 trial transactions)], so nodes are added as payment-provider customers arrive (3 nodes at 900 customers in the optimistic case). Real-time serving latency and CPU capacity for 2 million transactions a month per provider were not costed beyond the 20M infrastructure line.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 259 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 484.8M ÷ (1.89M × 0.99) = 259.1], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives 358 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 200M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian shops or payment providers that would buy fraud scoring was found. In the conservative and base cases cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position and would grow if losses continued [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −9,724M toman in the conservative case, −7,125M in the base case and −3,278M in the optimistic case [D]; the optimistic peak of 4,631M came earlier.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 3% monthly churn [A, a scoring API embedded in checkout is costly to remove] lifetime revenue per customer is about 62.4M toman [D: 1.89M × 0.99 ÷ 0.03]. Sales cost per account was not modelled; measure it in the trial.

risks.x: Labels and data: without confirmed fraud outcomes and device or card-related signals, a model cannot beat the shop's own rules; whether customers may share such data with a third party was not found.
Rules on card data: handling of card and payer data is regulated by the central bank and the card network; I found no text of the rules.
False positives: blocking real orders costs the shop more than the fraud it prevents; thresholds must be set per shop.
Concentration: a few payment-provider customers drive most of the volume and revenue; losing one changes the result more than losing many shops.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian payment providers and online shops, how much fraud they suffer, and what they pay for fraud tools; a fraud rate for Iranian e-commerce was not found.
Rules on sharing card, device and payer data with a scoring service; which signals Iranian gateways expose.
Competitor or in-house fraud tool prices in Iran.
Whether a gradient-boosted model reaches useful accuracy on Iranian order data without a large labelled history.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 24 Oct 2026.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on these assumptions, with a thin margin of safety and unverified demand. GPU cost is about 136 toman per summary or answer (an assumed 1,500 tokens on a text model) and gross margin is 88–92% [D]. Revenue per customer is about 304,000 toman a month ($1.15) against 417.1M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 1,386 paying customers on paper and 1,754 with GPU nodes and hires counted [D]. The base case (1,000 customers at month 12, 5,000 at month 24) breaks even in month 15 with a peak cash need of 3,548M toman (about $13,372) and +569M toman a month at month 24; cumulative cash only returns to +193M by month 24. The conservative case (300 / 1,500) never breaks even and is still losing 76M a month at month 24 (cumulative cash −6,502M, about $24,509, a floor); the optimistic case (3,000 / 15,000) breaks even in month 9 with a peak cash need of 1,837M. GPU price doubled, prices 30% lower and customers halved each push base break-even to month 17, 19 and 20 but stay profitable at month 24. Against that, I found no competitor price, no current count of active retail traders (the only sourced count is 9 million registered shareholders in 2016), and no text on whether summarising filings for investors needs a licence; the exchange also closed for nine days and fell sharply in June 2025, which hits customer numbers directly. Persian financial-text accuracy of a small model, especially on numbers in statements, was not tested. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Active retail investors who follow several listed companies and want to know what a new filing changes (profit forecast revisions, capital increases, dividend proposals, auditor opinions, monthly production and sales reports) — core by number. (b) Analysts, small research desks and financial journalists, who send many queries and want an API. (c) Accountants and company-secretary staff who track the filings of competitors or clients. Not targeted: users who want buy or sell recommendations, which this service does not give. Pool: Wikipedia lists about 388 listed companies in December 2024 and 9 million registered shareholders in 2016 (the latest shareholder count on the page; 4.5 million in 2011 and 7 million in 2014) [S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehran\_Stock\_Exchange, read 25 Oct 2026]; the exchange's May 2025 bulletin header reads 394 companies and 40 industries [S, TSE Bulletin May 2025, mondovisione.com PDF, read 25 Oct 2026]; foreign investors numbered 5,100 in the month ending 22 July 2025 [S, ice.it/it/news/notizie-dal-mondo/289696, read 25 Oct 2026]. No current count of retail investors who read filings was found.

Within minutes of a filing, the service sends a short Persian summary of what is new (figures compared with the previous period, the reason given, the date effective), flags the kind of notice, and answers questions over a company's filing history; every summary links to the original filing and carries a fixed notice that it is information, not advice. The labour replaced is reading and noting a filing by hand: 10 minutes per filing [A], about 23,837 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 750–1,200 toman per summary or answer, 3–5% of that [D]. The investor's real benefit, a missed or late reaction to a notice, cannot be sourced here.

A Bale/Eitaa/Telegram-style bot for watch-list alerts, a mobile web app, an API for analysts; acquisition through market-education channels, creators who discuss listed companies, and broker or portfolio-app partnerships.

Free trial of 20 summaries or answers [A]; self-serve; a visible link from each summary to its source filing; a monthly correction log; one customer-success person per 500 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate (see risks).

Monthly by number of summaries or answers: Basic 120,000 toman (100 items, about $0.45), Pro 350,000 (400, about $1.32), Analyst 1,500,000 (2,000 with API, about $5.65) [A, set at a few percent of the manual reading cost above; no competitor price was found]. Mix 60% / 32% / 8% [A] gives ARPU 304,000 toman a month (about $1.15) [D].

An 8B-class open instruction model with Persian output tuning and retrieval over each company's filing history; a pipeline that collects new filings and reads their PDFs, Excel files and tables; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 financial analyst or editor who checks summaries (40M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Collecting filings continuously; extracting the numbers in statements and checking each summary's figures against the source; classifying notices by type; keeping latency to minutes; handling errors and corrections quickly; keeping every output on the information side of the advice line.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); brokers and portfolio apps as distributors; the exchange or a data vendor if a licence for automated access is needed (terms not verified).

Fixed: team 209.1M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 analyst at 40M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure and filing archive 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 417.1M toman a month (about $1,572) [D]; one-time setup 150M [A]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 500 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 analyst at 40M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 1,000 tokens of retrieved filing text (the shared summary is cached) plus about 500 for question and answer; text workload, so the #1 throughput proxy applies
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 60% use [A] of the 100 / 400 / 2,000 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 4,819 customers at this usage [D: 1,102,562 ÷ (208.8 + 20 free-trial items)], so a second node is needed in the base case at about 5,000 customers and four in the optimistic case at 15,000 [D]. The cost of reading and parsing filings (PDF and Excel extraction, tables) was not separated; it is assumed to sit inside the 10M infrastructure line and the node, and the real GPU or CPU time per filing was not measured.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 1,386 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 417.1M ÷ (304,000 × 0.99) = 1,385.9], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives 1,754 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 150M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian investors who would pay for a filing summary was found. For scale only, 5,000 customers is 0.06% and 15,000 is 0.17% of the 9 million shareholders registered in 2016 [D, the latest count found, so the active pool may be smaller or larger]. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −6,502M toman in the conservative case, +193M in the base case (payback only at about month 24) and +16,994M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 3,548M came earlier.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 8% monthly churn [A, investors cancel tools when markets fall or trading dries up] lifetime revenue per customer is about 3.76M toman [D: 304,000 × 0.99 ÷ 0.08]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot. At 30% of the base customer path (the conservative case) there is no break-even within 24 months.

risks.x: Market activity: the exchange closed for nine days during the June 2025 strikes, reopened with 3% daily price limits, fell about 200,000 index points to 2,788,000 and saw about 9 trillion toman leave the market [S, iranwire.com/en/economy/142839, 30 Jun 2025, read 25 Oct 2026]. Paying demand follows trading activity, so a weak market lowers both customers and retention.

Advice line: summarising a filing is information, but short summaries can read as recommendations. Whether the Securities and Exchange Organization requires a licence for investor-facing summaries or alerts was not found; a general overview of Iran's securities law did not address investment advisers [S, generisonline.com, read 25 Oct 2026].

Accuracy and liability: a wrong figure or a missed qualification in an audit opinion can cost a user money; each summary needs numeric checks against the source and an easy correction path, which the analyst hire in the model only partly covers.
Free and bundled substitutes: filings are public, and brokers and portfolio apps can add summaries as a feature; I could not read competitor pages to compare price or quality.
Data access: automated collection from the exchange's disclosure portal may be restricted by its terms or rate limits; the terms were not checked.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of active retail investors and analysts today, and how many read filings; the latest shareholder count found is for 2016.
Prices of Iranian filing-alert and market-data subscriptions; the competitor and exchange-related pages I tried were blocked from automated reading or returned unrelated results.
Whether summaries or alerts for investors need a Securities and Exchange Organization licence, and the exchange's terms on automated access to filings.
Accuracy of an 8B-class model on Persian financial statements and notices, and real tokens per filing; the 1,500-token figure and the 30% utilisation are assumptions.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

title: ماشین‌حساب شاخص‌بندی قرارداد و بودجه برای شروط تورمی
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۴: شاخص‌بندی تورم، قیمت‌گذاری و پیش‌بینی تقاضا

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: پیمانکاران و موجران (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: قراردادهای بلندمدت ریالی با شاخص‌بندی ناکافی. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۹۶ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۸۵ پایه، ۸۳ رشد، ۲۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۶٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «قراردادهای بلندمدت ریالی با شاخص‌بندی ناکافی» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: موتور خودکار شروط تعدیل CPI/PPI و نرخ ارز؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق بولتن‌های ماهانه تورم مرکز آمار و بانک مرکزی و سازمان برنامه به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۵٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۶۴٬۵۴۶٬۹۸۱ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۱۰ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (ماهانه): پایه ۱٬۴۷۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۶۴۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۲۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۴۷۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۹۳٬۲۱۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۶۶۲٬۰۲۰٬۳۲۵ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۲۴ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۳۶٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۵٬۹۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: LightGBM / Prophet با فصلیت جلالی + حل‌کننده قید OR-Tools + توضیح‌دهنده Qwen3-8B روی CPU/GPU مشترک. مجموعه داده: موتور خودکار شروط تعدیل CPI/PPI و نرخ ارز.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی موتور خودکار شروط تعدیل CPI/PPI و نرخ ارز؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های بولتن‌های ماهانه تورم مرکز آمار و بانک مرکزی و سازمان برنامه در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: بولتن‌های ماهانه تورم مرکز آمار و بانک مرکزی و سازمان برنامه. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal. Model cost is small (about 363 toman per calculation, gross margin 91–94% [D]) because the arithmetic is deterministic and the model only reads the clause and writes the explanation; the economics are set by fixed cost. Revenue per customer is about 323,450 toman a month ($1.22) against 412.1M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 1,287 paying customers on paper and 1,748 with hires counted [D]. The base case (500 customers at month 12, 2,500 at month 24) breaks even in month 20 with a peak cash need of 4,845M toman (about $18,264) and +167M a month at month 24, but cumulative cash is still −4,359M, so payback is well beyond month 24. The conservative case (150 / 700) never breaks even (−225M a month at month 24, cumulative cash −7,917M, about $29,844, a floor); the optimistic case (1,500 / 8,000) breaks even in month 13 with +1,262M a month at month 24. Doubling the GPU price delays base break-even to month 23 with +17M at month 24; cutting prices 30% or halving customers leaves the base case loss-making. Demand rests on very high inflation (73% year on year in April 2026 [S]) and on rules that cap rent increases and make price adjustment a main source of contractor disputes, but I found no count of landlords or contractors who would pay, no price of a competing tool, and no source for the official indices the calculator would read. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Small and mid-size contractors and subcontractors with price-adjustment (ta'dil) or inflation clauses in public and private contracts, who must prepare adjustment claims — core by revenue. (b) Landlords, property managers and tenants who apply the legal rent-increase cap at each renewal — core by number, low price. (c) Accountants, engineers and lawyers who prepare such calculations for clients. Not targeted: public employers with their own budget offices. Context: Iranian leases renew yearly and the 2024 housing-market law sets mandatory rent caps, between 50% and 100% of provincial inflation where inflation exceeds 30%, with fines of up to ten times the unauthorized excess and a duty to register the lease for a tracking code [S, landager.com/en/property-compliance/iran/national/rent-increases and /overview, pages updated 9 May 2026, read 25 Oct 2026; the pages give 26% and 24% in one place and 25% for Tehran and 20% for other large cities in another, so the exact caps are not confirmed]. Official rents rose 31% year on year in April 2026 against 73% general inflation, and the 25% cap is described by local media as working as a de facto floor [S, aljazeera.com/news/2026/5/19/high-prices-in-iran-stunted-housing-market-leave-tenants-with-few-options, read 25 Oct 2026]. A study of 50 civil projects found price-adjustment disputes as a main cause of contractor claims, with final adjustment discrepancies averaging 28% without capital-adjustment insurance cover and 12% with it, and resolution times falling from 18 to under 6 months [S, qgl.lri.ir/article\_248464\_en.html, read 25 Oct 2026; 2021 data, small sample]. No count of landlords, rental contracts, contractors or ongoing contracts with indexation clauses was found.

The user uploads or pastes the clause and the contract amounts, or answers a few questions for a lease; the service identifies the formula (index, base date, weights, cap), fetches the matching published index values, shows a worked table and produces a ready notice, claim letter or renewal offer in Persian, with the calculation open for checking. The labour replaced is reading the clause, finding index values, calculating and writing the notice by hand: 20 minutes [A], about 47,674 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 3,200–4,900 toman per calculation, 7–10% of that [D]. The saving that matters, a claim filed correctly or a cap applied without a dispute, cannot be sourced here.

Mobile web app and a Bale/Eitaa/Telegram-style bot for landlords; direct sales and association talks for contractors; integrations or referrals with real-estate agency software and with engineering and accounting offices.

Free trial of 3 calculations [A]; self-serve with a worked example library; a reminder before each lease renewal or contract anniversary; one customer-success person per 400 customers [A]; a disclaimer that the output is a calculation aid, not legal advice. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate (see risks).

Monthly by number of calculations: Landlord 49,000 toman (10 calculations, about $0.18), Contractor 390,000 (100, about $1.47), Firm 1,600,000 (500, multi-project, about $6.03) [A, set at 7–10% of the manual cost above; no competitor price was found]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 323,450 toman a month (about $1.22) [D].

An 8B-class open instruction model for clause reading and letter drafting; a deterministic calculation engine with tests per clause type; a maintained library of published indices and rent caps (source and licence not confirmed); a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 part-time engineer-lawyer reviewer (40M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Keeping index tables and legal caps current; checking extracted formulas against the clause text; template letters for claims and renewals; support for disputes; making every number traceable to its index and date.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); real-estate agency software makers; engineering and contractor associations; the bodies that publish the indices (terms not verified).

Fixed: team 209.1M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 reviewer at 40M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure and index-data upkeep 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 30M = 412.1M toman a month (about $1,553) [D]; one-time setup 150M [A]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 400 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 reviewer at 40M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 3,000 input (clause excerpt and contract data) plus about 1,000 output (formula, worked table, letter); text workload, so the #1 throughput proxy applies
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 70% use [A] of the 10 / 100 / 500 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 6,232 customers at this usage [D: 413,461 ÷ (63.4 + 3 free-trial calculations)], so the optimistic case needs a second node near its month-24 level and the base case needs one. The calculation engine itself runs on CPU and is not costed separately; the 15M infrastructure line is an assumption that also covers keeping index tables current.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 1,287 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 412.1M ÷ (323,450 × 0.99) = 1,286.9], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives 1,748 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 150M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian landlords, contractors or indexed contracts was found. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −7,917M toman in the conservative case, −4,359M in the base case and +5,607M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 4,845M came earlier, in the month before break-even, and payback is well beyond month 24.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 10% monthly churn [A, a lease is renewed once a year, so landlords may subscribe for one use and leave] lifetime revenue per customer is about 3.20M toman [D: 323,450 × 0.99 ÷ 0.10]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Free substitutes: rent-increase and indexation calculators are simple enough that free web calculators or an agent's spreadsheet may satisfy landlords; I could not read any competitor page to compare, so the landlord plan may not sell at all.

Unsettled rules: the rent cap in force for 2026 and the way it is set (50%–100% of provincial inflation under the 2024 law [S]) were not confirmed, and the sources found conflict on the figures; a calculator that applies a wrong cap creates liability.
Index data: the calculator needs official index values (price indices and construction cost indices) in machine-readable form; their publishers, licences and update lag were not confirmed.

Contract variety: adjustment clauses differ by employer and contract template, and a study found no unified guideline for calculating adjustment damages [S, qgl.lri.ir/article\_248464\_en.html]; clause reading errors can change a claim by a large amount, so human review is needed for large contracts.

Concentration and timing: lease renewals cluster in some months, and contractor claims depend on public-sector payment behaviour; revenue may be seasonal, which the straight-line customer path does not show.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of landlords, rental contracts, contractors and contracts with adjustment clauses; no housing-statistics count was found.
Prices of competing calculators or advisory services and whether free ones already serve landlords.
The rent caps in force for 2026, the publishers and licences of the official indices, and whether registration systems expose lease data to third parties.
Real tokens per calculation, throughput on the actual node, and accuracy of an 8B-class model at reading Persian contract clauses.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

title: دستیار محاسبه حقوق و بیمه تأمین اجتماعی
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۶: عامل‌های گردش‌کار چندپلتفرمی و خودکارساز انطباق

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: منابع انسانی و حسابداران (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: کارشناس حقوق و دستمزد (۲۵ میلیون تومان در ماه) به‌همراه جریمه‌های تأمین اجتماعی. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۶۸ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۵۶ پایه، ۹۴ رشد، ۱۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۶٫۸٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «کارشناس حقوق و دستمزد (۲۵ میلیون تومان در ماه) به‌همراه جریمه‌های تأمین اجتماعی» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: قواعد مسکن، فرزند و اضافه‌کاری قانون کار ۱۴۰۵؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق دیسکت لیست تأمین اجتماعی و پورتال مالیاتی به‌همراه ۰٫۶۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۸٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۵۸٬۸۵۰٬۸۲۴ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۲۰ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر کارمند): پایه ۱٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۲٬۶۵۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۲۶٬۷۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۰۲٬۹۹۸٬۵۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی قواعد مسکن، فرزند و اضافه‌کاری قانون کار ۱۴۰۵؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های دیسکت لیست تأمین اجتماعی و پورتال مالیاتی در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal. Model cost is small (about 109 toman per employee-month, gross margin 98% [D]) because the pay, insurance and tax arithmetic is deterministic code and the model only reads attendance notes and exceptions and writes flags; the economics are set by fixed cost. Revenue per customer is about 752,000 toman a month ($2.83) against 429.4M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 577 paying customers on paper and 825 with hires counted [D]. The base case (300 customers at month 12, 1,500 at month 24) breaks even in month 18 with a peak cash need of 4,595M toman (about $17,321) and +318M a month at month 24, but cumulative cash is still −3,340M, so payback is beyond month 24. The conservative case (100 / 500) never breaks even (−168M a month at month 24, cumulative cash −7,602M, about $28,656, a floor); the optimistic case (800 / 4,000) breaks even in month 13 with +1,589M a month at month 24. Doubling the GPU price delays base break-even to month 21 and keeps month 24 profitable (+168M); cutting prices 30% or halving customers each leaves the base case loss-making through month 24. The need is real (statutory rates and the minimum wage change every year; the monthly minimum wage rose about 60% from 20 March 2026, from 103,909,680 to 166,255,500 rials [D, from S: wageindicator.org, read 25 Oct 2026]), but I found no competitor price or count of employers, and payroll modules inside established accounting packages are a likely substitute that I could not read. Correctness against the current insurance and tax rules is a hard requirement that I could not check line by line. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Accountants and bookkeeping offices that run payroll for several small clients — core by account size. (b) HR and finance staff of firms with 20–500 employees who still use spreadsheets. (c) Small businesses with under 20 employees who run payroll themselves. Not targeted: large employers with an ERP payroll module and in-house payroll staff. Pool: Iran had 24,983,452 employed persons in Q4 2024 [S, tradingeconomics.com/iran/employed-persons citing the Statistical Centre of Iran, read 23 Oct 2026]; the Social Security Organization reported about 12 million insured contributors and 37 million beneficiaries in 2014 [S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social\_Security\_Organization, read 25 Oct 2026; old and not split by employer]. No count of employers or payroll offices was found.

The customer uploads or types attendance, overtime, leave and mission data (or forwards a spreadsheet); the service computes pay, employee and employer insurance, income tax, severance and annual-leave accruals, the New Year bonus and allowances under the current year's rules, flags anomalies (pay below the minimum, overtime above the legal limit, missing insurance days), prepares payslips and the monthly insurance list for upload, and answers rule questions in Persian with the article cited. The labour replaced is doing this by hand or in a spreadsheet: 15 minutes per employee-month [A], about 35,756 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 7,000–11,000 toman per employee-month, 20–31% of that [D]. Employer insurance is 23% of gross pay (the 23% used in the 143,023 figure) and employee insurance 7%, 30% together [S, rivermate.com/guides/iran/taxes, read 25 Oct 2026; undated].

Web app with spreadsheet upload; an accountant partner programme (one accountant brings many client firms); integrations or export files for common Iranian accounting packages (formats not verified); acquisition through accountant communities and HR groups.

Free first month for up to 5 employees [A]; onboarding of the company's pay rules; one customer-success person per 150 customers [A]; a rule-change notice each year when the minimum wage and insurance ceilings are set, with re-run of the previous month for comparison. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by employees processed: Small 220,000 toman (up to 20 employees, about $0.83), Mid 900,000 (100, about $3.39), Large 3,500,000 (500, about $13.19) [A, set at 20–31% of the manual cost above; no competitor price was found]. Mix 60% / 30% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 752,000 toman a month (about $2.83) [D].

A tested rules engine for pay, insurance and income tax, updated every year; an 8B-class open instruction model for reading exceptions and answering rule questions; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 payroll and labour-law specialist (50M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.
Annual rule update and regression tests against worked examples; insurance-list file format maintenance; anomaly checks; answering rule questions with citations; protecting salary data.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); accountant networks; makers of accounting software that could import payroll results.

Fixed: team 221.4M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 specialist at 50M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure and encrypted storage 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 429.4M toman a month (about $1,619) [D]; one-time setup 200M [A] (rules engine and worked-example tests). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 150 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 specialist at 50M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 800 input (attendance and exception notes) plus about 400 output (flags and payslip note); the pay calculation is code, not tokens; text workload, so the #1 throughput proxy applies
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]

cost_model.x: One node covers about 15,697 customers at this usage [D: 1,378,203 ÷ (82.8 + 5 free-trial employee-months)], so the GPU is not the binding cost; the fixed node price is. A smaller or shared GPU would change the result and was not modelled. Encrypted storage of salary data is assumed to sit inside the 10M infrastructure line.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 577 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 429.4M ÷ (752,000 × 0.99) = 576.8], and stepping through customer counts with the hires each needs gives 825 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 200M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced count of Iranian employers or payroll offices was found. For scale only, base-case month-24 customers process about 124,000 employee-months a month [D: 1,500 × 82.8], about 1% of the roughly 12 million insured contributors reported for 2014 [D, S above]. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −7,602M toman in the conservative case, −3,340M in the base case and +7,463M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 4,595M came earlier, and payback is beyond month 24.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 4% monthly churn [A, payroll data and history are costly to move, but small firms close or switch to a bundled module] lifetime revenue per customer is about 18.6M toman [D: 752,000 × 0.99 ÷ 0.04]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Rule accuracy: a wrong insurance base, ceiling or tax bracket creates penalties for the employer and ends the customer; the rules change each year (minimum wage up about 60% in March 2026 [D, S above]) and this model prices one specialist and an annual update but no outside legal review.

Bundled substitutes: payroll modules in established Iranian accounting packages are a likely free or low-cost alternative; I could not open their pages (the vendor payroll page I tried was blocked from automated reading), so the price and quality gap is unknown.

Insurance-list upload: the monthly list is submitted to the Social Security Organization; whether it offers an API or only a file upload format was not confirmed, so the service may only prepare a file the customer submits by hand.
Data sensitivity: salary data of employees is personal data; I found no rule on hosting but a customer may require domestic hosting, which this model assumes.
Customer mix: the Mid and Large plans are 40% of customers but 82% of revenue in the model [D: (0.30 × 900,000 + 0.10 × 3,500,000) ÷ 752,000]; losing a few large accounts changes the result.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian employers, accountants who run payroll for clients, and workshops registered with the Social Security Organization; the only count found is an old national contributor figure.
Prices and features of payroll modules in Iranian accounting software, and any standalone payroll tool.
Current tax brackets, the insurance ceilings for 2026 and the format and access method of the monthly insurance list; the rate page found gave contribution rates only and no tax brackets.
Real tokens per employee-month, throughput on the actual node, and accuracy of an 8B-class model on Persian attendance notes.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

title: پیش‌نویس و بازبینی قرارداد فارسی
buyer: مؤسسات حقوقی و کسب‌وکارهای کوچک و متوسط
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۱: گفتگوی فارسی و بازیابی ترکیبی (RAG)

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: مؤسسات حقوقی و کسب‌وکارهای کوچک و متوسط (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: مشاور حقوقی بیرونی (۵ تا ۲۰ میلیون تومان به‌ازای هر قرارداد). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۶۶ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۷۱ پایه، ۷۰ رشد، ۲۵ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۸٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «مشاور حقوقی بیرونی (۵ تا ۲۰ میلیون تومان به‌ازای هر قرارداد)» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: بانک شروط قانون مدنی و قانون تجارت ایران؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق افزونه فارسی مایکروسافت ورد و ویرایشگر وب به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۴٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۴۶٬۹۵۰٬۸۶۰ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۱۰ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر کاربر): پایه ۱٬۳۲۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۲٬۷۶۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۶۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۵۳۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۴۰٬۲۵۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۱۵٬۹۴۳٬۵۲۵ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۳۷ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۵۵٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۰٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen3-14B/32B کوانتیزه (AWQ، مجوز Apache 2.0) با vLLM + امبدینگ فارسی BGE-M3 + پایگاه برداری Qdrant روی CPU. مجموعه داده: بانک شروط قانون مدنی و قانون تجارت ایران.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی بانک شروط قانون مدنی و قانون تجارت ایران؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های افزونه فارسی مایکروسافت ورد و ویرایشگر وب در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: افزونه فارسی مایکروسافت ورد و ویرایشگر وب. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal, with a thin margin of safety. Model cost is higher than for a chat-style service because a contract is long and legal Persian needs a larger model: about 4,535 toman per draft or review (about $0.017) on an assumed 30B-class model, gross margin 80–84% [D]. Revenue per customer is about 1.34M toman a month ($5.06) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 355 paying customers on paper and 411 with GPU nodes and hires counted [D]. The base case (200 customers at month 12, 900 at month 24) breaks even in month 16 with a peak cash need of 4,573M toman (about $17,237) and +353M a month at month 24, but cumulative cash is still −3,219M at month 24. The conservative case (60 / 250) never breaks even (−176M a month at month 24, cumulative cash −8,372M, about $31,559, a floor); the optimistic case (500 / 2,500) breaks even in month 11. Doubling the GPU price or halving customers each pushes base break-even to month 23 with a month-24 profit of only +53M and +16M, and cutting prices 30% leaves the base case slightly loss-making (−5M). Quality is the central risk: a model that mis-reads or invents a clause creates liability for a lawyer, I found no test of Persian legal-text accuracy for any open model, and the labour replaced is priced at the minimum-wage basis (no Iranian lawyer fee was found), which understates the value. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Solo lawyers and small law offices who draft and check commercial contracts, leases and agreements — core by number. (b) SMEs with no in-house counsel that need a first draft or a risk check before signing. (c) Larger firms and company legal departments that want clause libraries and consistent review. Not targeted: litigation work and political or security cases. Pool: the American Bar Association reports more than 70,000 qualified lawyers in Iran (undated) and 31 areas in which lawyers can seek specialization certificates, contract law among them, under a directive of 16 January 2022 [S, americanbar.org legal-profession-in-iran-steps-toward-specialization, read 25 Oct 2026]; Wikipedia gives over 20,000 members for the Central Bar Association, citing a 2018 article, with 16 regional bar associations in all [S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran\_Central\_Bar\_Association, read 25 Oct 2026]. No count of SMEs that buy legal drafting was found.

The user pastes or uploads a contract (or answers questions to draft one); the service flags missing or one-sided clauses, inconsistencies in names, dates and amounts, and ambiguous Persian wording, proposes replacement text from a clause library, and produces a clean draft with a short issue table, always with the source clause quoted. The labour replaced is a first read and issue list or a first draft: 45 minutes [A], valued here at 107,267 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), which understates a lawyer's time; no Iranian lawyer fee was found. The plans below charge 11,667–15,000 toman per document, 11–14% of that figure [D]. Reference points abroad: Luminance is listed at $10–$100 per user per month by a price-comparison site with no stated date, and Harvey publishes no price as of March 2026 [S, costbench.com/compare/harvey-ai-vs-luminance, read 25 Oct 2026]; the Solo plan below is about $1.70 a month.
Web app with Word import and export; a plug-in or email-forwarding route for lawyers; bar-association workshops and legal-education channels; referral by accountants and consultants for SMEs.

Free trial of 10 documents [A]; template and clause libraries by contract type; a human lawyer review option sold per document (not modelled); one customer-success person per 150 customers [A]; every output marked as a drafting aid that a qualified person must check. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of drafts or reviews: Solo 450,000 toman (30 documents, about $1.70), Office 2,000,000 (150, about $7.54), Firm 7,000,000 (600, about $26.39) [A, no Iranian competitor price was found; a legal-AI app named Robovakil exists on a store page I could not read]. Mix 65% / 28% / 7% [A] gives ARPU 1,342,500 toman a month (about $5.06) [D].

A 30B-class open instruction model with Persian legal tuning and retrieval over a clause library; Persian legal templates reviewed by lawyers; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 lawyer or legal editor (80M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Building and reviewing the clause library; evaluating outputs against lawyer-written answers; Word and PDF parsing of Persian contracts; keeping Iranian civil-code references correct; handling confidentiality and data residency.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); law firms or bar-association bodies as reviewers and distributors; legal publishers if a licence for statute text is needed (terms not verified).

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure and encrypted document storage 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 471.3M toman a month (about $1,777) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (clause library and evaluation set). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 150 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 12,000 input (contract and clause-library context) plus about 3,000 output (issue table and redline text)

[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 0.30 (a 30B-class model runs about 3.3 times slower than the 8B benchmark, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 50% use [A] of the 30 / 150 / 600 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 536 customers at this usage [D: 33,077 ÷ (51.8 + 10 free-trial documents)], so GPU nodes step up with customers: 2 nodes in the base case at 900 customers and 5 in the optimistic case at 2,500 [D]. A 30B-class model may not fit one 48 GB card at full context with the batch sizes assumed, and I did not test it; a smaller model would cut cost and accuracy together.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 355 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 471.3M ÷ (1,342,500 × 0.99) = 354.6], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 411 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. For scale only, 900 accounts is 1.3% of the 70,000-plus lawyers reported by the American Bar Association [D, S above], although many accounts would be offices of several lawyers and some would be SMEs. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −8,372M toman in the conservative case, −3,219M in the base case and +8,056M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 4,573M came earlier, and payback is beyond month 24.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 5% monthly churn [A, a clause library and saved drafts are costly to move, but trust in the output may fail early] lifetime revenue per customer is about 26.6M toman [D: 1,342,500 × 0.99 ÷ 0.05]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Output quality and liability: a clause the model misreads, or a fabricated article reference, is the lawyer's liability; I found no benchmark of Persian legal text for open models, so the model size, the retrieval design and the human-review cost (one legal editor in the model) are all unverified.
Confidentiality: client contracts are confidential; many lawyers and firms will require domestic hosting and no training on their documents, which the model assumes but I could not confirm as a rule.

Regulatory standing of the bar: the judiciary controls licensing and bar governance, and the profession is under pressure [S, ibanet.org New-report-No-Defence, 4 Dec 2025, read 25 Oct 2026]; this may slow adoption through bar channels and raise caution about storing client files.

Substitutes: general chat assistants already draft contracts in Persian at no or low price; the value of this service depends on clause libraries, Iranian-law accuracy and Word workflow, which I could not compare.
Price level: Solo lawyers may value the tool at far more or far less than the 450,000 toman assumed; no Iranian lawyer fee or competitor price was found.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of practising lawyers today, SMEs that buy drafting help, and in-house legal departments; the counts found are undated or old.
Iranian lawyer fees for drafting and review, and prices of Iranian legal-AI tools (a store page for one app was blocked from automated reading).
Accuracy of any open 30B-class model on Persian contracts and Iranian civil law, real tokens per document, and whether such a model runs at the assumed throughput on the RTX 6000 Ada node.
Rules on storing and processing client documents outside the lawyer's own premises, and on non-lawyers offering contract drafting.
Licensing of statute and clause-library text.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

title: پرسش و پاسخ حقوق ایران با استناد به مواد قانونی
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۱: گفتگوی فارسی و بازیابی ترکیبی (RAG)

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: وکلا و عموم مردم (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: پژوهشگر حقوقی تازه‌کار (۲۲ میلیون تومان در ماه). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۹۳ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۸۱ پایه، ۸۲ رشد، ۳۰ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۸٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «پژوهشگر حقوقی تازه‌کار (۲۲ میلیون تومان در ماه)» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: RAG با ارجاع تأییدشده روی تمام قوانین ایران و آرای وحدت رویه دیوان عالی؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق داتیک و آرشیو حقوقی مجلس به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۴٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۵۲٬۳۴۷٬۲۲۶ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۱۵ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (ماهانه): پایه ۱٬۲۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۲٬۸۷۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۸۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۳۲۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۰۲٬۳۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۷۵٬۲۴۴٬۲۵۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۴۳ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۶۴٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۰٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen3-14B/32B کوانتیزه (AWQ، مجوز Apache 2.0) با vLLM + امبدینگ فارسی BGE-M3 + پایگاه برداری Qdrant روی CPU. مجموعه داده: RAG با ارجاع تأییدشده روی تمام قوانین ایران و آرای وحدت رویه دیوان عالی.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی RAG با ارجاع تأییدشده روی تمام قوانین ایران و آرای وحدت رویه دیوان عالی؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های داتیک و آرشیو حقوقی مجلس در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: داتیک و آرشیو حقوقی مجلس. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

bmc.title: ساختار هزینه (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: هزینه کامل مستقل: ۴۱۵٬۶۸۸٬۱۱۵ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA مستقل: ۱۸۶٬۶۶۱٬۸۸۵ تومان/ماه (۳۱٫۰٪). هزینه سبد موتور مشترک (تقسیم توسعه/دفتر بین ۳ ابزار هم‌خانواده): ۳۳۷٬۴۴۸٬۱۱۵ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA سبد: ۲۶۴٬۹۰۱٬۸۸۵ تومان/ماه (۴۴٫۰٪).
