verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Each answer needs retrieved articles and a larger model for legal Persian, so GPU cost is about 1,391 toman per answered question (about $0.0052) and gross margin is 62–71% [D], but the prices a citizen or a lawyer can plausibly pay per question are small. Revenue per customer is about 265,500 toman a month ($1.00) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 1,793 paying customers on paper and about 6,454 with GPU nodes and hires counted [D]. The base case (800 customers at month 12, 4,000 at month 24) never breaks even (−200M toman a month at month 24, cumulative cash −7,744M, about $29,190, a floor); the conservative case (200 / 1,000) loses 319M a month; only the optimistic case (2,500 / 12,000) breaks even, in month 17, with a peak cash need of 4,478M, +157M at month 24 and cumulative cash still −3,758M. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base-case loss. The service would also compete with free access to the statutes themselves and with general chat assistants, and I found no test of how reliably a Persian model cites the right article without inventing one. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Citizens with everyday legal questions on rent, employment, inheritance, cheques, traffic fines and consumer disputes — core by number, lowest willingness to pay. (b) Lawyers and trainee lawyers who want a fast first pass through statutes, regulations and rulings. (c) Accountants, real-estate agents and HR staff who need the relevant article. Not targeted: representation in court and answers that replace a lawyer. Pool: more than 70,000 qualified lawyers in Iran (undated) [S, americanbar.org legal-profession-in-iran-steps-toward-specialization, read 25 Oct 2026]. No count of citizens who seek legal information online was found. Iranian legislation was free to read online but not openly licensed or machine-readable in the 2015 Open Data Index, with dotic.ir named as the online source [S, 2015.index.okfn.org/place/iran/legislation, read 25 Oct 2026; ten years old].

The user asks a question in plain Persian and gets a short answer that quotes the relevant articles (law, article number, text) and, where available, notes on contrary rulings, with a clear statement of what is uncertain; a lawyer plan adds a clause or ruling search. The labour replaced is finding the articles and writing a short answer: 15 minutes [A], about 35,756 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), which understates a lawyer's time; the plans below charge 2,250–3,000 toman per question, 6–8% of that [D]. The value to a citizen, avoiding a wrong step or a lawyer visit, cannot be sourced here, and no Iranian consultation fee could be read.

Bale/Eitaa/Telegram-style bot and a mobile web app for citizens; a browser extension or web tool for lawyers; partnerships with legal-education channels, law-student groups and real-estate or HR associations.

Free trial of 5 questions [A]; every answer quotes its source text with a link to the statute page; a visible "not legal advice" notice and a way to ask a human lawyer (not modelled); one customer-success person per 300 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of questions: Citizen 90,000 toman (30 questions, about $0.34), Lawyer 450,000 (150, about $1.70), Office 1,800,000 (800, about $6.79) [A, no competitor price was found]. Mix 70% / 25% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 265,500 toman a month (about $1.00) [D].

A 30B-class open instruction model with Persian legal tuning; a retrieval index over statutes, regulations and rulings with article-level chunks (source text licence unconfirmed); a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 lawyer or legal editor (80M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Collecting and updating legal texts; checking that every cited article exists and says what the answer claims; evaluating answers against lawyer-written ones; handling amendments and conflicting rules.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); law faculties and bar bodies for review; the publishers of legal texts if a licence is required (terms not verified).

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure and retrieval index 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 471.3M toman a month (about $1,777) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (text collection and evaluation set). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 300 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 4,000 input (retrieved articles and context) plus about 600 output (answer with citations)

[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 0.30 (a 30B-class model runs about 3.3 times slower than the 8B benchmark, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 60% use [A] of the 30 / 150 / 800 quotas, weighted by plan mix
[D] team 258.3M + GPU 150M + infrastructure and retrieval index 15M + accounting 8M + marketing 40M

cost_model.x: One node covers about 1,683 customers at this usage [D: 107,859 ÷ (59.1 + 5 free-trial questions)], so GPU cost is small next to people: the base case needs a second node from month 16 and 3 nodes at month 24, while one customer-success hire per 300 customers adds 13 hires, about 480M toman a month, by 4,000 customers [D: 13 × 36.9M]. A 30B-class model may not fit one 48 GB card at the batch sizes assumed, and I did not test it; a smaller model would cut cost and accuracy together.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 1,793 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 471.3M ÷ (265,500 × 0.99) = 1,793.1], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and customer-success hires each needs gives 6,454 customers (4 nodes) [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. For scale only, 4,000 accounts is 5.7% of the 70,000-plus lawyers reported by the American Bar Association [D, S above], although 70% of the base-case accounts are assumed to be citizens on the cheapest plan, so the lawyer pool is only a loose guide. In the conservative and base cases cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −9,589M toman in the conservative case, −7,744M in the base case and −3,758M in the optimistic case [D]; the optimistic trough of 4,478M came in month 18, and payback is beyond month 24 in every case.

sensitivities.x: No single change rescues the base case; the sensitivities only show how much deeper the loss gets. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 10% monthly churn [A, citizens ask a few questions and leave; lawyers may stay longer] lifetime revenue per customer is about 2.63M toman [D: 265,500 × 0.99 ÷ 0.10], while customer-success staffing alone costs 123,000 toman a month per customer [D: 36.9M ÷ 300], 46% of revenue per customer, which is why growth does not close the gap; support per customer would have to be far cheaper than assumed. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Accuracy and liability: a fabricated or outdated article reference can cause a wrong legal step; I found no benchmark of how reliably open models cite the right Iranian article, so model size, retrieval design and the human-review cost (one legal editor in the model) are unverified.

Free substitutes: Iranian legislation was readable online without charge in 2015 [S, 2015.index.okfn.org/place/iran/legislation, read 25 Oct 2026], and domestic legal assistants already exist: a "RoboLegal" robot giving voice and text legal advice from Iranian cases was reported with no price and no date on the page (URL dated 17 Sep 2025) [S, meatechwatch.com/2025/09/17/iran-launches-first-ai-powered-legal-robot-robolegal-to-expand-access-to-justice, read 25 Oct 2026]; search also returned titles of a Robovakil app and a Parsivakil service, whose pages I could not read.
Price level: citizens may not pay 3,000 toman a question when the substitute is free; lawyers may pay far more or less than 450,000 toman a month; no Iranian lawyer fee or competitor price was found.

Regulatory standing: the judiciary controls licensing and bar governance and the profession is under pressure [S, ibanet.org New-report-No-Defence, 4 Dec 2025, read 25 Oct 2026]; whether a non-lawyer service may give answers that look like legal advice is not confirmed.
Text rights and freshness: laws and rulings change often and the source text licence is unconfirmed; stale retrieval would produce wrong citations.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of citizens who look for legal information online, and the number of practising lawyers today (the 70,000-plus figure is undated).
Iranian lawyer consultation fees and prices of domestic legal-AI tools (Robovakil and Parsivakil pages were blocked or title-only; RoboLegal has no price on its page).
Accuracy of any open 30B-class model on Iranian statutes, real tokens per answer, and whether such a model runs at the assumed throughput on the RTX 6000 Ada node.
Licence and machine-readable access to current statutes, regulations and rulings (the only source found is ten years old).
Rules on non-lawyers giving legal answers, and on handling personal case details.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق پایگاه آرای ناشناس پژوهشگاه قوه قضائیه به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۴٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۴۴٬۴۷۷٬۵۴۴ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۰۹ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (ماهانه): پایه ۱٬۷۷۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۲٬۹۸۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۷٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۳۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۱۱٬۷۹۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۴۸۸٬۷۶۴٬۲۲۵ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۳۶ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۵۴٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۰٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen3-14B/32B کوانتیزه (AWQ، مجوز Apache 2.0) با vLLM + امبدینگ فارسی BGE-M3 + پایگاه برداری Qdrant روی CPU. مجموعه داده: مدل استخراج استدلال قضایی و رأی فارسی.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی مدل استخراج استدلال قضایی و رأی فارسی؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های پایگاه آرای ناشناس پژوهشگاه قوه قضائیه در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: پایگاه آرای ناشناس پژوهشگاه قوه قضائیه. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

bmc.title: ساختار هزینه (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: هزینه کامل مستقل: ۴۰۳٬۹۶۰٬۴۲۹ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA مستقل: ۱۰۷٬۸۳۴٬۵۷۱ تومان/ماه (۲۱٫۱٪). هزینه سبد موتور مشترک (تقسیم توسعه/دفتر بین ۳ ابزار هم‌خانواده): ۳۲۷٬۸۲۰٬۴۲۹ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA سبد: ۱۸۳٬۹۷۴٬۵۷۱ تومان/ماه (۳۵٫۹٪).

hosting_note: میزبانی محلی: استنتاج و داده روی گره‌های GPU داخلی و شبکه ملی اطلاعات می‌ماند. بدون پشتیبان API ابری.
channel_note: کانال کسب‌وکار کوچک: خریدار مغازه، فروشنده خرد، مطب، وکیل مستقل، آژانس کوچک، فریلنسر یا کشاورز است که خودش پول می‌دهد.

gtm: پایگاه آرای ناشناس پژوهشگاه قوه قضائیه
driver: مدل استخراج استدلال قضایی و رأی فارسی
dataset: Persian judicial reasoning & verdict extraction model
stack: Qwen3-14B/32B کوانتیزه (AWQ، مجوز Apache 2.0) با vLLM + امبدینگ فارسی BGE-M3 + پایگاه برداری Qdrant روی CPU
infrastructure: Sindad/Afranet (GPU/NIN), Zarinpal/PayPing (Shaparak gateway), and Vice-Presidency for Science & Technology (Danesh-Bonyan Type 1/2 tax exemption)

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal on these assumptions, and the decisive risk is data, not compute. GPU cost is about 1,965 toman per ruling summarized or searched (about $0.0074) and gross margin is 85–89% [D], but I found no evidence that Iranian court rulings are published in a form this service could collect, so the corpus, its licence and the 400M toman setup are unverified. Revenue per customer is about 955,000 toman a month ($3.60) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 499 paying customers on paper and 655 with the nodes and hires counted [D]. The base case (150 customers at month 12, 700 at month 24) breaks even only in month 24, with a peak cash need of 6,657M toman (about $25,093), +43M a month at month 24 and cumulative cash still −6,614M; the conservative case (50 / 200) never breaks even (−319M a month at month 24, cumulative cash −9,720M, a floor); the optimistic case (400 / 2,000) breaks even in month 14 with a peak cash need of 4,125M and +790M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each removes the base-case break-even. The service also depends on a 30B-class model handling legal Persian, which I could not confirm. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Solo lawyers and small law offices preparing cases — core. (b) Larger firms and in-house legal departments of banks, insurers and contractors that handle many disputes. (c) Law students, judges' assistants and legal researchers. Not targeted: citizens, and courts themselves, which would require government procurement. Pool: more than 70,000 qualified lawyers in Iran (undated) [S, americanbar.org legal-profession-in-iran-steps-toward-specialization, read 25 Oct 2026]. Demand for precedent: the judiciary head said in December 2007 that about eight million cases enter the judicial system a year, plus about four million handled by dispute-resolution councils [S, ncr-iran.org, an opposition group quoting the judiciary head, published 1 Mar 2008; old]. The Supreme Court General Board's uniform-precedent rulings bind all courts [S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme\_Court\_of\_Iran, read 25 Oct 2026], which gives lawyers a reason to search them.

The lawyer searches rulings by facts or legal question in plain Persian and gets a short summary with the court, branch, date, holding and the articles applied, plus a list of similar rulings and the uniform-precedent rulings that bind them. The labour replaced is reading rulings and noting the holding: 25 minutes per ruling or search session [A], about 59,593 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), which understates a lawyer's time; the plans below charge 6,875–10,000 toman per ruling, 12–17% of that [D].

A web tool and browser extension for lawyers; Word and PDF add-ins for firms; partnerships with bar associations, law faculties and legal-education channels; direct sales to in-house legal departments.

Free trial of 5 rulings [A]; every summary links to the source ruling text with the passage highlighted; a feedback button for wrong summaries; one customer-success person per 150 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of rulings: Solo 400,000 toman (40 rulings, about $1.51), Office 1,600,000 (200, about $6.03), Firm 5,500,000 (800, about $20.73) [A, no competitor price was found]. Mix 70% / 25% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 955,000 toman a month (about $3.60) [D].

A ruling corpus with metadata (court, branch, date, topic) — the scarce asset, with no confirmed lawful source; a 30B-class open instruction model with Persian legal tuning; an embedding index; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 legal editor (80M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Collecting and OCR-ing rulings and removing party names and personal data; summarizing and tagging; linking rulings to the statutes and uniform-precedent rulings they cite; evaluating summaries against lawyer-written ones; adding new rulings continuously.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); the judiciary or its legal-information centres and publishers of rulings if a licence is required (terms not verified); law faculties for evaluation.

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure and index 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 471.3M toman a month (about $1,777) [D]; one-time setup 400M [A] (collecting and OCR-ing the corpus, anonymisation, evaluation set). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 150 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 6,000 input (ruling text) plus about 500 output (summary with holding and cited articles); searches are cheaper but counted at the same size

[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 0.30 (a 30B-class model runs about 3.3 times slower than the 8B benchmark, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 50% use [A] of the 40 / 200 / 800 quotas, weighted by plan mix
[D] team 258.3M + GPU 150M + infrastructure and index 15M + accounting 8M + marketing 40M

cost_model.x: One node covers about 1,193 customers at this usage [D: 76,331 ÷ (59.0 + 5 free-trial rulings)], so the base case runs on one node and the optimistic case needs 2 at month 24. Customer-success staffing is the larger variable cost: one hire per 150 customers costs 246,000 toman a month per customer [D: 36.9M ÷ 150], 26% of revenue per customer. OCR of scanned rulings needs GPU or CPU time that I counted only inside the 400M setup and the 15M infrastructure line.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 499 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 471.3M ÷ (955,000 × 0.99) = 498.5], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 655 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 400M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. For scale only, 700 accounts is 1.0% of the 70,000-plus lawyers reported by the American Bar Association [D, S above], although many accounts would be offices of several lawyers. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −9,720M toman in the conservative case, −6,614M in the base case and +76M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 6,657M came just before month 24, and payback is beyond month 24 in the conservative and base cases.

sensitivities.x: The base case has almost no margin for error: month-24 profit is +43M, so any one of the three changes turns it into a loss. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 6% monthly churn [A, a searchable ruling archive is sticky once lawyers rely on it, but a lawyer who finds the corpus thin will leave quickly] lifetime revenue per customer is about 15.8M toman [D: 955,000 × 0.99 ÷ 0.06]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Corpus availability: in principle judgments are delivered in writing to the parties and their lawyers, but Revolutionary Courts often do not provide written copies, and the source I read describes delivery to parties only, not public publication [S, osar.ch report on access to case files, 25 Mar 2019, read 25 Oct 2026; six years old]. A corpus would then have to come from a judiciary licence or from lawyers uploading their own rulings, which raises confidentiality and quality problems. This could make the service impossible regardless of the model.
Personal data: rulings name parties; automatic anonymisation errors are a legal risk; the applicable rules were not found.
Accuracy and liability: a wrong summary of a holding, or a ruling shown as binding when it is not, harms the lawyer's client; I found no benchmark of Persian legal summarization by open models.
Substitutes: lawyers already share rulings in professional channels and the judiciary may offer its own search to lawyers; I could not check either, and a state-run search would undercut any price.

Regulatory standing of the bar: the judiciary controls licensing and the profession is under pressure [S, ibanet.org New-report-No-Defence, 4 Dec 2025, read 25 Oct 2026]; this may slow adoption through bar channels.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: Whether any lawful, machine-readable source of Iranian court rulings exists, how many rulings it holds, and on what licence; the Supreme Court Wikipedia page does not say whether rulings are published.
A current count of practising lawyers and of rulings issued per year (the 8 million cases a year figure dates from 2007 and counts cases, not written rulings).
Prices of Iranian ruling-search tools and lawyer research fees.
Accuracy of any open 30B-class model on Persian court rulings, real tokens per ruling, and throughput on the RTX 6000 Ada node.
Rules on processing and anonymising judgments and on selling access to them.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: مشاوران املاک (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: قراردادهای دست‌نویس مورد اختلاف یا حق‌الزحمه کارشناس حقوقی. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۷۳ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۵۴ پایه، ۹۶ رشد، ۲۳ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۱۱٫۰٪.

bmc.text: جایگزین «قراردادهای دست‌نویس مورد اختلاف یا حق‌الزحمه کارشناس حقوقی» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: قانون الزام به ثبت رسمی معاملات ۲۰۲۶؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق انطباق با کاتب و خط‌سبز به‌همراه ۰٫۴۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۲٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۴۶٬۱۶۷٬۴۱۲ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر قرارداد): پایه ۱٬۷۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۰۹۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۷٬۲۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۳۸۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۱۹٬۷۸۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۹۱٬۸۸۹٬۹۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۲۶ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۳۹٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۱۷٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen3-14B / DeepSeek-V3 Distill کوانتیزه با آداپتورهای LoRA لحن برند فارسی. مجموعه داده: قانون الزام به ثبت رسمی معاملات ۲۰۲۶.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی قانون الزام به ثبت رسمی معاملات ۲۰۲۶؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های انطباق با کاتب و خط‌سبز در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: انطباق با کاتب و خط‌سبز. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

bmc.title: ساختار هزینه (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: هزینه کامل مستقل: ۳۶۲٬۲۱۴٬۸۹۸ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA مستقل: ۲۵۷٬۵۶۵٬۱۰۲ تومان/ماه (۴۱٫۶٪). هزینه سبد موتور مشترک (تقسیم توسعه/دفتر بین ۳ ابزار هم‌خانواده): ۲۹۸٬۶۴۴٬۸۹۸ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA سبد: ۳۲۱٬۱۳۵٬۱۰۲ تومان/ماه (۵۱٫۸٪).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Compute is almost free (about 363 toman per agreement drafted, about $0.0014, gross margin 94–96% [D]), but the price an agency can plausibly pay per agreement is small, so revenue per customer is about 527,500 toman a month ($1.99) against 422.1M toman of fixed cost. Break-even needs about 808 paying customers on paper and 1,162 with a node and hires counted [D], against only 1,771 real-estate-agency companies in one web index [S]. No scenario breaks even in 24 months: the base case (80 customers at month 12, 300 at month 24) loses 302M toman a month at month 24 with cumulative cash −8,565M (about $32,284, a floor), the conservative case (30 / 120) loses 359M a month, and even the optimistic case (200 / 700) loses 167M a month with cumulative cash −7,213M. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base-case loss. Lease registration and the 13-digit tracking code go through the national system and authorised agencies, so the product can draft but not register, and I found no API for it. A much leaner team might change the answer but the model keeps the standard four-person team. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Small real-estate agencies that write rental and sale agreements daily — core. (b) Larger agencies and chains, and property managers. (c) Landlords and developers writing agreements directly. Not targeted: notaries, who issue official deeds. Pool: a web index counts 3,902 real-estate companies in Iran, including 1,771 labelled real-estate agency, 950 commercial brokerage and 701 property management, with overlapping labels, snapshot October 2026 [S, discolike.com/company-stats/real-estate/iran, read 25 Oct 2026]; this counts companies with a web presence only, and the real number of agency offices was not found.

The agent enters parties, property and money terms in a form, voice note or chat and gets a complete Persian rental or sale agreement with the clauses the law needs: two copies, two witnesses, exact start and end dates, rent and deposit written in words and numerals, identity and deed details [S, landager.com/en/property-compliance/iran/national/lease-requirements, page updated 10 Apr 2026, read 25 Oct 2026]; the tool flags missing fields and amount mismatches. The labour replaced is filling and checking a template: 30 minutes [A], about 71,512 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 5,000–8,333 toman per agreement, 7–12% of that [D].
Web app and Telegram/Bale/Eitaa bot for agents; integrations with agency software and listing sites; agent associations and guild unions; direct visits to agencies.

Free trial of 3 agreements [A]; saved clause libraries and party records; a lawyer-reviewed clause set; one customer-success person per 200 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of agreements: Small office 250,000 toman (30 agreements, about $0.94), Office 800,000 (120, about $3.02), Chain 2,500,000 (500, about $9.42) [A, no competitor price was found]. Mix 65% / 30% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 527,500 toman a month (about $1.99) [D].

A reviewed library of rental, sale and addendum templates with clause options; an 8B-class open model for filling and checking, with rules for amounts and dates; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]), much larger than the load needs; 2 engineers, a part-time lawyer on retainer (40M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Maintaining templates against the 1997 landlord-tenant law, the 2024 rent-market law and local rent caps; field validation (national ID, postal code, amounts in words); export to print and PDF; handing the agent the data needed to register the agreement.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); agent associations; the operator of the national registration system if an integration exists (not found).

Fixed: team 209.1M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 part-time lawyer at 40M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 422.1M toman a month (about $1,591) [D]; one-time setup 120M [A] (templates and legal review). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 200 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 part-time lawyer at 40M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 2,500 input (template, fields, clause options) plus about 1,500 output (full Persian text)

[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]; no 30B factor because an 8B model fills a template [A]
[D] 70% use [A] of the 30 / 120 / 500 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 6,966 customers at this usage [D: 413,461 ÷ (56.4 + 3 free-trial agreements)], so one node is enough in every scenario and 150M toman a month is 36% of fixed cost for a load a small server could carry; a cheaper GPU or CPU plan would lower the cost, which I did not model. The fixed team and marketing, not compute, decide the result.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 808 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 422.1M ÷ (527,500 × 0.99) = 808.3], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 1,162 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 120M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. For scale only, 300 accounts is 17% of the 1,771 agency companies in the web index [D, S above], 700 is 40% and the break-even 1,162 is 66%, although the index misses offices without a web presence and some accounts would be one-person offices. In every case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −9,229M toman in the conservative case, −8,565M in the base case and −7,213M in the optimistic case [D]; payback is beyond month 24 in all three.

sensitivities.x: No single change rescues the base case. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 4% monthly churn [A, saved clause libraries and party records raise switching cost, but agents can fall back on paper or word-processor templates] lifetime revenue per customer is about 13.1M toman [D: 527,500 × 0.99 ÷ 0.04]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Registration is outside the product: a lease is registered through the national real-estate registration system by authorised agencies, which issue a hologram document and a 13-digit tracking code; without the code, suits and dispute-council notices are not possible [S, landager.com lease-requirements page, updated 10 Apr 2026, read 25 Oct 2026]. If the agent must re-key the data into that portal, the time saved is smaller than assumed; no public API was found.

Legal validity: an agreement missing one witness signature or exact dates can lose fast-track eviction or be void [S, same page]; a template error is the vendor's reputational risk and needs lawyer review, which the model covers only with a part-time retainer.

Law changes: the page lists a 2024 law on the land, housing and rent market and rent caps for 2024–2025, with 25% for Tehran [S, landager.com national overview, updated 9 May 2026, read 25 Oct 2026]; earlier checks of this source found inconsistent cap figures, so templates must be reviewed against the official text.

Substitutes: agencies already use paper or word-processor templates and the registration portal itself; a search title reports that a new self-service (Khodnevis) system replaced the earlier Iran Amlak system for lease registration, which may reduce the need for a separate drafting tool (title only; the page was blocked).
Price level: the value of 5,000–8,333 toman per agreement against an agency commission could not be compared; the commission rate and a competitor price were not found.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of real-estate agency offices in Iran (the index counts companies with a web presence only) and agreements written per office per month.
Agency commission rates and fees for drafting or registering an agreement (the one search hit, a 2020 headline on halved commissions, was blocked).
Whether the national registration system offers an API or accepts third-party data entry, and whether the Khodnevis system produces the agreement text itself.
Competitor prices for agreement generators in Iran.
Licence terms for template text and rules on non-lawyers drafting contracts.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: استارتاپ‌ها و مشاوران (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: حق‌الزحمه دلال ثبت شرکت (۸ تا ۲۵ میلیون تومان). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۵۶ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۶۳ پایه، ۶۵ رشد، ۲۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۸٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal at best, and weak in the base case. A guidance case costs about 9,070 toman of GPU time (about $0.034) and gross margin is 96–97% [D], but most customers would be founders who need one case and leave, so the customer path is mostly new buyers each month. Revenue per customer is about 1.30M toman a month ($4.89) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 367 paying customers on paper and 396 with the node and hires counted [D]. The base case (100 customers at month 12, 400 at month 24) does not break even within 24 months (−31M toman a month at month 24, cumulative cash −6,742M, about $25,412, a floor); the conservative case (40 / 150) loses 279M a month; the optimistic case (250 / 1,000) breaks even in month 15, with a peak cash need of 4,007M and +629M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base-case loss. The base case needs about 13% of the roughly 3,000 new limited companies registered each month, a ratio based on a single 2020 count [D]. Accuracy of guidance on Iranian licensing was not tested, and no domestic consultant fee was found. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Founders and startups forming an LLC or sole proprietorship and finding the licences they need — core by number, one case each. (b) Business-formation consultants, accountants and lawyers who handle many cases. (c) Agencies and incubators that onboard many founders. Not targeted: foreign investors, whose registration involves extra steps and consultants. Pool: 36,158 new limited liability corporations (or equivalent) were registered in 2020, 0.627 per 1,000 people aged 15 to 64, formal sector only [S, ceicdata.com/en/iran/businesses-registered-statistics citing the World Bank Entrepreneurship Database, read 25 Oct 2026; single year, five years old], which is about 3,013 a month [D]. No count of consultants who handle registrations was found.

The founder describes the business in plain Persian and gets the entity type options, the licences and approvals the activity needs, the documents to prepare, the order of steps and the expected fees and timeline, with the source rule for each step and a checklist; consultants get case tracking and templates. The labour replaced is working this out with a consultant or by visiting offices: two hours of guidance work [A], about 286,046 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), which understates a consultant's time; the plans below charge 250,000–450,000 toman per case, 87–157% of that [D]. For foreigners, a consultancy quotes an average of €26,140 and 22 weeks for an LLC including bank accounts and government fees [S, healyconsultants.com/iran-company-registration/fees-timelines, read 25 Oct 2026]; this is a foreign-investor price, not a domestic one.

Web app and a Telegram/Bale/Eitaa bot for founders; search content on licences; partnerships with startup incubators, accelerators, accounting firms and co-working spaces; a consultant plan for firms that handle many cases.

One free case [A]; every step cites the rule or agency; a checklist that updates when rules change; an option to hand the case to a human consultant (not modelled); one customer-success person per 200 customers [A]. Plans billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of cases: Founder 450,000 toman for 1 case (about $1.70), Consultant 3,000,000 for 10 (about $11.31), Agency 10,000,000 for 40 (about $37.69) [A, no domestic competitor price was found]. Mix 75% / 22% / 3% [A] gives ARPU 1,297,500 toman a month (about $4.89) [D].

A curated rule base for registration and licences (Companies Registration Office, tax, guild and sectoral licences), updated as rules change; a 30B-class open instruction model with Persian capability; a retrieval index; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 legal editor (80M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.
Mapping activities to licences and issuing bodies; keeping fees, forms and timelines current; testing guidance against real registrations; routing edge cases to humans.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); registration consultants and lawyers for hand-off; incubators and accountants as channels.

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 471.3M toman a month (about $1,777) [D]; one-time setup 200M [A] (rule base and test cases). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 200 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 20 chat turns: about 26,000 input (rules, forms, chat context) plus about 4,000 output

[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 0.30 (a 30B-class model runs about 3.3 times slower than the 8B benchmark, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 90% use [A] of the 1 / 10 / 40 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 3,493 customers at this usage [D: 16,538 ÷ (3.7 + 1 free-trial case)], so one node is enough in every scenario and compute is not the constraint; the fixed team and marketing are. A 30B-class model may not fit one 48 GB card at the batch sizes assumed, and I did not test it.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 367 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 471.3M ÷ (1,297,500 × 0.99) = 366.9], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 396 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 200M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A] and mean customers buying in a given month. For scale only, 400 customers a month is 13% of the roughly 3,013 new limited companies a month implied by the 2020 count [D, S above], and 1,000 is 33%; the 2020 figure is five years old and excludes sole proprietors and licences added to existing firms. In the conservative and base cases cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −9,269M toman in the conservative case, −6,742M in the base case and −668M in the optimistic case [D]; the optimistic trough of 4,007M came earlier, and payback in that case is just beyond month 24.

sensitivities.x: The base case is close to break-even at month 24 (−31M), so modest gains in price or customers could flip it, but each sensitivity shows a deeper loss. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 25% monthly churn [A, a founder needs one registration and leaves; consultants stay] lifetime revenue per customer is about 5.1M toman [D: 1,297,500 × 0.99 ÷ 0.25], so the customer count in each month depends on constant new acquisition. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Guidance accuracy: a wrong licence list or fee can delay a business or cost money; I found no benchmark of how reliably an open model answers Iranian registration and licensing questions, and rules change often.
Rule base ownership: the guidance depends on a hand-maintained map of activities to licences and issuing bodies; the one legal editor in the model may not keep up with sector-specific licences.

One-case customers: founders form a company once, so acquisition cost repeats for each case and the assumed price (450,000 toman) is untested; consultants who handle many cases are fewer and I found no count.
Substitutes: consultants and lawyers who register companies, and official portals with their own instructions; I found no domestic fee for them, only a foreign-investor quote.
Official systems: registration and licensing are handled by government offices and portals; I did not confirm what they publish or whether the product could submit anything on the founder's behalf.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: A current count of company registrations, sole-proprietor registrations and licence applications (only the 2020 World Bank figure, via CEIC, was found).
Domestic fees of consultants and lawyers for company registration and licensing, and official government fees.
The list of licences by activity and which agencies issue them, and whether any official API or data feed exists.
Accuracy of any open 30B-class model on Iranian registration rules, real tokens per case, and throughput on the RTX 6000 Ada node.
Rules on non-lawyers giving registration advice.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

title: تحلیلگر اسناد مناقصه و نویسنده پیشنهاد
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۱: گفتگوی فارسی و بازیابی ترکیبی (RAG)

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: پیمانکاران و تأمین‌کنندگان (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: کارشناس مناقصه (۳۵ میلیون تومان در ماه) و ضمانت‌نامه‌های ازدست‌رفته. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۸۳ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۷۹ پایه، ۸۵ رشد، ۱۹ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۸٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «کارشناس مناقصه (۳۵ میلیون تومان در ماه) و ضمانت‌نامه‌های ازدست‌رفته» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: چک‌لیست خودکار پاکت فنی/مالی و سازنده پیشنهاد؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق ستاد ایران، تدبیر و پورتال‌های نفت و گاز به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۴٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۵۰٬۶۷۶٬۰۴۳ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۱۳ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر مناقصه): پایه ۱٬۵۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۳۱۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۵٬۲۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۴۴۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۸۳٬۱۲۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۵۶٬۸۷۹٬۶۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۴۱ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۶۱٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۰٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen3-14B/32B کوانتیزه (AWQ، مجوز Apache 2.0) با vLLM + امبدینگ فارسی BGE-M3 + پایگاه برداری Qdrant روی CPU. مجموعه داده: چک‌لیست خودکار پاکت فنی/مالی و سازنده پیشنهاد.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی چک‌لیست خودکار پاکت فنی/مالی و سازنده پیشنهاد؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های ستاد ایران، تدبیر و پورتال‌های نفت و گاز در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: ستاد ایران، تدبیر و پورتال‌های نفت و گاز. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable but thin on these assumptions, and the case rests on a customer count I could not source. A tender reading is long (about 130,000 tokens), so GPU cost is about 39,302 toman per tender (about $0.148) and gross margin is 86–90% [D]; the plans charge 216,667–300,000 toman per tender against about 1.14M toman of reading time at the minimum wage [D]. Revenue per customer is about 3.46M toman a month ($13.04) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 138 paying customers on paper and 149 with the node and hires counted [D]. The base case (100 customers at month 12, 350 at month 24) breaks even in month 15, with a peak cash need of 3,897M toman (about $14,689), +617M a month at month 24 and cumulative cash −607M; the conservative case (30 / 120) does not break even (−97M a month, cumulative cash −7,471M, a floor); the optimistic case (250 / 800) breaks even in month 9 with +1,674M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price delays break-even to month 17, cutting prices 30% to month 19 and halving customers to month 22. The base case needs customers equal to 24% of the 1,439 construction companies in one data vendor's list, so the demand side is the weak point; tender data in Iran was rated not open in 2015, and I could not verify how a vendor would obtain tender documents. A 30B-class model must also read long Persian technical documents reliably, which I could not confirm. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Mid-size contractors and consultancies that bid on public and private tenders — core. (b) Suppliers and equipment vendors answering procurement requests. (c) Bid consultants who prepare proposals for others. Not targeted: the issuing bodies themselves. Pool: a data vendor lists 1,439 construction companies in Iran, undated, with no size breakdown [S, coresignal.com/discover/construction/iran, read 25 Oct 2026]; suppliers and consultancies are not counted there, and the real number of firms that bid regularly was not found. Qualified-company lists can be small in some sectors: the oil ministry's updated list of exploration and production companies had 27 licensed companies and partnerships, with 6 of 22 applicants approved in the latest round [S, en.shana.ir/news/1593005, 10 Feb 2026, read 25 Oct 2026].

The user uploads the tender documents and gets a requirement and eligibility checklist (qualification, guarantees, deadlines, evaluation criteria), a risk list of unusual clauses, a gap list against the firm's own profile, and a proposal draft with the technical and commercial sections filled from the firm's past projects. The labour replaced is reading and building the checklist: 8 hours [A], about 1,144,184 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), which understates a bid manager's time; the plans below charge 216,667–300,000 toman per tender, 19–26% of that [D].
Web app with PDF and Word upload; partnerships with contractor associations, chambers of commerce and engineering-licence bodies; direct sales to bid managers; content on tender checklists.

One free tender analysis [A]; every checklist item links to the page and clause it came from; a library of the firm's past projects and standard forms; one customer-success person per 100 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of tenders: Starter 1,500,000 toman (5 tenders, about $5.65), Contractor 5,000,000 (20, about $18.85), Firm 13,000,000 (60, about $49.00) [A, no competitor price was found]. Mix 60% / 33% / 7% [A] gives ARPU 3,460,000 toman a month (about $13.04) [D].

A 30B-class open instruction model with strong Persian long-document handling; a document parser for scanned PDFs and tables; a library of standard tender forms and qualification rules; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 procurement editor (80M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Parsing and OCR of tender documents; extracting requirements and checking them against the firm's profile; drafting proposal sections; keeping templates current with procurement rules; evaluating accuracy on past tenders.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); contractor associations; tender-notice publishers if a feed is licensed (terms not verified).

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 procurement editor at 80M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 471.3M toman a month (about $1,777) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (parsers, templates, evaluation set). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 100 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 procurement editor at 80M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 120,000 input (about 150 pages of Persian conditions, specifications and forms, read in chunks) plus about 10,000 output (checklist, risks, proposal draft)

[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 0.30 (a 30B-class model runs about 3.3 times slower than the 8B benchmark, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 70% use [A] of the 5 / 20 / 60 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 358 customers at this usage [D: 3,817 ÷ (9.7 + 1 free-trial tender)], so GPU nodes step up with customers: 1 node in the base case through month 24 and 3 in the optimistic case at month 24 [D]. Customer-success staffing at one hire per 100 customers costs 369,000 toman a month per customer [D: 36.9M ÷ 100], 11% of revenue per customer. A 30B-class model may not fit one 48 GB card at long context with the batch sizes assumed, and I did not test it; scanned tender PDFs also need OCR that I counted only in the setup and infrastructure lines.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 138 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 471.3M ÷ (3,460,000 × 0.99) = 137.6], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 149 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. For scale only, the break-even 149 customers is 10% of the 1,439 construction companies in the vendor list, the base case's 350 is 24% and the optimistic 800 is 56% [D, S above]; the list is undated and excludes suppliers and consultancies, so these ratios are loose. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −7,471M toman in the conservative case, −607M in the base case and +11,383M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 3,897M came earlier, and base-case payback falls just after month 24.

sensitivities.x: The base case survives each change but with a smaller margin; halving customers leaves only +91M a month at month 24 and cumulative cash far below zero. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 8% monthly churn [A, a firm that finds the checklists accurate keeps using them for every tender, but bidding is seasonal and some firms win few tenders] lifetime revenue per customer is about 42.8M toman [D: 3,460,000 × 0.99 ÷ 0.08]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Access to tender documents: in 2015 Iran's government procurement data was rated 0% open, with no common tender platform found, not machine-readable and not openly licensed [S, 2015.index.okfn.org/place/iran/procurement, read 25 Oct 2026; ten years old]. The product works on documents the customer uploads, so it avoids needing a feed, but it cannot find tenders for the customer; whether issuers charge for or restrict document copies was not confirmed.

Accuracy: a missed qualification condition or guarantee amount can disqualify a bid; I found no benchmark of open models on long Persian technical and legal documents, and tables and scans make extraction harder.
Demand: tenders are won on price, relationships and qualification more than on document reading, and a firm may already have bid managers; the 216,667–300,000 toman a tender price is untested.
Confidentiality: tender documents of some private and defence-related buyers are restricted; customers may refuse upload to a third party unless hosting is domestic.

Sector concentration: qualified-company lists can be small, as in the oil ministry's list of 27 [S, en.shana.ir/news/1593005, 10 Feb 2026, read 25 Oct 2026], so some sectors have few potential customers.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of firms that bid on tenders regularly, by sector and size, and the number of tenders issued per year (the vendor count of 1,439 construction companies is undated).
Prices of Iranian bid-preparation services and tender-notice subscriptions (a foreign tender-notice vendor page listed no prices).
Whether issuers sell, restrict or standardise tender documents, and the typical length of a tender document in pages and tokens.
Accuracy of any open 30B-class model on long Persian tender documents, real tokens per tender, and throughput on the RTX 6000 Ada node.
Procurement rules that require a specific format or local-content declarations.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

title: نویسنده درخواست دانش‌بنیان و دریافت گرنت
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۵A: تولید محتوای فارسی و نگارش بازاریابی/آکادمیک

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: استارتاپ‌ها (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: مشاور دانش‌بنیان (۳۰ تا ۸۰ میلیون تومان به‌همراه درصد). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۹۱ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۸۱ پایه، ۸۷ رشد، ۲۳ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۱۱٫۰٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «مشاور دانش‌بنیان (۳۰ تا ۸۰ میلیون تومان به‌همراه درصد)» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: معیارهای ارزیابی معاونت علمی (سطح ۱، ۲، ۳) و اسناد دفاع R&D؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق داشبورد دانش‌بنیان و صندوق نوآوری به‌همراه ۰٫۴۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۲٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۴۷٬۰۰۲٬۰۷۲ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۰۴ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر درخواست): پایه ۱٬۴۷۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۴۲۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۵٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۴۷۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۳۰٬۹۸۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۶۰۲٬۵۹۰٬۶۷۵ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۲۹ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۴۳٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۱۷٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen3-14B / DeepSeek-V3 Distill کوانتیزه با آداپتورهای LoRA لحن برند فارسی. مجموعه داده: معیارهای ارزیابی معاونت علمی (سطح ۱، ۲، ۳) و اسناد دفاع R&D.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی معیارهای ارزیابی معاونت علمی (سطح ۱، ۲، ۳) و اسناد دفاع R&D؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های داشبورد دانش‌بنیان و صندوق نوآوری در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: داشبورد دانش‌بنیان و صندوق نوآوری. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal on these assumptions. An application draft costs about 14,512 toman of GPU time (about $0.055) and gross margin is 97% [D], and the plans charge 560,000–900,000 toman per application against about 2.29M toman of writing time at the minimum wage [D]. Revenue per customer is about 2.55M toman a month ($9.59) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 187 paying customers on paper and 202 with the node and hires counted [D]. The base case (80 customers at month 12, 300 at month 24) breaks even in month 19, with a peak cash need of 5,157M toman (about $19,438), +211M a month at month 24 and cumulative cash still −4,401M; the conservative case (25 / 100) does not break even (−219M a month, cumulative cash −8,762M, a floor); the optimistic case (200 / 700) breaks even in month 13 with +1,145M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price delays break-even to month 22, while cutting prices 30% or halving customers removes it. The customer base is a pool of about 7,882 knowledge-based companies counted in the Iranian year 1401 (2022–23) [S], of which about 2,000 lost their status in re-evaluations, so repeat applicants are fewer than the headline. I did not find the evaluation criteria, the fees or the programmes that fund applications, and the programme rules that drive demand change often. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Startups and technology firms applying for knowledge-based status, grants, loans or incubator places — core. (b) Consultants and incubators that prepare applications for many firms. (c) Existing knowledge-based firms re-evaluated for renewal. Not targeted: large state-backed firms with in-house teams. Pool: 7,882 knowledge-based companies in the Iranian year ending March 2023, 2.5 times the previous year, with about 2,000 firms losing approval in re-evaluations [S, tehrantimes.com/news/480196, undated, read 25 Oct 2026]; the sector's economic weight was put at over 9 quadrillion rials (about $34 billion in the source) in that year, and knowledge-based exports at about $500 million in the Iranian year 1403 (March 2024 to March 2025) [S, aziendeaccordi.ice.it news 283819 citing Iran Daily, 6 May 2025, read 25 Oct 2026]. No count of applications per year or of startups preparing to apply was found.

The user answers a structured interview and uploads company documents, and gets a first draft of the application: technical description, innovation claims, market and team sections, work plan, budget and the supporting-document checklist, formatted for the programme chosen; the tool flags missing evidence and compares claims with the programme's published criteria. The labour replaced is reading the rules and writing the draft: 16 hours [A], about 2,288,369 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), which understates a consultant's time; the plans below charge 560,000–900,000 toman per application, 25–39% of that [D].

Web app and Telegram/Bale/Eitaa bot; partnerships with science-and-technology parks, incubators, accelerators and university entrepreneurship centres; content on application checklists; direct sales to grant consultants.

One free application draft [A]; every claim links to the criterion it answers; a library of the firm's earlier texts for reuse in later applications; one customer-success person per 150 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of applications: Startup 900,000 toman for 1 application (about $3.39), Consultant 4,200,000 for 6 (about $15.83), Incubator 14,000,000 for 25 (about $52.77) [A, no competitor price was found]. Mix 65% / 30% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 2,545,000 toman a month (about $9.59) [D].

A current library of programme rules, forms and evaluation criteria (assembled by hand, licence not applicable if public); a 30B-class open instruction model with Persian capability; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 grants editor (80M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Tracking programmes and calls and updating rule sets; interviewing the applicant and drafting; checking drafts against criteria; keeping a library of approved wording; evaluating drafts against accepted applications where available.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); science-and-technology parks, incubators and grant consultants as channels and reviewers.

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 grants editor at 80M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 471.3M toman a month (about $1,777) [D]; one-time setup 200M [A] (rule library and test applications). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 150 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 grants editor at 80M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 40,000 input (guideline text, company documents, earlier drafts) plus about 8,000 output (forms, technical description, budget text)

[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 0.30 (a 30B-class model runs about 3.3 times slower than the 8B benchmark, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 90% use [A] of the 1 / 6 / 25 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 2,387 customers at this usage [D: 10,337 ÷ (3.3 + 1 free-trial application)], so one node is enough in every scenario and compute is not the constraint. Customer-success staffing at one hire per 150 customers costs 246,000 toman a month per customer [D: 36.9M ÷ 150], 10% of revenue per customer. A 30B-class model may not fit one 48 GB card at long context with the batch sizes assumed, and I did not test it.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 187 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 471.3M ÷ (2,545,000 × 0.99) = 187.1], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 202 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 200M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. For scale only, 300 customers is 3.8% of the 7,882 knowledge-based companies counted in 2022–23 [D, S above], although customers would include startups not yet approved and consultants serving many firms. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −8,762M toman in the conservative case, −4,401M in the base case and +4,402M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 5,157M came earlier, and base-case payback is beyond month 24.

sensitivities.x: A price cut or a loss of half the customers removes break-even; the margin is thin because 471.3M of fixed cost has to be covered by a low price per application. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 20% monthly churn [A, most startups apply once or twice a year and a programme call may close, so customers lapse quickly] lifetime revenue per customer is about 12.6M toman [D: 2,545,000 × 0.99 ÷ 0.20], so the customer count in each month depends on constant new acquisition. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Programme rules change: the knowledge-based status was re-evaluated in 2022–23 and about 2,000 firms lost approval [S, tehrantimes.com/news/480196]; criteria, benefits and funding calls change with policy, and I found no source for the current criteria or application fees.
Seasonal and episodic demand: applications cluster around calls and renewals, so monthly usage may be lumpy and the 90% quota use assumed may be too high.
Outcome pressure: the customer pays for an approval, not a draft; a rejected application causes churn and complaints even when the draft was correct, and I found no acceptance rates.
Substitutes: consultants and incubators already write applications for a fee, and science-and-technology parks offer help to their tenants; no price was found.
Confidentiality of business plans: customers may refuse upload of technology details unless hosting is domestic.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of applications per year for knowledge-based status, grants and loans, and acceptance rates (the 7,882 count is undated and from 2022–23).
Current evaluation criteria, fees and benefits of knowledge-based status (the one page read gave none), and the funding programmes and their application formats.
Prices of consultants who write applications in Iran.
Accuracy of any open 30B-class model on Persian grant writing, real tokens per application, and throughput on the RTX 6000 Ada node.
Rules on handling business plans submitted to a third party.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.
