support_scope: human-in-the-loop edge cases and SAYAD/Shaparak billing follow-ups

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. A site scan costs about 4,535 toman of GPU time (about $0.017) and gross margin is 87–93% [D], and the plans charge 31,250–62,500 toman per scan against about 429,000 toman of consultant time at the minimum wage [D]. But revenue per customer is only about 450,000 toman a month ($1.70) against 412.1M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 925 paying customers on paper and 1,505 with the node and hires counted [D]. The base case (500 customers at month 12, 2,000 at month 24) breaks even in month 21, with a peak cash need of 4,776M toman (about $18,002), +110M a month at month 24 and cumulative cash still −4,486M; the conservative case (150 / 600) does not break even (−256M a month, cumulative cash −7,815M); the optimistic case (1,200 / 5,000) breaks even in month 13 with +743M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each remove break-even, and the base case needs 2,000 customers, about 3% of the 66,000 websites detected with the trust-symbol badge [S]. I found no rule that makes a scan mandatory, no price for a human compliance review, and no count of shops that actually fail the rules. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Small online shops that want or must renew the electronic trust symbol (e-Namad) and need their site pages to match consumer and e-commerce rules — core. (b) Web agencies and shop-platform resellers that launch many shops. (c) Marketplace sellers with their own sites. Not targeted: large marketplaces with in-house legal teams. Pool: Wappalyzer tracks 66,000 websites using eNamad [S, wappalyzer.com/technologies/miscellaneous/enamad, undated, read 25 Oct 2026]; Donya-e Eqtesad, as reported by Intellinews on 13 Nov 2023, said more than 39,000 online shops obtained the e-Namad certificate in the first half of the Iranian year 1402 (21 Mar to 22 Sep 2023), up 25% on the same period a year earlier [S, intellinews.com/iran-registers-75-rise-in-e-commerce-transactions-301031, read 25 Oct 2026]. The two figures measure different things (sites detected versus certificates in a half year) and I did not reconcile them.

The shop owner enters a site address; the tool reads the main pages (home, product, cart, policies, contact, footer) and returns a checklist of what is missing or wrong against a rule set — seller identity and licence details, trust-symbol display, price and stock clarity, return and delivery terms, privacy and data-consent wording, advertising claims — with suggested replacement text in Persian, and re-checks monthly. The labour replaced is a consultant reading the site against the rules: 3 hours [A], about 429,069 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), which understates a legal consultant's rate; the plans below charge 31,250–62,500 toman per scan, 7–15% of that [D].

Web app with a free first scan; content on trust-symbol renewal checklists; integrations or referral deals with shop-builder platforms, hosting companies and web agencies; direct sales to agencies through the Agency plan.

One free scan [A]; every finding cites the rule it comes from and shows the page location; monthly re-scan emails; one customer-success person per 200 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of scans: Shop 250,000 toman for 4 scans (about $0.94), Pro 600,000 for 15 (about $2.26), Agency 2,500,000 for 80 (about $9.42) [A, no competitor price was found]. Mix 70% / 25% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 450,000 toman a month (about $1.70) [D].

A rule set built from the E-Commerce Act, the consumer-protection rules and the trust-symbol conditions, kept by a part-time legal editor (assembled by hand; texts are public law, but the current trust-symbol checklist was not read); a crawler on a CPU server (inside other infrastructure); an 8B-class open instruction model with Persian capability on a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 legal editor (40M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Crawling and cleaning pages; checking pages against the rule set with the model and fixed rules; maintaining the rule set when regulations or the trust-symbol conditions change; generating replacement wording; monthly re-scans; sending alerts when a page changes.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); web agencies, shop builders and hosting firms as channels; a lawyer for periodic review of the rule set.

Fixed: team 209.1M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 40M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 15M (crawler server), accounting 8M, marketing 30M = 412.1M toman a month (about $1,553) [D]; one-time setup 120M [A] (rule set and test sites). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 200 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 40M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 45,000 input (about 15 pages at about 3,000 tokens each) plus about 5,000 output (findings and replacement wording)
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 80% use [A] of the 4 / 15 / 80 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 3,504 customers at this usage [D: 33,077 ÷ (8.4 + 1 free-trial scan)], so one node is enough in the conservative and base cases and the optimistic case needs a second node at month 24. Customer-success staffing at one hire per 200 customers costs 184,500 toman a month per customer [D: 36.9M ÷ 200], 41% of revenue per customer, which is the largest cost per customer after the node. Crawling cost (bandwidth, headless browsers, blocked requests) is only the 15M toman a month of infrastructure [A] and was not measured.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 925 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 412.1M ÷ (450,000 × 0.99) = 925.0], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 1,505 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 120M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. For scale only, 2,000 customers is 3.0% of the 66,000 websites detected with the trust-symbol badge [D, S above], and the optimistic 5,000 is 7.6% [D]; the pool is undated and not all of those sites would want a paid checker. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −7,815M toman in the conservative case, −4,486M in the base case and +1,744M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 4,776M came earlier, and base-case payback is beyond month 24.

sensitivities.x: Every stress removes break-even because the base case earns only +110M a month at month 24 on 2,000 customers; the low price per customer (about $1.70) means the fixed cost is covered only at high counts. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 6% monthly churn [A, small shops cancel when a renewal passes] lifetime revenue per customer is about 7.4M toman [D: 450,000 × 0.99 ÷ 0.06], so holding 2,000 customers needs about 120 new customers a month [D: 2,000 × 0.06]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Demand is not forced by a rule I could find: the E-Commerce Act sets duties on consumer information, advertising and personal data (Articles 59 and 67–77), but the one law summary read gave no penalty amounts [S, mondaq.com e-commerce-law-and-cybersecurity-in-iran, 10 Mar 2023], so shops may not pay unless a licence or renewal depends on it.

Rule and trust-symbol conditions change: the trust symbol is issued through enamad.ir with the business licence under a regulation dated 19 Feb 2017 [S, legalmondo.com/?p=4773, 5 Dec 2017], and the current checklist was not read; a stale rule set produces wrong findings.
Liability for wrong findings: a "compliant" result that proves wrong can be blamed on the tool; the service must be worded as guidance and not legal advice.

Shops without websites: many micro-sellers trade on Instagram or messaging apps, which the crawler cannot scan the same way, so the pool of 66,000 sites overstates reach for social sellers (one search headline asks whether an Instagram page can get the symbol; title only).
Substitutes: web agencies, the issuer's own review and free checklists; no price was found.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: Current trust-symbol conditions, fees and renewal rules (zarinpal.com, zoomit.ir and digikala.com/mag pages are blocked from fetching; search returned titles only).
Any count of shops that fail the rules, and whether the 66,000 and 39,000 figures can be reconciled.
Fine amounts and enforcement practice under the E-Commerce Act and consumer-protection rules.
Price of a human compliance review or of agency checklists in Iran.
Accuracy of an 8B-class open model on Persian legal checklists, real tokens per scan, and crawler cost.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

title: دسته‌بندی اسناد و جست‌وجوی آرشیو برای ادارات
segment: سازمانی، صنعتی و نهادی B2B
engine: موتور ۲: استخراج اسناد، بینایی و OCR فارسی

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: مؤسسات حقوقی و شهرداری‌ها (سازمانی، صنعتی و نهادی B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: کارمندان بایگانی (۲۰ میلیون تومان در ماه) و پرونده‌های کاغذی مفقود. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۳۶ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۱۳ پایه، ۱۶ رشد، ۷ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۴٫۰٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «کارمندان بایگانی (۲۰ میلیون تومان در ماه) و پرونده‌های کاغذی مفقود» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: OCR فارسی و دسته‌بند تاکسونومی اداری؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق فراغستر، NAS محلی و گردش‌کار اسکنر به‌همراه ۰٫۸۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۸٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۶۸٬۹۷۹٬۰۱۷ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۰٫۹۱ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (پروژه‌ای): پایه ۷٬۷۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۱۶٬۳۰۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۲۸٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۱٬۹۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۳۰٬۵۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۶٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۸۹٬۵۶۴٬۲۵۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۴۰ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۶۰٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۱۶٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B تنظیم‌شده + PaddleOCR فارسی + پردازشگر پسین سفارشی جلالی/ارقام روی GPU داخلی. مجموعه داده: OCR فارسی و دسته‌بند تاکسونومی اداری.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی OCR فارسی و دسته‌بند تاکسونومی اداری؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های فراغستر، NAS محلی و گردش‌کار اسکنر در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers but thin against compute cost and dependent on slow buyers. A four-page document costs about 1,827 toman of GPU time plus 222 toman of spot-checking and storage, 2,049 toman in all (about $0.0077) [D], and the plans charge 3,250–4,000 toman per document against about 14,302 toman of clerk time at the minimum wage [D]; gross margin is 55–63% [D], lower than a text-only service because Persian scan reading runs on a vision model. Revenue per customer is about 19.6M toman a month ($74) against 461.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 25 paying customers on paper and 33 with the nodes and hires counted [D]. The base case (40 customers at month 12, 150 at month 24) breaks even in month 11, with a peak cash need of 2,542M toman (about $9,583) and +1,161M a month at month 24; the conservative case (15 / 60) breaks even in month 17 with a peak cash need of 4,411M and +165M at month 24; the optimistic case (100 / 350) breaks even in month 6 with +3,186M. Doubling the GPU price removes break-even (−39M a month at month 24), while a 30% price cut delays it to month 16 and halving customers to month 15. Two cautions. First, my first draft of the prices (1,125–1,667 toman per document) gave negative gross margin on the two larger plans and every scenario lost money; I reset the prices to about 23–28% of the clerk's cost because compute cost per document requires it, so the result depends on buyers accepting that price, for which I found no competitor price. Second, municipalities and state bodies buy by procurement and may be limited to approved suppliers and domestic hosting, so the linear customer ramp is optimistic for those accounts. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Law firms and legal departments with large paper and PDF archives — core. (b) Offices and institutes (contractors, consultancies, associations, universities) with correspondence and contract archives. (c) Municipalities and large enterprises that hold decades of letters and plans. Not targeted: state bodies that require a certified office-automation supplier, which would be a separate procurement project. Pool: Iran had 1,245 cities as of March 2016 [S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative\_divisions\_of\_Iran citing the Statistical Centre of Iran Geo 94 report, read 25 Oct 2026] and 2,589 rural districts (dehestans) as of 2026 [S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehestan\_(administrative\_division), read 25 Oct 2026]; each city has a municipality, but I found no count of municipalities, only of cities. Lawyers: more than 70,000 are cited in #31 [S, undated]. No count of offices with paper archives was found.

The office uploads scans, photos and PDFs; the tool reads the text, classifies each document (letter, contract, invoice, court paper, plan), extracts metadata (date, parties, reference number, subject), proposes a folder and filing name, and makes the whole archive searchable in Persian by meaning and by exact words, with the original page linked to every hit. The labour replaced is a clerk reading and filing each document: 6 minutes [A], about 14,302 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 3,250–4,000 toman per document, 23–28% of that [D]. Physical scanning is not included and costs far more than the software: a US source gives $0.05–$0.25 per page for scanning plus $0.01–$0.15 for OCR indexing [S, selector.kurlon.com cost-to-digitize-documents-2026, undated, US bids], so a four-page document is about $0.24–$1.60 at those rates [D], not an Iranian price.

Direct sales to law firms and bar-related bodies; partnerships with scanning and archiving contractors, who bring the paper to the software; pilots with a municipality or a university library; content on filing and retrieval.

A free pilot on 200 documents [A]; a named onboarding person per account during the backlog load; every search hit links to the page image so staff can verify; one customer-success person per 40 customers [A] (onboarding is heavy). Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate, with a project fee waived [A].

Monthly by document quota: Law firm 6,000,000 toman for 1,500 documents (about $22.62), Office 21,000,000 for 6,000 (about $79.16), Municipality or enterprise 130,000,000 for 40,000 (about $490) [A, set at about 23–28% of clerk cost after a lower first draft failed; no competitor price was found]. Mix 60% / 33% / 7% [A] gives ARPU 19,630,000 toman a month (about $74) [D]. A separate one-time project fee for large backlogs is possible and not counted.

A Persian scan-reading pipeline (open vision-language model, proxy of the Qwen2.5-VL-7B benchmark below), a classifier and search index (embedding model; BGE-M3 is MIT-licensed and lists 100+ languages, Persian not named [S, HF card]); domestic GPU nodes (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]) and domestic storage (Arvan storage EUR0.020 per GB extra, undated [S]); 2 engineers, 1 solutions engineer for large accounts (80M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Page reading and layout handling (stamps, handwriting notes, tables); classification and metadata extraction; building and updating the search index; per-customer tuning of categories; sampling outputs for human spot-check (3% of documents [A]); onboarding the backlog.

Domestic GPU/cloud host and storage; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); scanning and archive contractors, law-firm software vendors and municipal IT contractors as channels.

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 solutions engineer at 80M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 30M = 461.3M toman a month (about $1,739) [D]; one-time setup 200M [A] (classifier tuning and Persian test archive). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 222 toman per document for spot-checks and storage [A], an extra customer-success hire per 40 customers [A], an extra GPU node whenever load passes one node's capacity (the dominant variable cost).
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 solutions engineer at 80M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026

[D] 832 [S, Qwen2.5-VL-7B on an L40S, 32 concurrent requests, 512px image, 500 tokens in and 150 out, Clarifai blog, 26 Jun 2025] × 0.67 (Persian token overhead and Ada vs L40S, [A]); a proxy, not a measurement on Persian scans
[D] 4 pages [A] × 600 output tokens a page [A] ÷ 557 × 2 (scan resolution above the benchmark, [A]) × 1.10 (classification and embedding, [A])
[A] 3% of documents spot-checked at one minute of loaded wage (72) plus about six months of scan storage (150)
[D] 70% use [A] of the 1,500 / 6,000 / 40,000 quotas, weighted by plan mix
Law firm 63.1%, Office 58.0%, Municipality or enterprise 54.9%
[D] after GPU, spot-checks and storage, and 1% gateway

cost_model.x: One node covers only about 20 customers at this usage [D: 82,096 ÷ (3,976 + 200 free-pilot documents)], so compute is the main variable cost: the base case needs 8 nodes at month 24 and the optimistic case 18 [D], and nodes are 1,200M of the base case's 1,784M monthly cost at month 24 (67%) [D]. Customer-success staffing at one hire per 40 customers costs 922,500 toman a month per customer [D: 36.9M ÷ 40], 4.7% of revenue per customer. The one-time backlog load of a new customer is not modelled separately; it would arrive as a burst above the monthly quota and may need extra capacity or a project fee.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 25 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 461.3M ÷ (19,630,000 × 0.99 − 3,976 × 222) = 24.9], and stepping through customer counts with the nodes and hires each needs gives 33 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 200M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. At 150 customers the mix gives about 90 law firms, 50 offices and 10 municipality or enterprise accounts [D]; ten accounts is under 1% of the 1,245 cities [D, S above], but the linear ramp assumes procurement-driven buyers sign at the same pace as firms, which is optimistic. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −3,616M toman in the conservative case (payback beyond month 24, so the peak cash need of 4,411M came earlier), +5,105M in the base case and +24,250M in the optimistic case [D].

sensitivities.x: Compute price is the decisive stress: doubling it removes break-even because nodes are two thirds of the cost base, while price and customer shocks only delay it. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 2% monthly churn [A, archives are sticky once indexed, but pilots can end] lifetime value per customer is about 927.6M toman [D: (19,630,000 × 0.99 − 3,976 × 222) ÷ 0.02], and holding 150 customers needs about 3 new customers a month [D: 150 × 0.02]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Procurement and approved suppliers: municipalities and state bodies may buy only through tenders or from certified office-automation suppliers; I found no rule either way, and sales cycles longer than the ramp assumed would delay break-even.
Data residency and confidentiality: law-firm files and municipal papers are sensitive, so customers are likely to require domestic hosting and contractual secrecy [A]; no specific rule was read.

Scan quality: stamps, handwriting, faxed pages and old typewritten letters degrade reading; the throughput proxy is an English-language benchmark and the only Persian result I have is a 98% word accuracy on a clean sentence set from an academic article cited in #21, not on archives.
Compute dominates cost: nodes are 67% of base-case monthly cost at month 24, and backlog uploads arrive in bursts that raise the real number of nodes above the 30% average utilisation assumed.
Price acceptance: the plans only work at about 3,250–4,000 toman per document, after a lower first draft failed on cost; a cheaper non-GPU OCR engine would undercut it, and I did not cost one.
Substitutes: local office-automation and document-management vendors and scanning contractors; no price was found.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of municipalities (only 1,245 cities in 2016 was found) and of offices holding paper archives.
Prices of Iranian document-management, OCR and archive-digitization services (the one price source read is a US page).
Procurement and approved-supplier rules for municipalities and state bodies, and data-residency rules for legal files.
Accuracy and real throughput of an open vision-language model on Persian scans, and Persian retrieval quality of BGE-M3 (Persian is not named on its card).
Real documents per customer, pages per document and the size of backlog loads.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: شهروندان و وکلا (حرفه‌ای/خرد، خرده‌فروش و B2B2C (بسته‌های مدرسه/پلتفرم)). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: عریضه‌نویس یا حق‌الزحمه تنظیم دادخواست توسط وکیل (۱ تا ۵ میلیون تومان). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۴۵۷ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۲۳۰ پایه، ۱۷۵ رشد، ۵۲ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۱۳٫۰٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «عریضه‌نویس یا حق‌الزحمه تنظیم دادخواست توسط وکیل (۱ تا ۵ میلیون تومان)» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: قالب‌های دادخواست و شکواییه منطبق با عدل‌ایران/ثنا؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق دفاتر خدمات الکترونیک قضایی به‌همراه ۰٫۴۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۲٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۲۹٬۰۳۰٬۵۶۶ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۵۲ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal-to-viable on these assumptions, and decided by customer acquisition, not by compute. A document costs about 726 toman of GPU time (about $0.0027) and gross margin is 97–98% [D]; the plans charge 40,000–120,000 toman per document against about 286,046 toman of drafting time at the minimum wage [D]. Revenue per customer is about 531,000 toman a month ($2.00) against 507.1M toman of fixed cost, of which 130M is marketing, so break-even needs about 965 paying customers on paper and 1,176 with the node and hires counted [D]. The base case (1,000 customers at month 12, 4,000 at month 24) breaks even in month 13, with a peak cash need of 3,290M toman (about $12,400) and +1,116M a month at month 24; the conservative case (300 / 1,200) does not break even (−24M a month at month 24, cumulative cash −6,837M); the optimistic case (3,000 / 12,000) breaks even in month 7 with +4,325M. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each delay break-even (to months 15, 16 and 18) without removing it in the base case. The catch is that 80% of customers in the mix are one-time citizen buyers [A], so the base case needs about 3,200 new citizen purchases every month at month 24, and the 130M marketing line only works if each costs about 40,000 toman to win [A]. I found no count of complaints or petitions filed, no price for a drafting office or lawyer, and no rule on who may draft legal papers for others. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Citizens who must write a complaint, petition or objection to a court, a consumer or administrative body, or an employer — core by count. (b) Lawyers and legal assistants who draft many such papers — core by revenue. (c) Small law offices and judicial-services offices. Not targeted: complex litigation needing a lawyer's own strategy. Pool: no count of complaints or petitions filed per year was found. Headlines seen in search only (pages blocked by robots rules, not opened) report tens of thousands of public complaints against goods and service providers over several months in 2019–2020 [S, headline text only, eghtesadonline.com, not verified]; the number of lawyers is cited as more than 70,000 in #31 [S, undated].

The user answers plain questions (who, what happened, when, what evidence, what is wanted); the tool selects the document type and the receiving body, drafts the petition or complaint in formal Persian with the legal basis and a list of attachments, and gives a checklist for filing. The labour replaced is the research and drafting time: 2 hours [A], about 286,046 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 40,000–120,000 toman per document, 14–42% of that [D]. The judiciary's electronic-services regulation (15 Aug 2022) says petitions are filed through the portal or an electronic judicial-services office, with the system calculating the fee and issuing a tracking code, so the tool produces text for the user to file and does not file for them [S, nourlaw.com, read 25 Oct 2026].

Search and content on common complaint types (tenancy, consumer, employment, traffic fines, insurance); Telegram, Bale and Eitaa bots; partnerships with legal-services offices and lawyers' associations; a lawyer plan sold directly.

Self-service for citizens with a clear 'not legal advice, check with a lawyer' notice [A]; one free draft [A]; lawyers get templates, a clause library and a history of past drafts; one customer-success person per 300 customers [A]. Citizens pay per document in toman, lawyers monthly, indexed to the exchange rate.

Citizen 120,000 toman for 1 document (about $0.45); Lawyer 1,500,000 a month for 30 documents (about $5.65); Firm 6,000,000 a month for 150 (about $22.62) [A, no competitor price was found]. Mix 80% / 17% / 3% [A] gives ARPU 531,000 toman a month (about $2.00) [D].

A library of Iranian procedural forms and the articles of law that each complaint type cites, checked by a lawyer (public texts; completeness not verified); an 8B-class open instruction model with Persian capability; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 legal editor (40M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Building and updating the form and law library; intake interviews and drafting; automatic checks that required elements and attachments are present; lawyer review of templates; search and social acquisition of citizen buyers.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); a lawyer or lawyers' association as reviewer; judicial-services offices as a channel.

Fixed: team 209.1M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 40M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 130M = 507.1M toman a month (about $1,911) [D]; one-time setup 100M [A] (form library and lawyer review). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 300 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 40M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 6,000 input (user's facts, retrieved articles of law, template) plus about 2,000 output (the petition text)
[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 90% use [A] of the 1 / 30 / 150 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 19,955 customers at this usage [D: 206,730 ÷ (9.4 + 1 free draft)], so one node is enough in every scenario and compute is not the constraint. Customer-success staffing at one hire per 300 customers costs 123,000 toman a month per customer [D: 36.9M ÷ 300], 23% of revenue per customer. Marketing is the real variable cost: the 130M a month is sized for about 3,300 new paying accounts a month at roughly 40,000 toman each [A], which matches the base case at month 24 (about 3,200 new one-time citizen buyers a month [D: 80% of 4,000], plus a few lawyer accounts) but is too little for the optimistic case and more than the conservative case needs.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 965 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 507.1M ÷ (531,000 × 0.99) = 964.6], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 1,176 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 100M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]; no sourced population supports them, since no count of petitions or complaints filed was found. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −6,837M toman in the conservative case, +3,494M in the base case and +32,792M in the optimistic case [D].

sensitivities.x: Compute is a small part of cost, so a GPU price rise matters least; the number of buyers and the marketing cost to win them matter most, and the table keeps marketing fixed at 130M while customers halve. The model's customer path is fixed and does not include churn. A citizen's purchase is one-time, so lifetime revenue is about 118,800 toman [D: 120,000 × 0.99], while a lawyer plan at 5% monthly churn [A, lawyers keep a tool that saves drafting time] is about 29.7M toman [D: 1,500,000 × 0.99 ÷ 0.05]; the blended ARPU therefore rests on a monthly flow of new citizen buyers.

risks.x: Who may draft and file: I found no rule on whether a tool or a non-lawyer may draft petitions for others, or which filings require a lawyer; the judiciary's 2022 regulation covers electronic filing and does not settle this [S, nourlaw.com].

Wrong legal basis: a petition that cites the wrong article or body can lose the user a case or a deadline, which creates complaints, refunds and liability; the service needs lawyer-checked templates and visible disclaimers.

Acquisition cost: the base case needs about 3,200 new citizen buyers a month at month 24 at about 40,000 toman each [A]; free general chatbots can draft the same text, so a paid product must win on trust and form accuracy.

Sensitive data: complaints contain names, disputes and evidence, and customers may refuse to upload them unless hosting is domestic; the E-Commerce Act's personal-data articles are summarised in #38 and no specific rule for legal papers was read.
Seasonality and episodes: demand follows disputes and deadlines (tenancy renewals, fines, tax and insurance cases), so monthly counts will be lumpy.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: Number of complaints and petitions filed per year, and the share written with paid help (the only figures are search headlines, not opened).
Prices of lawyers, judicial-services offices and typing offices for drafting a petition.
Rules on drafting legal papers for others and on which filings need a lawyer.
Accuracy of an 8B-class open model on Persian legal drafting and correct article citation, and real tokens per document.
Real cost to win a citizen buyer (40,000 toman is an assumption) and conversion from search traffic.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: درمانگاه‌ها (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: حقوق منشی کلینیک (۱۶ تا ۲۲ میلیون تومان در ماه). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۲۱۵ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۸۶ پایه، ۹۹ رشد، ۳۰ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۸٫۵٪.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal-thin on these assumptions. A booking conversation costs about 423 toman (about $0.0016) including two SMS messages, and gross margin is 74–82% [D]; the plans charge 1,333–2,000 toman per booking against about 9,535 toman of receptionist time at the minimum wage [D], and about 1.6% of a general practitioner's visit tariff of 126,000 toman [D, S below]. Revenue per customer is only about 1.445M toman a month ($5.45) against 417.1M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 301 paying clinics on paper and 514 with the node and hires counted [D]. The base case (250 customers at month 12, 800 at month 24) breaks even in month 18, with a peak cash need of 4,231M toman (about $15,947) and only +64M a month at month 24 (cumulative cash −4,120M); the conservative case (100 / 300) does not break even (−185M a month, cumulative cash −7,002M); the optimistic case (700 / 2,500) breaks even in month 10 with +940M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each remove break-even. Onboarding and support are the heavy cost: one customer-success hire per 60 clinics costs 42.6% of revenue per customer [D]. Booking marketplaces already list doctors, I found no price for them, and I found no rule on handling patient data. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Doctors with private offices who answer booking calls through a secretary or not at all — core by count. (b) Clinics and polyclinics with a reception desk and several doctors — core by revenue. (c) Dental, physiotherapy and similar practices. Not targeted: public hospitals with state booking systems. Pool: about 100,000 doctors in Iran in a 2011 table [S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare\_in\_Iran, read 25 Oct 2026; the table gives no source]; in Mashhad 2,915 physicians, about 45% of those registered with the council, had private offices in October 2013, 51.9% general practitioners [S, jmmc.mums.ac.ir/article\_2284, read 25 Oct 2026]. Applying 45% to 100,000 gives about 45,000 doctors with private offices [D, rough: one city, 2013, and doctors have since emigrated or stopped practising; the Medical Council head said about 30,000 general practitioners were unwilling to practise over low fees, 9 Jan 2025 [S, iranintl.com/en/202501093061, read 25 Oct 2026]].

Patients message a Telegram, Bale or Eitaa bot, a web chat or a link on the clinic's page; the bot asks the intake questions the doctor needs (reason, duration, medicines, allergies, insurance), proposes free slots, books, sends the confirmation and reminder by SMS, and hands the doctor a one-paragraph summary before the visit; it does not give medical advice and routes red-flag answers to a human. The labour replaced is the secretary's phone and message time: 4 minutes per booking [A], about 9,535 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans below charge 1,333–2,000 toman per booking, 14–21% of that [D]. For scale, the tariff for a general practitioner visit is 1.26 million rials (126,000 toman) and for a specialist 1.89 million rials (189,000 toman) [S, iranintl.com/en/202501093061, 9 Jan 2025; the year the tariff was set is not stated].

Direct sales and field visits to clinics in the biggest cities; partnerships with clinic-software and medical-association vendors; referral from medical-supplier representatives; a free booking page for each doctor.

Free pilot of 20 bookings [A]; setup call to load schedules and rules; weekly digest of no-shows and booked slots; one customer-success person per 60 customers [A] (onboarding is heavy). Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of bookings: Doctor office 600,000 toman for 300 bookings (about $2.26), Clinic 2,500,000 for 1,500 (about $9.42), Polyclinic 8,000,000 for 6,000 (about $30.16) [A, no competitor price was found]. Mix 70% / 25% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 1,445,000 toman a month (about $5.45) [D].

A scheduling engine with clinic rules; Persian intake question sets per specialty reviewed by a physician (clinical content, to be written); an 8B-class open instruction model with Persian capability; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]) and SMS access through a domestic provider; 2 engineers, 1 field onboarding hire (40M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Loading doctors' schedules and rules; maintaining intake question sets; handling reschedules and cancellations; sending reminders; escalating red-flag answers; monitoring no-show and booking data for each clinic.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; an SMS provider (domestic SMS is about 100–200 rials on the same network and 150–250 rials across networks [S, sent.dm, 3 May 2025]); payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); a physician adviser for intake questions; clinic-software vendors.

Fixed: team 209.1M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 field onboarding at 40M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 417.1M toman a month (about $1,572) [D]; one-time setup 120M [A] (intake sets and clinic pilots). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 60 toman per booking for SMS and handling [A], an extra customer-success hire per 60 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.

cost_model.x: One node covers about 568 customers at this usage [D: 413,461 ÷ (708 + 20 free-pilot bookings)], so one node is enough in the conservative case, the base case needs a second node at month 24 and the optimistic case needs 5 [D]. Customer-success staffing at one hire per 60 customers costs 615,000 toman a month per customer [D: 36.9M ÷ 60], 42.6% of revenue per customer, the largest cost per customer; if clinics need less hand-holding than assumed this falls, and if they need more break-even moves out. No intake-accuracy or no-show-reduction benefit is priced in.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 301 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 417.1M ÷ (1,445,000 × 0.99 − 708 × 60) = 300.5], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 514 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 120M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. For scale only, 800 customers is 1.8% of the rough pool of 45,000 doctors with private offices [D, above], and 2,500 is 5.6% [D]; many customers would be multi-doctor clinics, so the share of doctors reached is higher. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −7,002M toman in the conservative case, −4,120M in the base case and +4,098M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 4,231M came earlier, and base-case payback is beyond month 24.

sensitivities.x: The base case earns only +64M a month at month 24, so any of the three shocks removes break-even; the low revenue per clinic ($5.45 a month) means fixed cost is covered only at several hundred accounts. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 4% monthly churn [A, clinics keep a booking tool once schedules are loaded, but small offices stop paying] lifetime value per customer is about 34.7M toman [D: (1,445,000 × 0.99 − 708 × 60) ÷ 0.04], and holding 800 customers needs about 32 new customers a month [D: 800 × 0.04]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Existing booking platforms: online doctor-booking apps and websites already exist in Iran (Paziresh24 appears as an app listing in search results, and one search headline ranks online doctor-visit searches; pages not opened); I found no price or fee, so the price assumption could be above or below what doctors already pay.
Patient data: intake answers are health data; I found no rule on handling it, but clinics are likely to require domestic hosting and secrecy [A].
Clinical safety: a bot that mis-triages a red-flag answer creates liability; the service must not advise, must escalate, and needs physician-reviewed question sets.

Doctor supply: doctors are emigrating or leaving practice (the Medical Council head cited about 30,000 unwilling general practitioners [S, iranintl.com/en/202501093061]), which shrinks the pool and changes who buys.

Messaging channel access: patients mostly book by phone; adoption of Bale, Telegram and Eitaa bots, and the SMS route, depend on the same platforms and operator rules as #10, and near-total internet blackouts have occurred (Bale, TechRadar, June 2025, as noted in #19).
Onboarding cost: schedules, rules and staff habits differ for every clinic; if onboarding takes more than one customer-success hire per 60 clinics the margin disappears.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: A current count of doctors with private offices and of clinics (the 100,000 figure is from a 2011 table, the 45% share from one city in 2013).
Prices and fees of Paziresh24 and other booking platforms (Paziresh24's app page is blocked from fetching; search returned titles only).
Rules on handling patient data and on automated intake in private practice.
No-show rates and the real share of bookings made by phone.
Accuracy of an 8B-class open model on Persian medical intake, real tokens per booking, and SMS price under a signed contract.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but it rests on Persian medical speech recognition that I could not verify. A visit note costs about 856 toman (about $0.0032) including GPU time and audio storage, and gross margin is 76–82% [D]; the plans charge 3,000–4,000 toman per note against about 9,535 toman of typing time at the minimum wage [D], which understates a doctor's time. Revenue per customer is about 2.99M toman a month ($11.27) against 407.1M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 138 paying accounts on paper and 164 with the node and hires counted [D]. The base case (150 accounts at month 12, 600 at month 24) breaks even in month 13, with a peak cash need of 2,711M toman (about $10,219) and +691M a month at month 24 (cumulative cash +1,643M); the conservative case (50 / 200) breaks even in month 22 with a peak cash need of 5,050M and +71M at month 24; the optimistic case (400 / 1,500) breaks even in month 7 with +2,189M. Doubling the GPU price delays break-even to month 18, cutting prices 30% to month 19 and halving customers to month 17. The decisive risk is accuracy: on the one public Persian ASR leaderboard I read, a general open model made 36–76% word errors and a fine-tuned Persian model 11–22% on general test sets, and I found no medical-vocabulary test or confirmed licence for that fine-tuned model. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Doctors in private practice who type or hand-write a note for every visit — core. (b) Clinics and polyclinics that equip several doctors. (c) Hospital departments and teaching clinics. Not targeted: hospitals with an in-house record system that forbids add-ons. Pool: about 45,000 doctors with private offices, a rough figure derived in #41 from a 2011 count of about 100,000 doctors and a 45% private-office share in one city in 2013 [D from S, see #41]; the Medical Council head said about 30,000 general practitioners were unwilling to practise over low fees (iranintl.com/en/202501093061, 9 Jan 2025 [S]). At 600 accounts in the base case the mix gives about 1,770 doctor users (420 single doctors, 150 clinics of 5, 30 departments of 20) [D], 3.9% of that pool [D].

The doctor speaks the visit summary in Persian (with drug names, English terms and numbers); the tool transcribes it and fills a structured note: complaint, history, findings, diagnosis, prescription list, advice and follow-up, in the clinic's template, ready to paste into the record or print. The labour replaced is typing: 4 minutes per note [A], about 9,535 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), far below a doctor's own time value; the plans below charge 3,000–4,000 toman per note, 32–42% of that [D]. Foreign anchors: AI scribes list at $39–$119 per clinician per month for Freed, about $150 for Heidi's paid plan and about $200–$600 for Abridge, and AWS HealthScribe is $0.10 per audio minute [S, getfreed.ai/resources/cost-of-ai-scribes, dated 21 Jul 2026, read 25 Oct 2026; vendor-comparison page, not independently verified]; the Doctor plan below at about $4.52 a month is 3.8–11.6% of Freed's range [D], and a 3-minute note at the AWS rate is $0.30 against about $0.015 here [D].
Phone and web app with one-tap recording; clinic-software integrations; sales through medical societies and supplier representatives; a free trial to individual doctors who then bring their clinics.

Free first 20 notes [A]; custom note templates per specialty and per doctor; correction learning (the tool remembers drug lists and phrasing the doctor edits); one customer-success person per 60 accounts [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of notes: Doctor 1,200,000 toman for 300 notes (about $4.52), Clinic 5,000,000 for 1,500 across 5 doctors (about $18.85), Department 18,000,000 for 6,000 across 20 doctors (about $67.85) [A, no Iranian competitor price was found]. Mix 70% / 25% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 2,990,000 toman a month (about $11.27) [D].

A Persian speech-recognition model that handles medical terms, drug names and mixed Persian-English speech (an open Persian fine-tune such as gooya-v1.4 scored 11–22% word error on public test sets [S, navidved Open Persian ASR Leaderboard, 23 Oct 2026]; its licence was not confirmed); a note-structuring 8B-class instruction model; a medical term and drug list; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 clinical language editor (40M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Transcribing and structuring notes; building medical vocabulary and template sets; measuring word and field error rates with doctor-corrected samples; integrating with record or clinic software; keeping audio and notes secure.
Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); a physician adviser; clinic-software vendors; medical societies as channels.

Fixed: team 209.1M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 clinical editor at 40M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 30M = 407.1M toman a month (about $1,535) [D]; one-time setup 150M [A] (vocabulary, templates and doctor-reviewed test sets). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 20 toman per note for audio storage [A], an extra customer-success hire per 60 accounts [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.

[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026

cost_model.x: One node covers about 246 accounts at this usage [D: 179,440 ÷ (708 + 20 free-trial notes)], so the base case needs 3 nodes at month 24 and the optimistic case 7 [D]. Customer-success staffing at one hire per 60 accounts costs 615,000 toman a month per account [D: 36.9M ÷ 60], 21% of revenue per account. Speech recognition is 83% of GPU time per note [D: 6.00 ÷ 7.22], so the unmeasured 30× speed assumption drives the cost. Accuracy review by the doctor is not priced.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 138 paying accounts on the fixed-cost formula [D: 407.1M ÷ (2,990,000 × 0.99 − 708 × 20) = 138.2], and stepping through account counts with the node and hires each needs gives 164 accounts [D]. Accounts ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 150M setup falls in month 1.

Account counts are [A]. At month 24 the base case is about 1,770 doctor users, 3.9% of the rough 45,000 private-office pool [D, above]; the optimistic case is about 4,425 users, 9.8% [D: 1,050 single doctors + 375 clinics × 5 + 75 departments × 20], and the conservative case about 590 users [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −4,909M toman in the conservative case (payback beyond month 24, so the peak cash need of 5,050M came earlier), +1,643M in the base case and +16,531M in the optimistic case [D].

sensitivities.x: No single stress removes break-even in the base case, but each leaves it thin, and a 30% price cut together with the unmeasured speech speed would erase most of the month-24 profit. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 5% monthly churn [A, doctors stop dictating if corrections take longer than typing] lifetime value per account is about 58.9M toman [D: (2,990,000 × 0.99 − 708 × 20) ÷ 0.05], and holding 600 accounts needs about 30 new accounts a month [D: 600 × 0.05]. Marketing cost per account was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Medical-term accuracy: general Persian ASR is poor on specialised speech (whisper-large-v3 scored 36–76% word error on the leaderboard's four test sets, 75.7% on customer-service calls; a fine-tuned Persian model 11–22% [S, navidved leaderboard, 23 Oct 2026]); drug names, Latin terms and numbers are the hard part and no medical test set was found. A wrong dose in a note is a safety issue, so the doctor must review every note.
Licence of the Persian ASR model: not confirmed (as in #17); a non-commercial licence would block the service until a model is built or licensed.
Patient data: voice and notes are health data; I found no specific rule, but clinics are likely to require domestic hosting and secrecy [A].
Integration: notes are only useful if they reach the clinic's record or print template; Iranian clinic software varies and I found no integration standard.
Habit: doctors who already type quickly or use paper may not adopt dictation, and clinic noise degrades audio.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers in the base case, but thin in the conservative case and blocked by two things I could not verify: a Persian-population-validated image model and the medical-device rules for diagnostic software. A scan costs about 2,886 toman (about $0.0109) to analyse, including GPU time and a 3% specialist audit, and gross margin is 68–84% by plan [D]; the plans charge 7,500–15,000 toman per scan against about 19,070 toman of specialist reading time at the minimum wage [D], which understates a specialist's time. Revenue per account is about 5.55M toman a month ($20.92) against 510.5M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 118 paying accounts on paper and 135 with the node and hires counted [D]. The base case (120 accounts at month 12, 450 at month 24) breaks even in month 13, with a peak cash need of 3,921M toman (about $14,779) and +1,186M a month at month 24 (cumulative cash +3,536M); the conservative case (40 / 150) breaks even in month 23 with a peak cash need of 6,983M and only +67M at month 24, and it has not paid back by month 24; the optimistic case (300 / 1,200) breaks even in month 8 with +3,815M. Doubling the GPU price delays break-even to month 14, cutting prices 30% to month 17 and halving customers to month 18. The decisive risks are clinical: I found no public accuracy figure for an image model on Iranian clinics' panoramic and chest films, and no Iranian rule on diagnostic AI, so the tool must be sold as a second reader whose findings a clinician confirms, and a licence for any open medical-image model is unconfirmed. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Dental offices that take panoramic, bitewing and periapical films — core. (b) Radiology clinics that read chest, spine and dental films for referrers. (c) Dental or hospital chains and hospital radiology departments. Not targeted: patients directly. Pool for (a): Iran had 35,404 dentists in 2019 (30,811 general, 4,593 specialists), 43 per 100,000 people (Journal of Oral Health and Oral Epidemiology, johoe.kmu.ac.ir/article\_91637.html, read 26 Oct 2026 [S]); with 60% of them in private offices [A, no source found] that is about 21,242 offices or practitioners [D], and the base case at month 24 (450 accounts, about 360 of them dental offices) is 2.1% of that pool [D]. I found no count of Iranian radiology clinics.

The tool reads an uploaded panoramic or chest film, marks suspected findings (caries, periapical lesions, bone loss, impacted teeth, nodules or fractures on the chest or limb films) and drafts a one-paragraph note, so the dentist or radiologist reviews a prepared reading rather than starting from nothing. The labour replaced is the first read: 8 minutes per film [A], about 19,070 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans charge 7,500–15,000 toman per scan, 39–79% of that [D]. Foreign anchors: dental-AI subscriptions cost roughly $200–$500 a month per office, average $300, and consumer apps $5–$25 per scan [S, realdentalcosts.com/en/dental-costs/ai-dentistry-diagnosis-cost, reviewed 31 May 2026, read 26 Oct 2026; US edition, from vendor and practice data, not independently verified]; the Overjet comparison page says Overjet and VideaHealth price per location or usage and Pearl per user per month, with no figures given (overjet.com/blog/cost-of-dental-ai-overjet-vs-pearl-vs-videahealth, 22 Apr 2025, read 26 Oct 2026 [S]). The dental-office plan below at about $5.65 a month is 1.9% of the $300 average [D].

Web upload and a plug-in for the film-capture software dental offices and radiology clinics already use; sales through dental associations, equipment and film-sensor suppliers; a free trial to individual offices.

Free first 10 scans [A]; every finding is labelled as a suggestion for clinician confirmation; the 3% sample audited by a specialist is reported back to the clinic as an accuracy log [A]; one customer-success person per 60 accounts [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of scans: Dental office 1,500,000 toman for 100 scans (about $5.65), Radiology clinic 15,000,000 for 1,500 scans (about $56.54), Chain or hospital 60,000,000 for 8,000 scans (about $226.16) [A, no Iranian competitor price was found]. Mix 80% / 17% / 3% [A] gives ARPU 5,550,000 toman a month (about $20.92) [D].

A licensed or self-trained image model for panoramic and chest films, with a labelled Iranian sample for testing (open medical-image models often carry non-commercial or research licences; I confirmed none); a report-writing vision-language or 8B-class text model; specialist time for the 3% audit; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 customer-success hire and a 120M toman gross a month specialist and annotation budget [A].

Collecting and labelling films with consent; measuring sensitivity and false alarms per finding at each clinic; specialist audit of a sample; integration with capture software; keeping images and notes secure.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); a radiologist and a dental specialist as clinical advisers; equipment and software suppliers; dental and radiology associations as channels.

Fixed: team 307.5M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 120M specialist and annotation budget, gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 30M = 510.5M toman a month (about $1,924) [D]; one-time setup 600M [A] (labelled test and training films, clinical validation and legal review). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 2,500 toman per scan for the 3% specialist audit [A], an extra customer-success hire per 60 accounts [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 120M specialist and annotation budget, gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 0.5 s for a detection and segmentation model plus about 1.5 s for the report text from a vision-language or text model, on one RTX 6000 Ada; a non-text proxy, not measured
[A] films arrive in office hours and in bursts
[A] 3% of scans audited by a radiologist or dental specialist, 10 minutes each at a loaded 500,000 toman an hour (83,333 per audit)
[D] 80% use [A] of the 100 / 1,500 / 8,000 quotas, weighted by plan mix
Dental office 83.6%, Radiology clinic 75.9%, Chain or hospital 68.2%

cost_model.x: One node covers about 827 accounts at this usage [D: 388,800 ÷ (460 + 10 free-trial scans)], so the base case needs one node at month 24 and the optimistic case two [D]. The specialist audit is 87% of variable cost per scan [D: 2,500 ÷ 2,886] and the node is 29% of fixed cost [D: 150 ÷ 510.5], so the audit rate matters more than the GPU speed. Customer-success staffing at one hire per 60 accounts costs 615,000 toman a month per account [D: 36.9M ÷ 60], 11% of revenue per account. The cost of building or licensing the image model is only the 600M setup guess; clinician review of every flagged film is not priced.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 118 paying accounts on the fixed-cost formula [D: 510.5M ÷ (5,550,000 × 0.99 − 460 × 2,500) = 117.5], and stepping through account counts with the node and hires each needs gives 135 accounts [D]. Accounts ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 600M setup falls in month 1.

Account counts are [A]. At month 24 the base case is about 450 accounts and 207,000 scans a month [D: 450 × 460]; the optimistic case is about 960 dental offices, 4.5% of the rough 21,242 pool [D], plus about 204 radiology clinics and 36 chains, for which I found no population. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −6,888M toman in the conservative case (payback beyond month 24, so the peak cash need of 6,983M came earlier), +3,536M in the base case and +27,970M in the optimistic case [D].

sensitivities.x: No single stress removes break-even in the base case, and the GPU price barely matters because the node is a small part of cost; the month-24 profit is most exposed to price and to the account count. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 4% monthly churn [A, clinics keep a tool that is built into the capture step] lifetime value per account is about 108.6M toman [D: (5,550,000 × 0.99 − 460 × 2,500) ÷ 0.04], and holding 450 accounts needs about 18 new accounts a month [D: 450 × 0.04]. Marketing cost per account was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Accuracy: I found no public sensitivity or false-alarm figure for an image model on Iranian clinics' films; missed lesions or false alarms would turn the tool into extra work, and the 3% audit rate would have to rise (at 10% the audit cost per scan is about 8,333 toman [D: 83,333 × 10%], which would cut the dental-office plan's gross margin to about 41% [D] and make the chain plan, at 7,500 toman a scan, loss-making).

Image-model licence: open medical-image models are often research or non-commercial; none was confirmed, so the service may require training a model on licensed data, which the 600M setup does not cover.

Device rules: diagnostic software may need registration as a medical device with the health ministry; I found no Iranian rule, so the product is described as a second reader and clinical liability stays with the clinician [A].
Patient data: films are health data; clinics are likely to require domestic hosting and consent [A]; I found no specific rule.
Adoption: dentists who read films quickly may see little value, and capture software from equipment vendors may not accept add-ons.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: Sensitivity and false-alarm rates of any image model on panoramic or chest films from Iranian clinics, and the licence of any open model that reaches them.
Whether Iranian rules classify diagnostic image software as a regulated medical device, and what approval it needs.
The number of radiology clinics, how many films a dental office takes a month, and the private-practice share of dentists (60% is an assumption).
Any Iranian price for image-reading or dental-AI software.
Real GPU time per film (2.0 seconds is an assumption).
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 26 Oct 2026.

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: داروخانه‌ها (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: حذف داروهای منقضی و از دست رفتن فروش کمبودها. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۹۳ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۷۴ پایه، ۸۹ رشد، ۳۰ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۶٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «حذف داروهای منقضی و از دست رفتن فروش کمبودها» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: نگاشت داروی ژنریک/برند ایرانی IRC و مدل تقاضای فصلی؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق نرم‌افزار داروخانه ایمن‌افزار، قائم و فارابی به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۵٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۶۳٬۱۸۸٬۹۳۵ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۱۰ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (ماهانه): پایه ۱٬۵۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۰۹۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۸۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۴۴۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۷۸٬۶۳۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۶۴۸٬۰۹۱٬۶۵۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۲۴ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۳۶٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۵٬۹۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: LightGBM / Prophet با فصلیت جلالی + حل‌کننده قید OR-Tools + توضیح‌دهنده Qwen3-8B روی CPU/GPU مشترک. مجموعه داده: نگاشت داروی ژنریک/برند ایرانی IRC و مدل تقاضای فصلی.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی نگاشت داروی ژنریک/برند ایرانی IRC و مدل تقاضای فصلی؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های نرم‌افزار داروخانه ایمن‌افزار، قائم و فارابی در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: نرم‌افزار داروخانه ایمن‌افزار، قائم و فارابی. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

bmc.title: ساختار هزینه (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: هزینه کامل مستقل: ۴۲۵٬۹۷۵٬۳۶۵ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA مستقل: ۲۵۲٬۶۵۴٬۶۳۵ تومان/ماه (۳۷٫۲٪). هزینه سبد موتور مشترک (تقسیم توسعه/دفتر بین ۳ ابزار هم‌خانواده): ۳۴۹٬۱۴۵٬۳۶۵ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA سبد: ۳۲۹٬۴۸۴٬۶۳۵ تومان/ماه (۴۸٫۶٪).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal. The service is cheap to run, about 319 toman (about $0.0012) per daily order proposal with gross margin around 98% [D], so the result depends almost entirely on how many pharmacies pay and on a small team's fixed cost. Revenue per account is about 1.50M toman a month ($5.67) against 407.1M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 274 paying accounts on paper and 373 with the node and hires counted [D]. The base case (150 accounts at month 12, 600 at month 24) breaks even in month 18, with a peak cash need of 4,394M toman (about $16,561) and +227M a month at month 24, but cumulative cash is still −3,643M then, so it has not paid back; the conservative case (60 / 200) never breaks even in 24 months, with a peak cash need of 7,293M and −183M at month 24; the optimistic case (300 / 1,200) breaks even in month 13 with +825M. Doubling the GPU price delays break-even to month 22, while cutting prices 30% or halving customers removes break-even within 24 months. Account counts are heavy because chains count as one account but several branches, and the 8,500-pharmacy pool is an undated figure [S]. The tool forecasts demand and expiry from the pharmacy's own sales; it cannot forecast supply shortages, and I could not verify how pharmacy software, wholesaler lists or the national track-and-trace system would give it data. Substitution hints are suggestions for the pharmacist only. Customer counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Independent community pharmacies — core. (b) Pharmacy chains and groups of branches. (c) Hospital pharmacies and wholesalers' retail arms. Pool: about 8,500 pharmacies in Iran (Chemanager, chemanager-online.com/en/node/418762, read 26 Oct 2026; the page gives no year and its market figure is for 2015, so the count is probably several years old [S]). At month 24 the base case has 600 accounts: about 360 single pharmacies, 192 with alerts and 48 chains of 10 branches, covering about 1,032 pharmacies, 12.1% of the pool [D]; the optimistic case covers about 2,064, 24.3% [D], which is a very high share; the conservative case about 344, 4.0% [D].

Each morning the tool turns the pharmacy's sales and stock export into a proposed order (what to reorder, how much), flags items that will expire before they sell, and, when a product is short at the wholesaler, suggests same-ingredient alternatives matched through Iranian brand names. The labour replaced is the daily stock and expiry check: 20 minutes per order [A], about 47,674 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); the plans charge 26,667–40,000 toman per proposal, 56–84% of that [D]. Context [S]: Stimson reports that as many as 300 drug types were in short supply and about 100 unavailable (citing IRNA), most prices rose 15% to over 150%, about $35 million of pharmacy cheques to drug companies bounced and 3 in 10 patients abandon a purchase at checkout (stimson.org/2025/irans-dire-and-growing-drug-shortage, 2025, read 26 Oct 2026); Iran International reported on 13 Dec 2025 that suppliers warned of worsening shortages (iranintl.com/en/202512136473, lead only). Foreign anchors: inventory software with expiry tracking such as Vencru lists at $0, $6, $30 and $50 a month, and general inventory tools such as Zoho Inventory at $39–$299 a month [S, vencru.com/blog/7-best-inventory-management-software-for-pharmacy, published 24 May 2024, modified 20 May 2025, read 26 Oct 2026; currency not stated, presumed USD]; the single-pharmacy plan below at about $3.02 a month is 50% of the $6 plan [D]. A vendor blog says one chain cut excess inventory by 50% across 332 locations with AI replenishment, with no year or baseline (leafio.ai/blog/pharmacy-inventory-management, updated 29 Apr 2026 [S], vendor claim).

Web app and a data-export connector for the pharmacy software in use; sales through pharmacist associations, wholesaler sales representatives and pharmacy-software vendors; a free first month to individual pharmacies.

Free first 3 proposals [A]; a weekly summary of expiring stock; the pharmacist accepts or edits every proposal, and the tool learns from edits; one customer-success person per 80 accounts [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of proposals: Pharmacy 800,000 toman for 30 proposals (about $3.02), Pharmacy plus alerts 1,200,000 for 30 proposals with expiry and substitution alerts (about $4.52), Chain 8,000,000 for 300 proposals across 10 branches (about $30.16) [A, no Iranian competitor price was found]. Mix 60% / 32% / 8% [A] gives ARPU 1,504,000 toman a month (about $5.67) [D].

A drug master list with brand names, active ingredients and strengths (the national list was not confirmed to be open); a forecasting engine on the pharmacy's own sales; a small instruction model to write substitution notes and match names; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 customer-success hire and a 40M gross a month pharmacist adviser and data cleaner [A].

Cleaning drug names and units; connecting to pharmacy software exports; backtesting forecasts on each pharmacy's history; maintaining the substitution list with a pharmacist; updating prices and shortages from wholesaler lists.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); pharmacy-software vendors; wholesalers and distributors as data and sales partners; a licensed pharmacist adviser.

Fixed: team 209.1M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 40M pharmacist adviser and data cleaner, gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 30M = 407.1M toman a month (about $1,535) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (drug master list, name matching and connectors). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 30 toman per proposal for messages and storage [A], an extra customer-success hire per 80 accounts [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 40M pharmacist adviser and data cleaner, gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] the forecast over about 3,000 products runs on CPU at negligible cost; the GPU writes substitution notes for 5–10 flagged items; not measured
[A] proposals are generated in a morning window
[D] 85% use [A] of the 30 / 30 / 300 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 11,060 accounts at this usage [D: 518,400 ÷ (43.9 + 3 free-trial proposals)], so a single node serves every scenario; it is a fixed cost of 150M that is idle in practice, and a CPU-only design would cut about 133M of fixed cost [D: 150M less a 17M toman CPU server, [A]], but I did not model it because the substitution note needs a language model. Customer-success staffing at one hire per 80 accounts costs 461,000 toman a month per account [D: 36.9M ÷ 80], 31% of revenue per account, which is the largest variable item. A pharmacist's review of the substitution list and wholesaler price data are not priced.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 274 paying accounts on the fixed-cost formula [D: 407.1M ÷ (1,504,000 × 0.99 − 43.9 × 30) = 273.7], and stepping through account counts with the node and hires each needs gives 373 accounts [D]. Accounts ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Account counts are [A]. At month 24 the base case covers about 1,032 pharmacies, 12.1% of the 8,500 pool [D, above]; the optimistic case about 2,064 (24.3%) and the conservative case about 344 (4.0%) [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −7,293M toman in the conservative case, −3,643M in the base case (not yet paid back at month 24; the peak cash need of 4,394M came earlier) and +1,956M in the optimistic case [D].

sensitivities.x: Two of the three stresses remove break-even within 24 months, and the doubled GPU price still halves month-24 profit, because the idle node is a large part of fixed cost. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 3% monthly churn [A, a tool tied to daily ordering is sticky once the export connector works] lifetime value per account is about 49.6M toman [D: (1,504,000 × 0.99 − 43.9 × 30) ÷ 0.03], and holding 600 accounts needs about 18 new accounts a month [D: 600 × 0.03]. Marketing cost per account was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Data access: forecasts need each pharmacy's sales history; pharmacy software varies and I found no export standard. The national drug track-and-trace system (TTAC) appears in search titles, but the one detailed page was blocked, so whether pharmacies or third parties can use its data is unverified.

Shortage forecasting: shortages come from supply, price and import decisions, not from a pharmacy's sales; the tool can only react to a wholesaler's out-of-stock list, which I did not find in machine-readable form.
Substitution rules: pharmacists may only dispense alternatives under health-ministry rules and prescriber consent; I did not verify them, so hints are advisory [A].

Low willingness to pay: 3 in 10 patients abandon purchases at checkout [S, Stimson], and pharmacy margins are not given in any source I opened; a price near $3–$5 a month may be affordable, but pharmacies with bounced cheques may delay payment.
Account counts: chains count as one account but ten branches in the pool share; opening that many branches is slower than opening single pharmacies.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: A current count of Iranian pharmacies (8,500 is undated) and how many use inventory software.
Pharmacy margin rules and any Iranian price for pharmacy inventory or expiry software.
Whether TTAC or wholesaler stock data can be reached by a third party, and the rules for brand-to-generic substitution.
The real share of stock lost to expiry in Iranian pharmacies (the foreign figures I found are vendor claims without year or method).
Real GPU time per proposal (1.5 seconds is an assumption).
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 26 Oct 2026.

bmc.text: جایگزین «عوارض دارویی و جست‌وجوی دستی در دارویاب» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: گراف تداخل برند و ژنریک داخلی سازمان غذا و دارو؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق صندوق فروش داروخانه و سامانه‌های HIS بیمارستانی به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۴٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۵۳٬۷۲۴٬۲۳۶ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۱۳ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (ماهانه): پایه ۱٬۴۷۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۲۰۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۷٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۴۷۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۱۸٬۱۹۵٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۹۰٬۳۷۶٬۲۲۵ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۴۲ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۶۳٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۰٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen3-14B/32B کوانتیزه (AWQ، مجوز Apache 2.0) با vLLM + امبدینگ فارسی BGE-M3 + پایگاه برداری Qdrant روی CPU. مجموعه داده: گراف تداخل برند و ژنریک داخلی سازمان غذا و دارو.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی گراف تداخل برند و ژنریک داخلی سازمان غذا و دارو؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های صندوق فروش داروخانه و سامانه‌های HIS بیمارستانی در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: صندوق فروش داروخانه و سامانه‌های HIS بیمارستانی. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

bmc.title: ساختار هزینه (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: هزینه کامل مستقل: ۴۲۲٬۷۶۰٬۱۱۵ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA مستقل: ۱۹۵٬۴۳۴٬۸۸۵ تومان/ماه (۳۱٫۶٪). هزینه سبد موتور مشترک (تقسیم توسعه/دفتر بین ۳ ابزار هم‌خانواده): ۳۴۴٬۸۲۰٬۱۱۵ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA سبد: ۲۷۳٬۳۷۴٬۸۸۵ تومان/ماه (۴۴٫۲٪).

gtm: صندوق فروش داروخانه و سامانه‌های HIS بیمارستانی
