verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: weak to marginal, and blocked first by hardware I could not source. The base case (120 paying sites at month 24) breaks even only in month 23 and earns +11M toman a month at month 24, with cumulative cash still −5,489M (about $20,690); the conservative case (45 sites) never breaks even (cumulative −8,357M), and the optimistic case (300 sites) breaks even in month 13 and ends at +1,053M cumulative [D]. Halving the customer count, cutting prices 30%, or doubling the GPU price each put the base case below break-even [D]. Site counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian plants with rotating machinery that would pay for monitoring (an undated headline mentions 43,000 active industrial units in 2019 [S, eghtesadonline, page blocked, title only]). The service needs vibration sensors that the customer must buy: vendor-blog prices are $150 to $350 for an entry-level wireless sensor, $400 to $800 with FFT, and $900 to $1,800 industrial-rated [S, oxmaint.com, 28 May 2026, vendor blog, unverified]; at 265,295 toman an entry sensor is 39.8M to 92.9M toman [D], about 133 to 310 months of the 300,000 toman a machine subscription here [D]. I did not find whether such sensors can be imported or built domestically, so hardware sourcing and price are unverified and not in the model. Detection quality on Iranian machines is unproven; the standard public benchmark (CWRU) shows accuracy dropping from about 95% to about 53% when the split stops leaking test information [S, arxiv 2407.14625].

r: (a) Small plants with about 5 critical machines (pumps, fans, motors). (b) Mid-size plants with about 20 machines. (c) Large plants (steel, cement, petrochemical suppliers, mines) with about 100 machines [A]. Pool: no count of Iranian plants by size with rotating assets was found; the plan sizes and mix are [A]. 120 paying sites at month 24 is [A].

Wireless vibration and temperature sensors on motors, pumps, fans and gearboxes send readings to the cloud; the tool learns each machine's normal spectrum, flags bearing, imbalance, misalignment and looseness patterns early, and writes a plain Persian work-order suggestion with severity and time left. The value is avoided breakdowns and planned repairs, not labour: the walk-around labour replaced is a technician taking readings for one machine: 45 minutes [A], 107,267 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), and the plans work out at 300,000, 250,000 and 200,000 toman a machine-month, 279.7%, 233.1% and 186.5% of that cost [D], so the price has to be justified by downtime avoided, which I did not quantify. Foreign anchors: cloud maintenance software with IoT integration $3 to $15 per asset per month; a 50-asset site $35,000 to $75,000 installed and $8,000 to $18,000 a year ongoing; claims of 25% to 30% lower maintenance cost and 6 to 14 months payback are attributed to named studies but are not verified on the page (oxmaint.com, 28 May 2026, vendor blog [S]).
Direct sales to maintenance managers, partnerships with motor and pump dealers and repair shops [A], industrial exhibitions, and a 2-machine free pilot per site.
Site survey and installation support; monthly report by a reliability engineer for large sites; 1 support engineer per 40 sites [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans per site: Small with 5 machines 1,500,000 toman (about $5.65), Mid with 20 machines 5,000,000 (about $18.85), Large with 100 machines 20,000,000 (about $75.39) [A, no price was found]. Mix 50% / 35% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 5,500,000 toman a month (about $20.73) [D]. Sites have 90% of their machines connected [A], so 22.05 machine-months a site [D]. 5% monthly churn [A]. Hardware is sold at cost and is not in the model.

Anomaly-detection models on one 48 GB GPU node (150M toman a month [S]), a data pipeline for sensor streams, sensors and gateways bought for resale; 2 engineers at 50M, 1 reliability engineer at 50M and 1 support engineer at 40M, gross [A].
Sensor sourcing and testing, site installation and baselining, model tuning per machine type, alert tuning to avoid false alarms, selling to maintenance managers.
Sensor suppliers (none confirmed), motor and pump service firms, a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 233.7M toman a month ((50M + 50M + 40M + 50M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 441.7M toman a month (about $1,665) [D]; one-time setup 300M [A] (about $1,131) for test sensors and demo kit. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 20,000 toman per machine-month for data connection, alerts and storage [A], compute time, and an added GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 reliability engineer at 50M + 1 support engineer at 40M, gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[A] feature extraction on about 4,300 vibration windows, anomaly scoring and report; no benchmark found
[D] 90% connected [A] of the 5 / 20 / 100 machines, weighted by plan mix
[D] after compute, data cost and 1% gateway

cost_model.x: One node serves about 269 sites including 2 free pilot machines each [D: 6,480 ÷ (22.05 + 2)], so the base case fits on one node and the optimistic case needs a second near month 24 [D, from the model]. The GPU node is 34.0% of fixed cost [D: 150M ÷ 441.7M]. The 120-second compute time is a guess; sensor-data models are often cheaper on CPU, which I did not test.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 88 paying sites on the fixed-cost formula [D: 441.7M ÷ (5,500,000 × 0.99 − 22.05 × 20,000) = 88.3], and stepping through site counts with support staff and node steps gives 108 on one node [D]. Sites ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 300M setup falls in month 1.

Site counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −8,357M toman in the conservative case, −5,489M in the base case and +1,053M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per site at 5% churn is about 100.08M toman, about $377.24 [D: (5,500,000 × 0.99 − 22.05 × 20,000) ÷ 0.05].

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 120 sites at 5% monthly churn [A], which needs 6 replacements a month and the ramp adds about 7 [D], so about 13 gross additions a month at month 24. With 40M of marketing that is about 3.16M toman (about $11.91) per site [D], which is very low for an industrial sale needing site visits and a pilot; the model does not stress marketing or the cost of installation visits, so the base case is likely too favourable.

risks.x: Hardware: sensors are imported goods under sanctions and exchange-rate swings; I did not verify supply, price or a domestic source, and the customer's hardware outlay is far larger than the subscription.
Detection quality: models trained on public rigs generalise poorly to other machines; alerts that miss a failure or cry wolf end the contract.
Value case: the price is above the labour replaced, so sales rest on avoided downtime that depends on each plant's cost of stoppage, which I did not quantify.
Installation cost: site visits, mounting and baselining are not in the model; the vendor blog gives $80 to $200 a node [S, unverified].
Connectivity and data location: plants may refuse cloud data and ask for on-premises edge units, which changes the cost model.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian plants with rotating assets worth monitoring, by size and sector.
Availability and price of vibration sensors and gateways in Iran.
Iranian prices for condition-monitoring services.
Detection accuracy on Iranian plant machinery and typical cost of unplanned stoppage.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 28 Oct 2026.

title: بازرسی کیفیت مبتنی بر دوربین
segment: سازمانی، صنعتی و نهادی B2B
engine: موتور ۲: استخراج اسناد، بینایی و OCR فارسی

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: کارخانه‌ها (سازمانی، صنعتی و نهادی B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: ۳ تا ۴ بازرس چشمی در هر شیفت (۸۰ میلیون تومان در ماه). پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۳۲ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۱۴ پایه، ۱۰ رشد، ۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۴٫۰٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «۳ تا ۴ بازرس چشمی در هر شیفت (۸۰ میلیون تومان در ماه)» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: بازرس بینایی عیب سطح، بسته‌بندی و چاپ برچسب به‌صورت لحظه‌ای؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق دوربین‌های صنعتی GigE/USB3 و GPU لبه محلی به‌همراه ۰٫۸۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۸٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۵۶٬۴۰۴٬۰۶۲ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۰٫۹۱ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر خط): پایه ۶٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۱۵٬۹۰۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۲۶٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۱٬۸۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۱۵٬۶۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۶٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۴۸۲٬۰۸۶٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۳۶ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۵۴٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۱۶٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B تنظیم‌شده + PaddleOCR فارسی + پردازشگر پسین سفارشی جلالی/ارقام روی GPU داخلی. مجموعه داده: بازرس بینایی عیب سطح، بسته‌بندی و چاپ برچسب به‌صورت لحظه‌ای.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی بازرس بینایی عیب سطح، بسته‌بندی و چاپ برچسب به‌صورت لحظه‌ای؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های دوربین‌های صنعتی GigE/USB3 و GPU لبه محلی در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: دوربین‌های صنعتی GigE/USB3 و GPU لبه محلی. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

bmc.title: ساختار هزینه (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: هزینه کامل مستقل: ۴۳۵٬۰۴۵٬۰۸۲ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA مستقل: ۸۰٬۵۵۴٬۹۱۸ تومان/ماه (۱۵٫۶٪). هزینه سبد موتور مشترک (تقسیم توسعه/دفتر بین ۳ ابزار هم‌خانواده): ۳۵۰٬۳۲۵٬۰۸۲ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA سبد: ۱۶۵٬۲۷۴٬۹۱۸ تومان/ماه (۳۲٫۱٪).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal on the numbers and fragile, because the cost is dominated by GPU inference in the cloud. The base case (90 paying lines at month 24) breaks even in month 14 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −1,369M toman, about $5,160), and it needs 12 GPU nodes by then, about 70% of monthly cost [D]. The conservative case (30 lines) never breaks even (cumulative −6,652M) and the optimistic case (240 lines) breaks even in month 8 and ends at +11,862M cumulative [D]. A doubled GPU price or 30% lower prices push the base case below break-even; half the customers still reaches break-even in month 22 with +6M a month at month 24 [D]. Line counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian production lines that would pay for inspection. Gross margin on the larger plans is only 26.3% to 47.1% [D], and this model sends every image to our GPUs; running inference on a box at the factory would cut that cost but needs hardware I did not price. Accuracy is unproven on Iranian products: the public benchmark result (99.1 image-level AUROC on MVTec AD, 95.5 with 16 normal images [S]) is for clean test sets, not for a changing production line. Cameras, lighting and mounting are bought by the customer and are not in the model.

r: (a) Small lines in packaging, food and plastics checking about 100,000 images a month. (b) Mid-size lines in auto parts, tiles and appliances at about 500,000 images. (c) High-speed lines at about 2,000,000 images [A]. Pool: no count of Iranian lines by industry was found; the plan sizes and mix are [A]. 90 paying lines at month 24 is [A].

The factory mounts a camera at a station; the tool learns what a good part looks like from a few dozen photos (PatchCore reaches 95.5 image AUROC from 16 normal images on its benchmark [S, arxiv 2106.08265]), flags defects with a heat-map, counts and logs rejects per shift, and sends a reject signal or an alert. The labour replaced is a human inspector reviewing 1,000 images at about 10 seconds each: 167 minutes [A], 398,081 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 100,000, 70,000 and 50,000 toman per 1,000 images, 25.1%, 17.6% and 12.6% of that cost [D]. Foreign anchors are vendor-marketing figures that disagree with each other: year-one software licence $4,000 to $18,000 per station (about $333 to $1,500 a month [D]), model training $1,500 to $6,000 per defect class, integration $4,000 to $45,000, ongoing 10% to 20% of deployment a year, payback 7 to 17 months with no case data (ifactoryapp.com, 25 Aug 2026 [S]).
Direct sales to plant managers and quality heads, system integrators and automation firms [A], industrial exhibitions, and a free pilot of 20,000 images.
Pilot and model training with a vision engineer; monthly review of reject rates; 1 support engineer per 15 lines (onboarding is heavy) [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans per line: Line S with 100,000 images 10,000,000 toman (about $37.69), Line M with 500,000 images 35,000,000 (about $131.93), Line L with 2,000,000 images 100,000,000 (about $376.94) [A, no price was found]. Mix 50% / 35% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 32,250,000 toman a month (about $121.56) [D]. Lines use 80% of their images [A], so 420 thousand-image units a line a month [D]. 4% monthly churn [A]. Hardware and installation are the customer's cost.

An anomaly-detection and classification model stack on GPU nodes at 150M toman a month each [S]; an image-ingest service; 2 computer-vision engineers at 60M, 1 integration engineer at 50M and 1 support engineer at 40M, gross [A].
Pilot training per product, lighting and camera advice, threshold tuning, rejection logic and PLC integration support, drift monitoring, selling to plant managers.
Automation integrators, camera and lighting suppliers (none confirmed), a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month ((60M + 60M + 50M + 40M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), first GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 50M = 476.3M toman a month (about $1,795) [D]; one-time setup 300M [A] (about $1,131). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 3,000 toman per 1,000 images for storage and transfer [A], and one added GPU node for each 3,535 units of load at 30% utilisation.
[D] (2 CV engineers at 60M + 1 integration engineer at 50M + 1 support engineer at 40M, gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S, A] PatchCore-10% takes 0.22 s an image on a GPU in the paper (Table 5); assumed equal on this GPU
[D] 80% use [A] of the 100 / 500 / 2,000 thousand images, weighted by plan mix
62.6% Line S, 47.1% Line M, 26.3% Line L
[D] team 258.3M + first GPU node 150M + infrastructure 10M + accounting 8M + marketing 50M

cost_model.x: One node serves only about 8 lines including the 20 free units each [D: 3,535 ÷ (420 + 20)], so the base case needs 12 nodes at month 24 and the optimistic case 30 [D, from the model]; in the base case 12 nodes cost 1,800M toman a month, about 70% of that month's total cost of 2,564M [D: 12 × 150M ÷ 2,564M]. The break-even formula below ignores the node steps, so the stepped figure is the useful one.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 16 paying lines on the fixed-cost formula [D: 476.3M ÷ (32,250,000 × 0.99 − 420 × 3,000) = 15.5, which counts the 150M node once], and stepping through line counts with support staff and node steps gives 39 on 5 nodes [D]. Lines ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 300M setup falls in month 1.

Line counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −6,652M toman in the conservative case, −1,369M in the base case and +11,862M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per line at 4% churn is about 766.69M toman, about $2,890 [D: (32,250,000 × 0.99 − 420 × 3,000) ÷ 0.04]; this treats compute as a cost per unit and so already includes GPU nodes.

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 90 lines at 4% monthly churn [A], which needs about 4 replacements a month and the ramp adds 5 [D], so about 9 gross additions a month at month 24. With 50M of marketing that is about 5.8M toman (about $21.90) per line [D], which is very low for a sale that needs a pilot and a site visit; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable.

risks.x: GPU cost: the service is as cheap as its inference; cloud inference on every image is the model's largest cost, and doubling the GPU price makes the base case lose 1,461M a month at month 24 [D].
Edge versus cloud: factories may refuse to send images out or lack bandwidth; an on-site box shifts hardware cost to the customer or to us, and I did not price it.
Accuracy on real lines: public benchmarks use clean images; lighting, vibration and product changes degrade results, and false rejects cost the customer money.
Hardware and sanctions: industrial cameras, lenses and lighting are imported; availability and price in Iran were not verified.
Price anchor: the foreign figures come from vendor marketing that disagrees with itself; domestic prices were assumed and not tested.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian production lines that run visual inspection manually, by industry.
Prices and availability of industrial cameras, lenses and lighting in Iran.
Detection accuracy and false-reject rate on Iranian production lines.
Inference speed on the RTX 6000 Ada for the chosen model, and edge-box costs.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 28 Oct 2026.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the demand and the content rights are unproven. The base case (3,000 paying seats at month 24) breaks even in month 5, peaks at a cash need of 1,350M toman (about $5,090) and reaches +59,556M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (900 seats) breaks even in month 9 and ends at +11,155M cumulative; the optimistic case (9,000 seats) breaks even in month 4 and ends at +197,107M [D]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 6, prices 30% lower in month 6, and half the seats in month 7 [D]. The reason is the low unit cost: a question costs about 1,861 toman to serve (about $0.007) against about 47,674 toman of engineer time to find the same clause by hand [D]. Seat counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian engineering firms, factories or engineers who work from standards, so no pool supports them. The larger blockers are rights and quality. ISIRI (INSO) standards are sold documents, and I could not verify whether their text may be indexed and quoted in a commercial product; the Persian answer quality on technical clauses is also untested. Without a licence, the service can only index the customer's own copies and internal manuals, which fits the per-seat model but narrows the pitch.

r: (a) Engineering consultancies, contractors and factories that work to ISIRI, ISO and IEC standards and keep internal procedures and equipment manuals. (b) Quality and safety departments in plants. Seats are bought by the firm. Pool: I found no count of such firms or engineers; the 3,000-seat base case is [A] and is about 100 firms of 30 seats.

An engineer asks a question in Persian or English and gets the clause, the page and the quote, from the standards and manuals the firm has uploaded or licensed, with a link back to the source page. The labour replaced is searching and reading: 20 minutes per lookup [A], which is 47,674 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 15,000, 10,000 and 7,500 toman a question, 31.5%, 21.0% and 15.7% of that cost [D]. Foreign anchor: Glean does not publish prices; a competitor blog reports from about $50 per user per month, minimum 100 to 250 users, a minimum annual contract of about $50,000 to $60,000 and a Vendr median contract of $98,890 a year (eesel.ai, published 1 Oct 2025, edited 5 Oct 2026 [S, third-party estimates]). $50 is about 13,264,750 toman at 265,295 [D].
Direct sales to quality managers and engineering heads, standards-consultancy firms as resellers [A], industrial and engineering conferences, a free 10-question trial per seat.
Self-serve onboarding with document upload; a monthly review of unanswered questions to fix retrieval; 1 support person per 300 seats [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Per-seat monthly plans: Starter with 100 questions 1,500,000 toman (about $5.65), Pro with 300 questions 3,000,000 (about $11.31), Team with 800 questions 6,000,000 (about $22.62) [A, no domestic price was found]. Mix 45% / 40% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 2,775,000 toman a seat a month (about $10.46) [D]. Seats use 60% of their quota [A], so 171 questions a seat a month [D]. 3% monthly churn [A].

A retrieval pipeline (document parsing with Persian and table handling, embeddings, reranking) and a 30B-class model on GPU nodes at 150M toman a month each [S]; 2 ML engineers at 60M, 1 integration engineer at 50M and 1 support person at 30M, gross [A].
Document ingestion and OCR of scanned standards, citation checking, evaluation on a question set written with engineers, access control per firm, selling and onboarding.
Standards publishers or INSO for a content licence (none confirmed), a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 246.0M toman a month ((60M + 60M + 50M + 30M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), first GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 60M = 474.0M toman a month (about $1,787) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (about $942). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 500 toman a question for embeddings and storage [A], and one added GPU node for each 609 seats at 30% utilisation.

cost_model.x: One node serves about 609 seats including the 10 free trial questions each [D: 110,256 ÷ (171 + 10)], so the base case needs 5 nodes at month 24 and the optimistic case 15 [D, from the model]; in the base case 5 nodes cost 750M toman a month, about 42% of that month's total cost of 1,783M [D: 5 × 150M ÷ 1,783M].

revenue.x: Break-even is about 178 paying seats on the fixed-cost formula [D: 474.0M ÷ (2,775,000 × 0.99 − 171 × 500)], and stepping through seat counts with support staff and node steps gives 179 on 1 node [D]. Seats ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Seat counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is +11,155M toman in the conservative case, +59,556M in the base case and +197,107M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per seat at 3% churn is about 88.73M toman, about $334 [D: (2,775,000 × 0.99 − 171 × 500) ÷ 0.03].

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 3,000 seats at 3% monthly churn [A], which needs about 90 replacements a month and the ramp adds about 167, so about 257 gross additions a month at month 24 [D]. With 60M of marketing that is about 233,000 toman (about $0.88) a seat [D], very low for a business-to-business sale; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable. Because the margin is so high, the result depends on seats and content rights far more than on compute.

risks.x: Content rights: standards are copyrighted publications; without a licence from INSO or another publisher the product can index only the customer's own copies and manuals, which may be too narrow for the pitch.

Answer accuracy: a wrong clause cited in a design or an audit is costly; retrieval quality on Persian technical text, tables and scanned pages is unmeasured here, and customers will want exact quotes with page links.
Seat pool: the number of firms that buy per-seat tools for engineers is unknown, and free general assistants compete on the same question.
Data security: factories and defence-linked firms may refuse cloud upload of internal manuals, pushing demand to on-premises installs (see #99), which this model does not price.
Price anchor: the foreign figure is a competitor's estimate of a vendor that does not publish prices; domestic prices were assumed and not tested.

title: تولیدکننده گزارش مهندسی از داده آزمون و شبیه‌سازی
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: مشاوران مهندسی (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: ۳ تا ۵ روز زمان مهندس ارشد برای قالب‌بندی گزارش آزمون. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۷۴ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۷۲ پایه، ۷۴ رشد، ۲۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۱۱٫۰٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «۳ تا ۵ روز زمان مهندس ارشد برای قالب‌بندی گزارش آزمون» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: تولید خودکار برگه محاسبات، تفسیر نمودار و متن فنی فارسی؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق ورود CSV از ANSYS/SolidWorks/Lab به Word/LaTeX فارسی به‌همراه ۰٫۴۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۲٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۴۲٬۷۵۵٬۷۷۰ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۰۱ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the customer pool is unsourced and the conservative case is only marginal. The base case (150 paying consultancies at month 24) breaks even in month 9, peaks at a cash need of 2,279M toman (about $8,589) and reaches +9,239M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (45 consultancies) breaks even in month 20 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −4,534M); the optimistic case (360) breaks even in month 6 and ends at +36,454M [D]. Every sensitivity stays profitable, with break-even in month 12 for a doubled GPU price, month 13 for prices 30% lower and month 14 for half the customers [D]. Compute is not the issue: one GPU node covers about 871 customers, so the base case runs on one node [D]. The risks are demand and trust. I found no count of Iranian engineering consultancies or test labs, so the customer counts are assumptions. The product writes the narrative and tables around numbers the engineer supplies; for certification-grade reports a signing engineer must still check every figure, and a language model that mis-states a number is a liability. The model prices one generic report type; each new report format (a test standard, a simulation template) needs engineering time that I covered only with the three-person team.

r: (a) Engineering consultancies and design offices that issue test, analysis or simulation reports. (b) Testing and calibration laboratories. (c) R&D departments in plants. The engineer uploads test data (CSV or instrument export) or simulation results and a report template; the tool computes summary statistics, draws the plots, drafts the method, results and conclusion text in Persian or English, and exports a DOCX with captions, table numbers and units checked against the data. The labour replaced is writing the report: 4 hours per report [A], which is 572,092 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The packs work out at 300,000, 250,000 and 200,000 toman a report, 52.4%, 43.7% and 35.0% of that cost [D]. No foreign price anchor for a comparable product was found.

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: سایت‌های صنعتی (سازمانی، صنعتی و نهادی B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: افزایش تعرفه گاز/برق صنعتی و جریمه پیک. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۲۹ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۹ پایه، ۱۶ رشد، ۴ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۴٫۰٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «افزایش تعرفه گاز/برق صنعتی و جریمه پیک» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: بهینه‌ساز پیک‌سایی، توان راکتیو و زمان‌بندی حرارتی؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق کنتور هوشمند، BMS و تجزیه‌گر قبض توانیر به‌همراه ۰٫۸۵ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۵٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۴۵٬۲۴۳٬۹۴۸ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۰٫۸۰ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (ماهانه + سهم از صرفه‌جویی): پایه ۶٬۷۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۱۵٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۲۸٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۲٬۵۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۴۹۶٬۳۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۶٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۴۶۴٬۰۴۰٬۵۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۱۸ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۲۷٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۱۹٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: LightGBM / Prophet با فصلیت جلالی + حل‌کننده قید OR-Tools + توضیح‌دهنده Qwen3-8B روی CPU/GPU مشترک. مجموعه داده: بهینه‌ساز پیک‌سایی، توان راکتیو و زمان‌بندی حرارتی.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی بهینه‌ساز پیک‌سایی، توان راکتیو و زمان‌بندی حرارتی؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های کنتور هوشمند، BMS و تجزیه‌گر قبض توانیر در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: کنتور هوشمند، BMS و تجزیه‌گر قبض توانیر. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal on the numbers, and the value case rests on energy savings I could not price. The base case (75 paying sites at month 24) breaks even in month 12, peaks at a cash need of 2,392M toman (about $9,017) and reaches +3,491M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (24 sites) reaches break-even only in month 24 and ends at −4,856M cumulative; the optimistic case (180 sites) breaks even in month 7 and ends at +19,763M [D]. Break-even in the base case slips to month 13 with doubled compute prices, month 14 with prices 30% lower and month 17 with half the sites [D]. The plans are priced at 116.5% to 186.5% of the cost of an engineer's hour per daily run [D], so labour saved does not justify them; the service must pay for itself through lower energy bills. At an assumed 5% saving, a Site S plan needs an energy bill of at least 160M toman a month (about $603) and Site L at least 1,000M (about $3,770) to break even for the customer [D], but I could not retrieve Iranian industrial electricity or gas tariffs, so I cannot say how many sites meet that. Site counts are assumptions, with no sourced pool. The savings-share fee named in the service list is not modelled; it is possible upside and would need metering the customer accepts as proof. The model runs on CPU servers, not GPUs.

r: (a) Small sites: greenhouses, workshops and commercial buildings with one or two meters. (b) Mid-size plants with several zones or production lines. (c) Large industrial sites with sub-metering. Pool: I found no count of Iranian sites with smart meters or building-management systems; 75 paying sites at month 24 is [A]. The only sourced figure is a national saving potential of 190 million barrels of oil equivalent a year in Iranian industry (eceee 2014 summer-study paper, undated figure [S]), which gives no per-site number.

The tool reads meter and sensor data, forecasts load, and each day recommends or sends schedules (pump and compressor start times, greenhouse heating and lighting, chiller set-points) that cut peak demand and waste, with alerts when a site drifts from its normal pattern. The labour replaced is an energy engineer reviewing a day of data: 60 minutes [A], 143,023 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 266,667, 200,000 and 166,667 toman a run, 186.5%, 139.8% and 116.5% of that cost [D], so the labour comparison does not support the price and the saving must. No foreign price anchor was found.
Direct sales to plant managers and greenhouse owners, energy-audit consultants as resellers [A], industrial-estate associations, and a free 10-run trial.
Onboarding with a meter-integration engineer; monthly savings report; 1 support person per 20 sites (integration is heavy) [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans per site: Site S with 30 runs 8,000,000 toman (about $30.16), Site M with 100 runs 20,000,000 (about $75.39), Site L with 300 runs 50,000,000 (about $188.47) [A, no price was found]. Mix 50% / 35% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 18,500,000 toman a site a month (about $69.73) [D]. Sites use 90% of their runs [A], so 85.5 runs a site a month [D]. 3% monthly churn [A]. No savings-share fee is included.

A load-forecasting and schedule-optimisation engine on CPU servers (3 servers, 51M toman a month [A, from Arvan EUR54 a month for a 4-vCPU server at 300,000 toman per euro, rounded to 17M each]); 3 engineers at 60M and 1 support person at 30M, gross [A].
Meter and sensor integration, forecasting per site type, constraint modelling of pumps and heating, savings measurement, selling.
Meter and sensor suppliers and integrators (none confirmed), energy-audit consultants, a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month ((60M + 60M + 60M + 30M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), compute 51M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 50M = 377.3M toman a month (about $1,422) [D]; one-time setup 300M [A] (about $1,131). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 1,000 toman a run for storage and alerts [A], and one added 3-server group for each 68 sites at 30% utilisation.

cost_model.x: One compute group serves about 68 sites including 10 free trial runs each [D: 6,480 ÷ (85.5 + 10)], so the base case needs 2 groups at month 24 and the optimistic case 3 [D, from the model]; in the base case 2 groups cost 102M toman a month, about 18% of that month's total cost of 559M [D]. People and marketing dominate cost.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 21 paying sites on the fixed-cost formula [D: 377.3M ÷ (18,500,000 × 0.99 − 85.5 × 1,000) = 20.7], and stepping through site counts with support staff gives 23 on 1 group [D]. Sites ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 300M setup falls in month 1.

Site counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −4,856M toman in the conservative case, +3,491M in the base case and +19,763M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per site at 3% churn is about 607.65M toman, about $2,290 [D: (18,500,000 × 0.99 − 85.5 × 1,000) ÷ 0.03].

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 75 sites at 3% monthly churn [A], which needs about 2 replacements a month and the ramp adds about 4, so about 6 gross additions a month at month 24 [D]. With 50M of marketing that is about 7.8M toman (about $29.4) per site [D], low for a sale that needs meter integration; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable.

risks.x: Unproven savings: the whole case rests on the customer saving more than the fee; the 5% saving used for the check above is an assumption, and a site that has already tuned its schedules saves less.
Tariff structure: how much a shifted load saves depends on Iranian industrial tariffs, subsidies and supply cuts, which I could not retrieve.
Metering and integration: many sites lack interval meters or open interfaces; sensor installation is a hardware and integration cost not in the model.
Control risk: sending schedules to pumps or heaters can disrupt production; customers may accept recommendations only, which weakens the savings.
Savings-share contracts need an agreed baseline; disputes are likely and the revenue is not modelled.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: Iranian industrial electricity and gas tariffs, and how many sites have interval meters or building-management systems.
The saving a site would actually achieve; no case study with Iranian data was found.

bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (ماهانه): پایه ۱٬۵۵۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۳۱۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۴۴۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۶۷۵٬۶۸۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۶۴۵٬۲۷۴٬۴۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۲۴ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۳۶٬۰۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۵٬۹۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: LightGBM / Prophet با فصلیت جلالی + حل‌کننده قید OR-Tools + توضیح‌دهنده Qwen3-8B روی CPU/GPU مشترک. مجموعه داده: موتور تطبیق معادل (SKF/Timken/Bosch به معادل چینی/داخلی).

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی موتور تطبیق معادل (SKF/Timken/Bosch به معادل چینی/داخلی)؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های نرم‌افزار CMMS/انبار (همکاران سیستم/سپیدار) در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: نرم‌افزار CMMS/انبار (همکاران سیستم/سپیدار). زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal-thin. The base case (90 paying plants at month 24) breaks even in month 14 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −450M toman, about $1,696), with a peak cash need of 2,947M (about $11,107) [D]. The conservative case (30 plants) never breaks even and ends at −5,814M cumulative; the optimistic case (240 plants) breaks even in month 8 and ends at +12,343M [D]. In the base case, doubled compute prices move break-even to month 15, prices 30% lower to month 19 and half the plants to month 22, with month-24 profit of only +69M in the last case [D]. Plant counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian plants that run a maintenance store with usable part-usage history. The service also depends on data the customer must export from a maintenance or accounting system, and on a catalogue of alternative suppliers and equivalent parts that I could not find or price; the alternative-sourcing half of the product is therefore not costed. Price pressure is real because the larger plans cost only 16.1% of a planner's time per 100-part refresh [D], leaving little room to discount. The service runs on CPU servers, not GPUs.

r: (a) Small plants and workshops with about 500 stocked parts. (b) Mid-size plants with about 3,000. (c) Large plants, mines and fleets with about 15,000 [A]. Pool: I found no count of Iranian plants with a maintenance store and digital part records; 90 paying plants at month 24 is [A].

The tool reads part-usage history, forecasts intermittent demand per part, recommends reorder points and safety stock, flags dead stock, and lets the planner ask for an equivalent part or another supplier. The labour replaced is a planner reviewing 100 parts: 120 minutes [A], 286,046 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 200,000, 92,308 and 46,154 toman per 100-part refresh, 69.9%, 32.3% and 16.1% of that cost [D]. No foreign price anchor was found: the pages I read on spare-parts forecasting gave no prices (oxmaint.com, 7 Oct 2026 [S]).

Direct sales to maintenance and procurement managers, CMMS and accounting-software vendors as integration partners [A], industrial exhibitions, and a free forecast on one year of the plant's own data.
Data onboarding from the plant's maintenance system; quarterly review of stock-outs and dead stock; 1 support person per 25 plants [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans per plant: Plant S with 500 parts and 20 refreshes 4,000,000 toman (about $15.08), Plant M with 3,000 parts and 130 refreshes 12,000,000 (about $45.23), Plant L with 15,000 parts and 650 refreshes 30,000,000 (about $113.08) [A, no price was found]. Mix 50% / 35% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 10,700,000 toman a plant a month (about $40.33) [D]. Plants use 90% of their refreshes [A], so 137.7 refreshes a plant a month [D]. 3.5% monthly churn [A].

A forecasting engine for intermittent demand and an alternative-part matching index, run on CPU servers (3 servers, 51M toman a month [A, from Arvan EUR54 a month for a 4-vCPU server at 300,000 toman per euro, rounded to 17M each]); 3 engineers at 60M and 1 support person at 30M, gross [A].
Data import and cleaning, forecast back-testing per customer, safety-stock calculation, alternative-part and supplier matching, selling.

Maintenance and accounting software vendors, parts suppliers for the alternative-sourcing data (none confirmed), a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month ((60M + 60M + 60M + 30M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), compute 51M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 367.3M toman a month (about $1,384) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (about $942). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 500 toman a refresh for storage and alerts [A], and one added 3-server group for each 82 plants at 30% utilisation.

cost_model.x: One compute group serves about 82 plants including 20 free trial refreshes each [D: 12,960 ÷ (137.7 + 20)], so the base case needs 2 groups at month 24 and the optimistic case 3 [D, from the model]; in the base case 2 groups cost 102M toman a month, about 19% of that month's total cost of 545M [D]. People and marketing dominate cost.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 35 paying plants on the fixed-cost formula [D: 367.3M ÷ (10,700,000 × 0.99 − 137.7 × 500) = 34.9], and stepping through plant counts with support staff gives 39 on 1 group [D]. Plants ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Plant counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −5,814M toman in the conservative case, −450M in the base case and +12,343M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per plant at 3.5% churn is about 300.69M toman, about $1,133 [D: (10,700,000 × 0.99 − 137.7 × 500) ÷ 0.035].

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 90 plants at 3.5% monthly churn [A], which needs about 3 replacements a month and the ramp adds 5, so about 8 gross additions a month at month 24 [D]. With 40M of marketing that is about 4.9M toman (about $18.5) per plant [D], low for a sale that needs a data import; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable.

risks.x: Data quality: many plants keep part usage on paper or in spreadsheets with inconsistent part names; forecast quality depends on history that may not exist.

Alternative-sourcing data: equivalent-part and supplier matching needs a catalogue I could not find; sanctions and import restrictions change supply month to month, so even a good catalogue ages quickly.
Forecast limits: spare-part demand is intermittent and often driven by breakdowns; accuracy gains over a planner's rule of thumb are unproven here.
Small price room: the larger plans are priced at 16.1% of planner time, so discounting or free substitutes hit margin quickly.
Plant pool: the number of plants that keep digital part records is unknown.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian plants with a maintenance store and digital part records.
Any competitor product or price for spare-parts forecasting, in Iran or abroad.
The forecast accuracy gain over a planner's reorder rules; no benchmark with Iranian data was found.
A catalogue of equivalent parts and local suppliers for alternative sourcing.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 28 Oct 2026.

replaces: زیان محصول و مصرف بیش‌ازحد سموم وارداتی گران
gtm: ربات عکس بله/ایتا/تلگرام و اپ کافه‌بازار
driver: طبقه‌بند بینایی آفات گندم، پسته، گوجه و مرکبات ایران
dataset: Vision classifier for Iranian wheat, pistachio, tomato & citrus pests
stack: Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B تنظیم‌شده + PaddleOCR فارسی + پردازشگر پسین سفارشی جلالی/ارقام روی GPU داخلی
infrastructure: Sindad/Afranet (GPU/NIN), Zarinpal/PayPing (Shaparak gateway), and Vice-Presidency for Science & Technology (Danesh-Bonyan Type 1/2 tax exemption)
dist_partners: Bale/Eitaa/Telegram photo bot + Cafe Bazaar app
support_scope: human-in-the-loop edge cases and SAYAD/Shaparak billing follow-ups

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but willingness to pay and diagnosis accuracy are unproven and the revenue per farmer is tiny. The base case (12,000 paying farmers at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,989M toman (about $7,499) and reaches +29,029M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (3,000 farmers) breaks even in month 15 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −1,223M, about $4,610); the optimistic case (30,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +91,357M [D]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 9, prices 30% lower in month 10 and half the farmers in month 12 [D]. Average revenue is only 570,000 toman a farmer a month (about $2.15) [D], so the model needs thousands of paying users, and I found no count of Iranian farmers who would pay for an app; the customer counts are assumptions. Usage is assumed at 50% of quota because disease problems are seasonal, and churn at 8% a month. Accuracy is the central risk: a competitor review says the best-known apps struggle with rare conditions and regional variants and should be treated as screening tools (flypix.ai, 9 Jun 2026 [S]), and I have no Iranian crop-image dataset. The model sends photos to our GPUs; one node serves about 4,700 farmers [D]. Spraying advice for pesticides sold in Iran needs a product list I did not find.

r: (a) Individual farmers and orchardists with a smartphone. (b) Larger growers and greenhouses. (c) Cooperatives and agricultural service offices that buy for their members. Pool: I could not retrieve a count of Iranian agricultural holdings or farmers (the FAO census pages found were old and the Tehran Times greenhouse article was blocked); 12,000 paying farmers at month 24 is [A].

The farmer photographs a leaf or fruit; the tool names the likely disease or pest, gives treatment and prevention steps in Persian, and logs the case by location so co-ops see outbreaks. The labour replaced is an agronomist consultation: 30 minutes [A], 71,512 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 10,000, 6,250 and 6,000 toman a diagnosis, 14.0%, 8.7% and 8.4% of that cost [D]. Foreign anchor: Agrio is freemium with undisclosed prices (flypix.ai, 9 Jun 2026 [S]); I found no published price for Plantix.
Cooperatives and agricultural service offices [A], extension agents, Telegram and Instagram groups of farmers, agri-input shops, app stores (Cafe Bazaar and Myket), and 3 free diagnoses per user.
Self-serve app with a phone-support line for co-ops; seasonal campaigns; 1 support person per 300 customers [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans: Farmer with 20 diagnoses 200,000 toman (about $0.75), Farmer Pro with 80 diagnoses 500,000 (about $1.88), Co-op with 500 diagnoses 3,000,000 (about $11.31) [A, no domestic price was found]. Mix 60% / 30% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 570,000 toman a customer a month (about $2.15) [D]. Users use 50% of their quota [A], so 43.0 diagnoses a customer a month [D]. 8% monthly churn [A]. Store and payment fees 10% of revenue [A].

A crop-disease image classifier fine-tuned on collected Iranian crop images plus an advice generator, on GPU nodes at 150M toman a month each [S]; 2 ML engineers at 60M, 1 agronomist at 40M and 1 support person at 25M, gross [A].
Collecting and labelling crop-disease photos with agronomists, model retraining per crop and region, advice content in Persian, outbreak mapping, selling through co-ops.
Agricultural universities and research centres for labelled data (none confirmed), cooperatives, agri-input retailers, app stores, a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway.

Fixed: team 227.55M toman a month ((60M + 60M + 25M + 40M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), first GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 150M = 545.55M toman a month (about $2,056) [D]; one-time setup 300M [A] (about $1,131). Variable: store and payment fees 10% of revenue [A], 300 toman a diagnosis for storage and messages [A], and one added GPU node for each 4,696 customers at 25% utilisation.
[D] (2 ML engineers at 60M + 1 agronomist at 40M + 1 support person at 25M, gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[A] classifier about 0.1 s plus 1,500-token advice on an 8B-class model about 0.7 s, plus decode and queueing, rounded up
[D] 50% use [A] of the 20 / 80 / 500 quotas, weighted by plan mix
[D] team 227.55M + first GPU node 150M + infrastructure 10M + accounting 8M + marketing 150M

cost_model.x: One node serves about 4,696 customers including 3 free trial diagnoses each [D: 216,000 ÷ (43.0 + 3)], so the base case needs 3 nodes at month 24 and the optimistic case 7 [D, from the model]; in the base case 3 nodes cost 450M toman a month, about 15% of that month's total cost of 2,914M [D]. Marketing, support and fees dominate cost.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 1,091 paying farmers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 545.55M ÷ (570,000 × 0.90 − 43.0 × 300) = 1,090.9], and stepping through customer counts with support staff and node steps gives 1,337 on 1 node [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 300M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −1,223M toman in the conservative case, +29,029M in the base case and +91,357M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per customer at 8% churn is about 6.25M toman, about $23.56 [D: (570,000 × 0.90 − 43.0 × 300) ÷ 0.08].

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 12,000 farmers at 8% monthly churn [A], which needs about 960 replacements a month and the ramp adds about 750, so about 1,710 gross additions a month at month 24 [D]. With 150M of marketing that is about 87,700 toman (about $0.33) per farmer [D], very low for reaching farmers one by one; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable unless co-ops sign up members in bulk.

risks.x: Accuracy: diagnosis quality on Iranian crops, varieties and photo conditions is unproven, and a wrong diagnosis costs a farmer a crop or a spraying round.
Willingness to pay: farmers have free alternatives (agronomist calls, Telegram groups, free app tiers); 200,000 toman a month is an assumption.
Seasonality: usage and subscriptions fall outside the growing season, so 8% monthly churn and 50% quota use may both be optimistic.
Data: labelled Iranian crop-disease photos must be collected; the 300M setup does not cover a national dataset.
Treatment advice: recommending pesticides needs a product and regulation list for Iran that I could not verify, and liability for harmful advice.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian farmers, orchardists and greenhouse operators, and how many use smartphones for farm work.
Detection accuracy on Iranian crops; no local dataset or benchmark was found.
Prices of Plantix or Agrio subscriptions, and any Iranian competitor.
App-store and payment fees for Iranian stores (10% is assumed).
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 28 Oct 2026.

title: مشاور آبیاری و مصرف آب
segment: کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B
engine: موتور ۴: شاخص‌بندی تورم، قیمت‌گذاری و پیش‌بینی تقاضا

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: مزارع و گلخانه‌ها (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: تخلیه آب چاه و هزینه برق پمپ. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۶۴ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۷۰ پایه، ۷۶ رشد، ۱۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۶٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «تخلیه آب چاه و هزینه برق پمپ» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: زمان‌بند تبخیر-تعرق و کم‌آبیاری برای استان‌های خشک؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق فیدهای هواشناسی و ثبت EC/رطوبت خاک به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۵٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۵۲٬۴۶۷٬۰۳۱ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۰۵ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (به‌ازای هر هکتار): پایه ۱٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۳٬۵۳۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۶٬۴۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۶۳٬۴۸۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۳۸٬۱۲۳٬۴۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۲۱ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۳۱٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۵٬۹۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: LightGBM / Prophet با فصلیت جلالی + حل‌کننده قید OR-Tools + توضیح‌دهنده Qwen3-8B روی CPU/GPU مشترک. مجموعه داده: زمان‌بند تبخیر-تعرق و کم‌آبیاری برای استان‌های خشک.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی زمان‌بند تبخیر-تعرق و کم‌آبیاری برای استان‌های خشک؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های فیدهای هواشناسی و ثبت EC/رطوبت خاک در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: فیدهای هواشناسی و ثبت EC/رطوبت خاک. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but it depends on a water saving I could not price and on farms having sensors or at least reliable field data. The base case (900 paying farms at month 24) breaks even in month 7, peaks at a cash need of 1,594M toman (about $6,009) and reaches +18,774M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (300 farms) breaks even in month 13 and ends at +516M cumulative; the optimistic case (2,400 farms) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +64,163M [D]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled compute price breaks even in month 7, prices 30% lower in month 9 and half the farms in month 10 [D]. The plans are priced at 83.9% to 104.9% of the cost of an adviser's hour per hectare-month [D], so labour saved does not justify them alone; the value must come from lower water, pumping energy or higher yield. Iran's smart-irrigation programme gives context but no saving figure: about 10,000 hectares across 110 pilot projects, with no water-saving number stated (tvbrics.com, undated, read 28 Oct 2026 [S]). Farm counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian farms that would pay. The model runs on CPU servers, not GPUs; sensors, valves and controllers are the customer's cost and are not priced.

r: (a) Small farms and orchards of about 5 hectares. (b) Medium farms and greenhouses of about 30 hectares. (c) Large farms and agro-industrial companies of about 150 hectares [A]. Pool: no count of Iranian farms with pumps, sensors or irrigation records was found; 900 paying farms at month 24 is [A].

The tool combines the weather forecast, crop stage, soil data and any sensor readings to tell the farm how long and when to irrigate each plot, warns of frost and heat, and logs water use per hectare. The labour replaced is an irrigation adviser planning and checking one hectare for a month: 60 minutes [A], 143,023 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 150,000, 133,333 and 120,000 toman per hectare-month, 104.9%, 93.2% and 83.9% of that cost [D]. No foreign price anchor was found.
Water-user associations and irrigation-network operators, agricultural cooperatives, equipment dealers for pumps and drip systems [A], and a free 3-hectare-month trial.
Onboarding with plot mapping; seasonal check-ins; 1 support person per 150 farms [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans: Farm S with 5 hectares 750,000 toman (about $2.83), Farm M with 30 hectares 4,000,000 (about $15.08), Farm L with 150 hectares 18,000,000 (about $67.85) [A, no price was found]. Mix 60% / 30% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 3,450,000 toman a farm a month (about $13.00) [D]. Farms use their whole quota [A], so 27.0 hectare-months a farm [D]. 4% monthly churn [A].

A crop-water model and forecasting engine on CPU servers (3 servers, 51M toman a month [A, from Arvan EUR54 a month for a 4-vCPU server at 300,000 toman per euro, rounded to 17M each]); 3 engineers at 60M and 1 support person at 30M, gross [A].
Crop-coefficient and soil data per region, weather-data sourcing, sensor integration, savings measurement, selling through associations.
Weather-data providers, sensor and drip-system dealers (none confirmed), water-user associations, a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month ((60M + 60M + 60M + 30M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), compute 51M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 60M = 387.3M toman a month (about $1,460) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (about $942). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 1,000 toman a hectare-month for storage and alerts [A], and one added 3-server group for each 432 farms at 30% utilisation.

cost_model.x: One compute group serves about 432 farms including 3 free trial hectare-months each [D: 12,960 ÷ (27.0 + 3)], so the base case needs 3 groups at month 24 and the optimistic case 6 [D, from the model]; in the base case 3 groups cost 153M toman a month, about 20% of that month's total cost of 766M [D]. People and marketing dominate cost.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 114 paying farms on the fixed-cost formula [D: 387.3M ÷ (3,450,000 × 0.99 − 27.0 × 1,000) = 114.3], and stepping through farm counts with support staff gives 115 on 1 group [D]. Farms ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Farm counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is +516M toman in the conservative case, +18,774M in the base case and +64,163M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per farm at 4% churn is about 84.71M toman, about $319 [D: (3,450,000 × 0.99 − 27.0 × 1,000) ÷ 0.04].

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 900 farms at 4% monthly churn [A], which needs about 36 replacements a month and the ramp adds about 50, so about 86 gross additions a month at month 24 [D]. With 60M of marketing that is about 698,000 toman (about $2.63) per farm [D], very low for a sale that needs plot mapping; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable.

risks.x: Savings proof: the price exceeds the labour comparison, so a farm must see lower water or energy use or higher yield; I found no measured saving for an Iranian farm.
Data and sensors: soil-moisture sensors, flow meters and controllable valves are needed for good advice, and their cost, installation and supply were not verified.
Water allocation: in many areas water is allocated by quota or turn, which limits how much a farm can change its schedule.
Seasonality: demand and revenue may fall outside the growing season, which the flat 4% churn does not capture.
Farm pool: the number of farms willing to pay a monthly fee is unknown, and public programmes may supply similar tools free.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian farms and greenhouses with pumps, sensors or irrigation records, and how many pay for advisory tools.
The water or energy saving of smart irrigation on Iranian farms; the programme article gives none.
Prices of sensors, valves and controllers in Iran, and any competitor price.
CPU time per hectare-month for the chosen crop-water model.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 28 Oct 2026.

bmc.text: جایگزین «قیمت‌گذاری کمتر از هزینه پروژه در تورم ماهانه ۷ تا ۹ درصد» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: قیمت‌گذار خودکار متره و برآورد با تعدیل و کلید بازار آزاد؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

The base case (300 paying contractors at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,904M toman (about $7,178) and reaches +15,476M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (100 contractors) breaks even in month 16 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −1,978M, about $7,456); the optimistic case (900) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +65,845M [D]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price and prices 30% lower both break even in month 10, and half the contractors in month 13 [D]. Free substitutes exist for the base data: an Android app with the official base unit price lists for 1396 to 1404 and their labour, machinery, material and transport breakdown has over 20,000 installs and a 4.6 rating from 272 ratings (Cafe Bazaar, read 28 Oct 2026 [S]), so the paid value has to come from inflation indexing, automatic quantity reading and tender-specific pricing. Because the official price lists lag real market prices in a high-inflation economy, an index built from current supplier quotes would be the real product; I found no source for such quotes and the model prices one data analyst at 40M toman a month to curate them. Contractor counts are assumptions.

The user uploads a bill of quantities, a drawing schedule or a plain description; the tool matches each item to the official price list item, applies the current inflation index and local factors, adds transport and overheads, flags missing items and exports a priced estimate with a sensitivity to price changes. bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: تیم‌های خرید (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: مقایسه دستی بیش از ۲۰ پیش‌فاکتور نامرتب PDF/واتساپ. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۲۱۴ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۸۸ پایه، ۹۸ رشد، ۲۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۷٫۰٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی
bmc.text: جایگزین «مقایسه دستی بیش از ۲۰ پیش‌فاکتور نامرتب PDF/واتساپ» با کمتر از ۱۵٪ هزینه دستی/جریمه می‌شود. موتور داده: OCR و نرمال‌سازی شروط پرداخت (نقد/چک)، تحویل و مالیات میان پیشنهادها؛ با میزبانی ۱۰۰٪ داخل ایران روی دیتاسنترهای شبکه ملی اطلاعات، تا وبهوک‌های داخلی (بله/ایتا/وب محلی) در قطعی‌های اینترنت بین‌المللی فعال بمانند.

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها

bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۲۴ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

Quotes in Iran often arrive as phone photos, PDF invoices and chat messages with prices that expire within days; reading them accurately and keeping terms such as prepayment, validity and delivery comparable is the hard part, and an extraction error becomes a purchasing error.

Quote volatility: prices in high-inflation conditions expire within days, so a comparison may be stale before the purchase.
Buyer behaviour: many purchases are decided by relationships, prepayment terms and availability rather than price, which limits the value of a price-ranking tool.
Substitutes: a spreadsheet and a general assistant do part of the job for free.
Buyer pool: the number of teams that run formal RFQs is unknown.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian purchasing teams that run RFQs, and how many RFQs each runs a month.
Any domestic or foreign competitor price for quote comparison.
Extraction accuracy on Iranian quote formats.
Time a buyer spends per RFQ (2 hours is an assumption).
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 28 Oct 2026.

bmc.title: بخش‌های مشتری
bmc.text: خریدار هدف: فروشندگان خودرو و بازارگاه‌ها (کسب‌وکار کوچک و متوسط ایرانی، بازار، کلینیک و آژانس B2B). جایگزین یا کاهش‌دهنده: قیمت‌گذاری نادرست خودروهای رنگ‌شده یا با کارکرد تغییرکرده. پایه فعال حسابرسی‌شده در ماه ۱۲: ۱۴۴ حساب پرداخت‌کننده (۵۹ پایه، ۶۷ رشد، ۱۸ حرفه‌ای/سازمانی/بسته)، کالیبره‌شده با مقیاس بخش نرم‌افزار ابری ایران (لاتکا) و ریزش ماهانه ۶٫۵٪.

bmc.title: ارزش پیشنهادی

bmc.title: کانال‌ها و کمیسیون‌ها
bmc.text: ورود به بازار عمدتاً از طریق باما، دیوار، کار.آی‌آر و مراکز معاینه فنی به‌همراه ۰٫۶۰ نفر کارشناس فروش سازمانی. مدل: کمیسیون ۱۵٪ شرکا/بازارگاه بر ۶۵٪ از درآمد (۴۳٬۳۹۴٬۶۱۵ تومان در ماه در بهای تمام‌شده) برای انگیزه‌دهی به نمایندگان ERP، آژانس‌ها و فروشگاه‌های اپ.

bmc.title: روابط با مشتری
bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۰۱ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but it depends on price data I could not find and on a few large marketplace customers. The base case (360 paying dealers and marketplaces at month 24) breaks even in month 7, peaks at a cash need of 1,658M toman (about $6,250) and reaches +23,239M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (120 customers) breaks even in month 13 and ends at +1,730M cumulative; the optimistic case (900) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +71,113M [D]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 8, prices 30% lower in month 8 and half the customers in month 10 [D]. Revenue is concentrated: the Marketplace plan is 10% of customers [A] but 53% of revenue [D: 6,000,000 of 11,400,000 toman], so losing a few large accounts would change the result; it also has the lowest gross margin, 79.6% [D]. A price model needs a history of Iranian asking and sold prices, which marketplaces hold and I found no licensed source for; the pages I found gave only market-level figures (2025 new-vehicle sales of 1,192,969 units, BSCB via bestsellingcarsblog.com, 27 Jan 2026 [S]) and no used-car volume. Customer counts are assumptions. In a market where car prices move with the exchange rate, estimates go stale within days, and a fraud flag that wrongly accuses a seller is a reputational risk.

r: (a) Small car dealers and showrooms (Starter). (b) Larger dealer groups, inspection centres and insurers (Dealer). (c) Classified and car marketplaces that check every ad (Marketplace). Pool: I found no count of Iranian used-car dealers or of used-car transactions; 360 paying customers at month 24 is [A].

A query returns a price range for a car from make, model, year, mileage, region and condition, compares an ad's price and text with the range, and flags likely fraud signals such as duplicate photos, odometer or price anomalies and copied descriptions. The labour replaced is an appraiser comparing a car with recent listings and reading the ad: 15 minutes [A], 35,756 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 6,000, 4,000 and 2,000 toman a query, 16.8%, 11.2% and 5.6% of that cost [D]. No foreign or domestic price anchor was found.
Direct sales to dealer groups and marketplaces, an API for inspection and insurance firms, car-trade associations [A], and 30 free queries.
API documentation and a dashboard for small dealers; account management for marketplaces; 1 support person per 50 customers [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans: Starter with 500 queries 3,000,000 toman (about $11.31), Dealer with 3,000 queries 12,000,000 (about $45.23), Marketplace with 30,000 queries 60,000,000 (about $226.17) [A, no price was found]. Mix 60% / 30% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 11,400,000 toman a customer a month (about $42.97) [D]. Customers use 80% of their quota [A], so 3,360 queries a customer a month [D]. 4% monthly churn [A].

A price model over listing history, a fraud-signal pipeline (text and photo duplicates) and an 8B-class model on GPU nodes at 150M toman a month each [S]; 2 ML engineers at 60M, 1 data engineer at 50M and 1 support person at 30M, gross [A].
Collecting and cleaning listing and sale prices, retraining on exchange-rate shocks, fraud-signal tuning, API operations, selling.
Marketplaces or inspection centres for price data (none confirmed), insurers, a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 100 toman a query for storage [A], and one added GPU node for each 115 customers at 30% utilisation.

cost_model.x: One node serves about 115 customers including 30 free trial queries each [D: 388,800 ÷ (3,360 + 30)], so the base case needs 4 nodes at month 24 and the optimistic case 8 [D, from the model]; in the base case 4 nodes cost 600M toman a month, about 45% of that month's total cost of 1,324M [D: 4 × 150M ÷ 1,324M].

revenue.x: Break-even is about 42 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 454.0M ÷ (11,400,000 × 0.99 − 3,360 × 100) = 41.5], and stepping through customer counts with support staff and node steps gives 42 on 1 node [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is +1,730M toman in the conservative case, +23,239M in the base case and +71,113M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per customer at 4% churn is about 273.75M toman, about $1,032 [D: (11,400,000 × 0.99 − 3,360 × 100) ÷ 0.04].

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 360 customers at 4% monthly churn [A], which needs about 14 replacements a month and the ramp adds about 20, so about 34 gross additions a month at month 24 [D]. With 40M of marketing that is about 1.2M toman (about $4.4) per customer [D], very low for a business-to-business sale; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable.

risks.x: Price data: without a licensed history of Iranian asking and sold prices the model cannot be trained; marketplaces hold it and are also the biggest potential customers and competitors.
Price staleness: car prices move with the exchange rate and market sentiment, so estimates need daily retraining and still lag.
Customer concentration: about half of revenue comes from the 10% of customers on the Marketplace plan [D]; one lost account is a large hit.
False fraud flags: wrongly flagging an honest seller harms the customer's business and may carry legal risk; photo-duplicate checks need a reference index of listings.
Substitutes: marketplaces may build this in-house; free price guides exist.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian used-car dealers, inspection centres and marketplaces, and used-car transaction volume (only 2025 new-vehicle sales were found).
Whether any marketplace would license listing and sale price history, and on what terms.
Accuracy of a price model on Iranian data, and the fraud rate in car listings.
Any domestic competitor price for valuation or fraud checks.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 28 Oct 2026.

bmc.text: راه‌اندازی ترکیبی خودخدمت + تلفنی/رباتی. لینک‌های تمدید خودکار پیامکی کاوه‌نگار؛ ۱٫۰۵ نفر متخصص پشتیبانی برای موارد نیازمند دخالت انسان و پیگیری صورت‌حساب صیاد/شپارک.

bmc.title: جریان‌های درآمد (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: صورتحساب ماهانه به تومان (ماهانه): پایه ۱٬۷۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه | رشد ۲٬۸۷۰٬۰۰۰ | حرفه‌ای/سازمانی ۷٬۲۰۰٬۰۰۰ + بسته‌های مصرف (۳۸۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه میانگین). MRR ناخالص صورتحساب‌شده: ۵۶۹٬۲۸۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه؛ MRR خالص وصول‌شده پس از ۴٫۵٪ ذخیره مطالبات مشکوک/تأخیر چک: ۵۴۳٬۶۶۲٬۴۰۰ تومان/ماه.

bmc.title: منابع کلیدی
bmc.text: GPU داخلی: ۰٫۲۱ گره RTX 6000 Ada 48GB شامل ۲۵٪ بافر پیک (۳۱٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه) + سرورهای CPU/DB داخلی شبکه ملی اطلاعات (۲۵٬۹۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان/ماه). پشته فنی: LightGBM / Prophet با فصلیت جلالی + حل‌کننده قید OR-Tools + توضیح‌دهنده Qwen3-8B روی CPU/GPU مشترک. مجموعه داده: ارزش‌گذاری متری محله‌به‌محله و نویسنده آگهی فارسی پربازده.

bmc.title: فعالیت‌های کلیدی
bmc.text: حفظ دقت LoRA روی ارزش‌گذاری متری محله‌به‌محله و نویسنده آگهی فارسی پربازده؛ زنده نگه‌داشتن اتصال‌های پنل‌های دیوار، شیپور، کلید و آژانس دلتا در برابر تغییرات مسیریابی شبکه ملی اطلاعات/BGP؛ اجرای سخت‌گیرانه صورت‌حساب ماهانه و شاخص‌بندی فصلی CPI/ارز برای جلوگیری از فرسایش حاشیه ریالی توسط تورم.

bmc.title: شرکای کلیدی
bmc.text: شرکای توزیع و API: پنل‌های دیوار، شیپور، کلید و آژانس دلتا. زیرساخت: سینداد/افرانت (GPU/شبکه ملی اطلاعات)، زرین‌پال/پی‌پینگ (درگاه شپارک) و معاونت علمی و فناوری (معافیت مالیاتی دانش‌بنیان نوع ۱/۲).

bmc.title: ساختار هزینه (حسابرسی‌شده)
bmc.text: هزینه کامل مستقل: ۳۹۴٬۲۷۶٬۱۶۷ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA مستقل: ۱۷۵٬۰۰۳٬۸۳۳ تومان/ماه (۳۰٫۷٪). هزینه سبد موتور مشترک (تقسیم توسعه/دفتر بین ۳ ابزار هم‌خانواده): ۳۱۸٬۳۴۶٬۱۶۷ تومان/ماه؛ EBITDA سبد: ۲۵۰٬۹۳۳٬۸۳۳ تومان/ماه (۴۴٫۱٪).
